quote: We demonstrate an initial implementation of this system, and provide examples of student questions that highlight its benefits.
rationale: The paper is a system proposal and demonstration with illustrative examples, not an empirical study. The abstract reports no controlled comparison and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). It is also a conference companion paper, which would fall under E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order and is supported by the abstract's own description of the work.

quote: In this paper we will discuss a proposed system for sorting student coding assignments into groups with varying degrees of confidence that the work has or has not been created using GenAI.
rationale: The paper is a work in progress that proposes a system and states future work will compare outcomes. It reports no empirical comparison or quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. It is also a work-in-progress publication type, which would be E10, but the abstract's primary positive evidence is that no empirical study has been done yet, so E6 is the first applicable code given the abstract content. Students' GenAI use is observed in coursework rather than a learner-facing GenAI intervention with a control group. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.
rationale_note: Work-in-progress status also suggests E10; either way excluded.

quote: Second, we surveyed 125 users, predominantly engineering students, to analyze ChatGPTs role in academic support.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of users plus informal experiments with ChatGPT. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is a survey, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. No quantitative learning outcome is reported; the figures are usage and perception percentages. Exclusion code E3 is the first clearly applicable code in order of the protocol's checks, with E5 and E6 also likely. Positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This paper presents a lightweight framework designed to improve the syntactic correctness of Mermaid code generated by Gemini.
rationale: The record is a SoutheastCon 2026 paper, a conference venue, which the protocol makes ineligible as a conference proceeding (E10). The abstract also describes a tool-performance evaluation of Gemini's code output, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group and learning outcome. The venue alone supports E10, which is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is positively evidenced at the abstract stage.

quote: This study assesses the performance of ChatGPT4.0 on self-assessment questions pertaining to hand surgery
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT models answering hand surgery board-style self-assessment questions. Hand surgery is a clinical medical specialty, which falls under health professions education and is outside the protocol's STEM domain. The study also does not involve learners interacting with the tool, and it compares two ChatGPT versions with no non-generative-AI control group, so it would fail E1 and E3 as well. Under the protocol's ordering, E2 is the first applicable code, since the domain exclusion is clear from the abstract.

quote: This critical narrative review examines how these capabilities can contribute to school students' learning
rationale: The record is a critical narrative review of the literature, not an empirical study. It has no primary comparison group or data for a standardized mean difference. Under E6 (not an empirical study), it is excluded. Earlier checks on intervention, domain and outcome were not needed because the first applicable code is E6.

quote: This study conducted a systematic bibliometric analysis of 138 core literature published between 2021 and 2025 using VOSViewer and CiteSpace
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis of publications, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It fails the empirical design requirement, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract alone; E6 is the decisive reason).
rationale_short: Bibliometric review, not an empirical study.

quote: By uploading a common `spring constant' lab activity using Code Interpreter, we investigate the ability of ChatGPT to interpret the activity, generate realistic model data, produce a line-fit, and calculate the reduced chi square statistic.
rationale: The abstract describes an evaluation of ChatGPT Code Interpreter's outputs on a lab activity, with no described control group that does not use generative AI. The study appears to analyse ChatGPT's responses and generated data rather than compare learners with a control. Positive evidence of no comparison group is present, so exclude under E3 at the abstract stage.

quote: The utilization of the IBL Educator GPT has led to an improvement in teachers' perspectives regarding the adoption of artificial intelligence-based tools for personalizing teaching.
rationale: The participants are physics teachers (in-service, implied by the design-for-teachers framing), not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The only reported outcome is teachers' perspectives, which is a perception measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome (would also fail E5). No control group is described in the abstract. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the population criterion fails.
rationale_note: Population excluded on the basis that the intended users are physics teachers, not students.

quote: Two prompting approaches are compared: conventional zero-shot generation and CoT reasoning.
rationale: Generative AI (LLMs, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok) is used in a programming context, so intervention and domain appear met. However, the abstract compares two prompting approaches (zero-shot vs CoT), both using generative AI, with no clear non-AI control group, which points toward E3. The abstract also does not clearly describe learners interacting with the AI (the framework appears to be used for code generation) and the population is unspecified. Comparison design and learner-facing use cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded on positive evidence alone.

quote: A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 27 studies, not an empirical study with its own comparison group. Reviews are not eligible under the publication-type rule, and the review is not an empirical primary study, so it fails as not empirical (E6). Its included studies are not screened individually here.

quote: This work-in-progress experience report describes a professional development (PD) program supporting rural K–2 teachers
rationale: Work-in-progress experience report with post-PD interviews; no control group, no learner-facing generative AI, no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are in-service teachers. Not an empirical comparative study, so E6 applies as the first failing code in practice. Also the publication type is a work in progress (E10 could apply), but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the non-experimental report design.

quote: The article's core comprises two practical case studies-one in computer science, where ChatGPT aids in teaching programming
rationale: The abstract describes case studies and reflections on ChatGPT in computer science and English composition. Case studies are non-empirical/qualitative designs with no described control group or quantitative comparison, so the study fails the design criterion and is not an empirical comparative study (E6). The abstract's claims of "notable improvements" are not backed by a described comparison group or effect statistics. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the design is a case study/reflection.

Title describes a practical guide to developing ChatGPT-based interactive learning applications in biochemistry education. No abstract is available. The title suggests a guide or methods chapter rather than an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome, which points toward E6 (not an empirical study), but the record does not confirm this. Biochemistry may also be borderline for STEM domain. Because the abstract gives no positive evidence of failure, the record is retained as unsure for full-text review.

This study compares AI scoring systems (machine learning and LLM-based) against expert human scores for student explanations in physics. Learners do not appear to interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the AI is used to score text, which is closer to grading (an exclusion category under the protocol's intervention row, and potentially E1 as not learner-facing). Population (secondary-school students) and domain (physics) fit. There is no clear control group without generative AI, and the outcome is AI scoring accuracy rather than a learning outcome. The abstract does not positively establish these, but the likely failure on intervention (not learner-facing) and comparison/outcome suggests exclusion at full text. Left as unsure so the full text can be checked for the E1 issue, since the abstract gives no evidence that learners use generative AI.

quote: The present case study focuses on the way that Llama-based AI tutors impacted more than 370 students
rationale: The abstract describes a case study, which the protocol excludes as a non-eligible design (no evident randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group). Working paper publication type also falls outside journal articles (E10 possible), but the case-study design is the clearest positive evidence of failure, so E6 is applied. Comparison group is not described in the abstract. Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, so exclusion is justified.

The abstract describes a qualitative metaphor analysis (Grounded Theory) of 27 students' free associations about AI agents. It has no experimental or comparison group, no learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study in the sense of the protocol's eligible designs; E6 is the first applicable code given the design. Note that E1 (learner-facing intervention) and the comparison requirement also fail, but E6 is applied as the most fundamental issue. Decision is clear from the abstract.

decision_note: Excluded on publication type; see rationale.
quote: Simpósio Brasileiro de Fatores Humanos em Sistemas Computacionais
rationale: The venue is a Brazilian symposium on human factors in computing systems (IHC-style conference), indicating a conference proceedings paper, which is not an eligible publication type. The abstract also describes only an experience with initial impressions gathered from feedback and no comparison group, so it appears to lack a control condition (E3) and a quantitative learning outcome (E5); these are secondary to the publication-type exclusion. Domain (User Experience course) is also questionable as STEM.

The record has only a title and venue (WOP/HAIBRIDGE@ISWC 2025, a workshop venue) with no abstract. The title suggests an AI assistant for teaching knowledge engineering, but it does not show whether the tool is generative, whether a control group exists, the design, or any learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept as unsure for full-text review. The venue appears to be a workshop, which may also trigger E10 at full text if it is a non-journal publication.

quote: Prefix-Normalized Policy Optimization (PNPO), which replaces the cumulative ratio with the geometric mean of likelihood ratios along each causal prefix
rationale: The study is an RL training algorithm for LLMs (policy optimization on rollouts) evaluated on mathematical reasoning benchmarks. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLM is the object being trained. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). No student population or learning intervention is described. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a special issue, not the empirical study titled in the record header. The text describes no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and no sample. The record's own content is an editorial notice, so it is not an empirical study (E6). The title mentions AI-enhanced assistive interventions for adolescent cyberbullying, which is not a STEM learning outcome, but the retraction notice itself gives no evidence on the STEM criterion, so E6 is the primary reason. Retracted status is noted; it is not a duplicate. No injection detected.

quote: We present StudentSim, a training framework that turns sparse per-student data into individualized simulators through pooled training followed by per-student specialization.
rationale: The paper develops LLM-based student simulators evaluated on behavioral fidelity and guidance responsiveness against simulated learner responses, not on a learning outcome in a controlled comparison of learners. No control group of learners with vs. without generative AI is described, and the outcomes (F and R) are simulator-matching metrics rather than quantitative learning measures. It is not an empirical intervention study with learners, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense) is the closest code; the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is not a learner comparison study. Note that the first failing criterion in code order could arguably be E1 or E3; I selected E6 because the study's core contribution is a simulation framework rather than a learner-facing intervention evaluation. Flagging for audit.

quote: We find that GenAI attainment is at the level of a first-class degree, though current performance can vary between modules.
rationale: The study evaluates GenAI performance on exam questions by generating and blind-marking GenAI submissions. Learners do not interact with GenAI as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group of learners without GenAI; the only comparison is against invigilated student exam results, which is a descriptive benchmark rather than an experimental control group. The design is a case study of GenAI output, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Positive evidence of failure on the comparison and intervention criteria is present, so exclusion is supported. The first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the abstract does not clearly establish that, so E3 is given as the most direct failure of the comparison criterion. Consider reviewing at full text if the E1/E3 choice is contested.

The record has only a title and year (2026) with no abstract, venue, or design information. The title suggests a data science challenge report, but nothing in the record shows whether learners used a generative AI tool, whether there is a control group, or whether any quantitative learning outcome was reported. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: we propose a computational method of assessing corpus prevalence of MCQ options in large text corpora leveraging textual embeddings
rationale: The study is a computational analysis of corpus frequency of MCQ options (Wikipedia retrieval with embeddings). No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; LLMs are used to generate distractors and the work is not a learner-facing intervention. No control group or learning outcome is present. Excluded on E1 (not learner-facing generative AI), the first applicable code.

The record contains only a title and author affiliation block, with no abstract text. It describes ChatGPT's performance on USMLE, an evaluation of an LLM on exam questions rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group. There is no comparison group, no learner population, and no learning outcome from a learner-facing study. The design appears to be a commentary or evaluation piece rather than an empirical learner study, so E6 is applied (not an empirical study). Note that the protocol's first-applicable code order would place intervention/comparison issues earlier, but the record gives no positive evidence of a learner-facing intervention, so E6 is the best-supported code. Confidence is moderate given the sparse record.

quote: Journal of Education and Training Studies (JETS) would like to acknowledge the following reviewers for their assistance with peer review of manuscripts for this issue.
rationale: The record is a reviewer acknowledgements page, not a research study. It describes no intervention, comparison group, or learning outcome, and so is not an empirical study. It also is not a journal article reporting research. Coded E6 (not an empirical study); publication-type E10 would also be arguable, but E6 is the closest fit for a non-empirical editorial item. No generative AI content is present.

The record has only a title and venue (AERA 2026), with no abstract. Title suggests a programming context with generative AI support and a performance outcome, but the comparison group, design, population level, and publication type (AERA is typically a conference venue, which would be E10) cannot be determined. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review, where publication type and design should be checked.

quote: This study underscores the detrimental effects of over dependence on these tools, particularly regarding students' critical thinking skills, creativity, and academic integrity.
rationale: The study concerns EFL students' academic writing, which is language learning and not STEM content (E2). It is also a questionnaire and interview mixed-methods study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so other criteria likely fail as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced by the abstract.

quote: Using a design-based research approach, Beacon was developed iteratively and evaluated via mixed methods, combining questionnaires and semi-structured interviews with students and staff
rationale: The abstract describes a design-based research study evaluating a RAG tool through questionnaires and interviews only. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the evaluation is perception-based. Exclusion E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) is the first code that applies. Design is also qualitative/survey-based, and outcomes are perceptions only, but E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order.

quote: A questionnaire was developed and administered to probe the participants’ perceptions and practices.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of 301 EFL teachers about perceptions and reported practices with ChatGPT. It is not an empirical experimental study with learner outcomes: no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content (EFL/L2 writing), participants are in-service teachers (not students), and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the study is best characterized as a survey, and the design is non-experimental; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense of an eligible design) is applied as the primary reason. Note: the code ordering would place E1 first given teacher-only use; to follow the protocol order strictly, the exclusion is E1.

quote: my study will begin to bridge this gap by exploring how a purposeful sample of LCCS post-primary students in Ireland engage with GAI tools
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory study of how students engage with ChatGPT-type tools, with no control group or comparison condition mentioned. Positive evidence of no comparison group is present, so the record is excluded under E3 at the abstract stage. The study appears to be a qualitative exploration with no quantitative learning outcome described, which would also be relevant to the design and outcome criteria.

quote: Title: DidInfo 2025 : new perspective in informatics education - international proceedings on teaching informatics
rationale: The record is conference proceedings (title: "international proceedings"), which is an ineligible publication type under E10. The abstract also describes a conference overview and teaching agenda rather than an empirical study with a control group and a quantitative learning outcome, so it fails design and outcome criteria as well. E10 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is positively evidenced by the record.

quote: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and on-policy distillation (OPD) have emerged as two dominant methods for post-training reasoning LLMs.
rationale: The study concerns post-training of reasoning LLMs via RL and on-policy distillation. Training LLMs with teacher-student distillation and RL is not learner-facing generative AI used as part of a learning activity by students; it is a model training method. Excluded under E1 at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing. No student population or STEM learning context is described.

quote: Drawing on the platform Midjourney, students explored concepts, material moodboards, and spatial compositions, simulating professional scenarios.
rationale: Content is interior design/architecture education, which is not in the STEM domain list (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Exclude under E2. The study is also a practice-based workshop with no described control group or quantitative learning outcome, which would be further grounds for exclusion (E3/E5), but E2 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence of non-STEM domain.

quote: We compared how agents made with different AI platforms (ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Claude.ai) performed across three criteria: creator usability, accuracy of responses, and effectiveness of responsible AI guardrails.
rationale: The abstract describes comparing generative AI platforms against each other, with no non-AI control group. Outcomes are creator usability, response accuracy, and guardrail effectiveness, judged by student evaluators, not a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of E3 is present at the abstract stage, so this is excluded on the first failing code in order (E1 does not apply since students interact with the agents; E2 does not apply as the domain is physics and signal processing).

quote: This paper presents a comprehensive literature review on the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) in the teaching and learning processes within Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) engineering education.
rationale: The record is a literature review with illustrative scenarios, not an empirical study with a control group and outcome data. It fails the Design criterion and is not an empirical study (E6). The abstract describes synthesized cases from other studies, not a new experiment with a comparison group.

quote: we employed three different classification methods driven by different artificial intelligence technologies
rationale: The study uses GPT and other classifiers to automatically code discourse for researchers. The AI is applied by researchers to annotate data, not used by learners as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). No learner-facing generative AI and no control group of learners is described. Exclusion code E1 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.
rationale_short: GPT used by researchers for automatic coding of discourse, not learner-facing.

quote: Survey results were obtained from 203 university students and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM).
rationale: The study is a survey-based PLS-SEM analysis of student attitudes toward creating screencasts as assessments. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; attitudes/acceptance are perceptions only. Also, the intervention is student-created screencasts, not a learner interaction with a generative AI tool; GenAI is discussed only as context. Design is survey (not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design). Primary exclusion is E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design and outcome failures are also clear. At the abstract stage the exclusion rests on the absence of any comparison group and the survey-only design.

quote: The proposed research applies reverse engineering techniques in the field of computer graphics (CG) production education at Japanese vocational schools.
rationale: The record is a SIGGRAPH Educator's Forum entry, which is a conference venue and therefore not an eligible journal article (E10). The abstract also gives no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no empirical design; it only proposes a methodology and suggests ChatGPT use. Exclusion on E10 is the first applicable code given the publication type.

quote: Approaches used in Canadian academic institutions to keep nursing students safe during clinical placements: a systematic review protocol of policy and expert opinion.
rationale: The record is a systematic review protocol about policy and expert opinion on nursing student safety during clinical placements. It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, and falls in health professions education, which is excluded. Under E1-first ordering, the intervention criterion fails first (no learner-facing generative AI), but the abstract gives no evidence of AI; E6 is the clearest positive failure shown by the title, which describes a review protocol. Note the ordering issue: E1 would be the first applicable code in strict order, but the record gives no positive evidence of any generative AI intervention, so the exclusion rests on the non-empirical nature shown in the title.

quote: This proof-of-concept study explored the feasibility of implementing Digital Gender Hubs
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-methods feasibility study using surveys, focus groups and key informant interviews, with no control group, no intervention comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome (KAP and prevalence measures only). Not a GBV-to-STEM learning study; generative AI (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, TurboScribe) appears only as a tool used by researchers, not learners. Excluded on E6 as a descriptive, non-experimental feasibility study; E1 would also plausibly apply since AI is not learner-facing, but E6 reflects the design failure most directly.

The record has a title only and no abstract. The title suggests robotics programming education (STEM content) with LLM-assisted learning, which may fit the intervention and domain. However, the comparison group, study design, population level, and whether a quantitative learning outcome is measured cannot be determined from the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded. Date (2026) and journal article type (IEEE Transactions on Education) appear to meet criteria.

quote: The generated output is qualitatively analyzed to help evaluate the feedback's quality, content, structure, and other features.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative analysis of LLM-generated feedback on student programming solutions. It reports no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison and outcome supports exclusion. E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in code order, since no control group without generative AI is described. Outcome absence (E5) also applies, but E3 comes first in the code order. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is qualitative only.

quote: The same validated questionnaire was administered to undergraduate and graduate engineering students, combining the Big Five personality inventory, perceived team-role selection, and five multi-item scales
rationale: The study is a longitudinal survey of perceptions across two academic years with no control group that avoids generative AI. Design is survey/longitudinal pre-post without a comparison group, and outcomes are perceptions (attitude, trust, usefulness), not learning measures. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in order, though E5 (perceptions only) would also apply.

quote: This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) on artificial intelligence in education (AIEd) in elementary school nationalism education based on Scopus literature 2020-2024.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome, and its domain is civic/nationalism education rather than STEM. Under the protocol's ordering, E6 is the first code that applies. Note: the criteria values above are shown as an informal summary; the domain criterion is clearly not met.

Single-group pre-post design: residents complete a questionnaire before and after a teaching session with no separate control group. The LLMs were run as comparators on the same questionnaire, but they are not a learner control group that avoids generative AI, and the protocol excludes single-group pre-post designs. Exclusion code E3 applies. Domain (anticoagulation in medicine) is also not clearly STEM. The record is an abstract-only QI report of residents, and the protocol's intervention criterion is not met because residents were not interacting with a generative AI tool. Excluding on E3 at abstract stage on the basis of the explicit pre-post design.

quote: Survey data from 39 undergraduate students in algebra-based physics indicate that nearly all participants reported improved conceptual understanding
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group survey study of 39 students with no control group, and the evidence is self-reported perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in order. E5 would also apply, but E3 takes precedence.

quote: the architecture significantly reduced instructor workload
rationale: The AI is used by instructors to produce teaching materials (LaTeX/Beamer slides, Python figures), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies. The outcomes are instructor workload and ratings of materials, with no controlled comparison group or quantitative learning outcome described. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is teacher-only.

quote: This preliminary study explores learners’ perceptions of the AI-TA, focusing on perceived benefits, limitations, and recommendations for future design.
rationale: The study is a qualitative perception study using interviews and participatory design sessions with nine students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no comparison design. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design); the design also fails the comparison and outcome criteria. Earliest applicable code in order would be E6 given the qualitative design; the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative, perception-only design.
decision_note: Qualitative interview/participatory design study; no control group or learning outcome.

quote: The use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation has advanced rapidly
rationale: The study is an RL framework in which a small trainable Student agent is trained with AI feedback; the LLM Worker, Tutor, and Test Generator are all AI components evaluated on benchmarks (LiveCodeBench, HumanEvalPlus). No learners or students in K-12 or higher education are involved, so the population criterion fails. Although the abstract mentions a "Student" agent, it is a trainable model, not a human learner. Exclusion code E4 is applied as the first failing criterion in the protocol order that is clearly evidenced; the record is also a benchmark/ML method paper rather than a learning study. Coding is by the Student-model rule of the protocol (E1 could be argued too, since no learner interacts with the tool), but the clearest failure is population.

quote: We then fine-tune GPT-4o to detect LLM-generated responses and assess the impact on learning from LLM misuse.
rationale: At the abstract stage, the study's core contribution is a fine-tuned GPT-4o detector of LLM-generated text, not a learner-facing generative AI learning intervention. Learners are not described as interacting with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLM is used to classify responses. The study therefore appears not to meet the intervention criterion (E1). Comparison, design, and domain are not clear from the abstract, but E1 is the first applicable code. Excluding on E1 is a judgment that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI; the learner-misuse analysis is observational (suspected misuse vs. not), not a generative AI treatment vs. control contrast.

quote: Following PRISMA 2020, a structured Scopus TITLE-ABS-KEY search identified 871 records; 50 peer-reviewed journal studies published between 2024 and 2026 met the eligibility criteria.
rationale: This is a systematic review, not an empirical study (E6), and it is about English-language learning and academic writing, which is non-STEM content (E2). E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order and the content failure is clear from the abstract. The review also reports no pooled effect size and no primary experimental comparison. Excluding at the abstract stage on the content criterion is justified by the positive evidence of non-STEM focus.

criteria.rationale_note: LLMs evaluated directly on problems; no learner group or control group.

quote: We evaluate four LLMs—GPT-4o, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Llama 3.2, and DeepSeek R1—on 80 LeetCode Top Interview 150 problems
rationale: The study benchmarks four LLMs directly on LeetCode problems. There is no learner group interacting with the LLMs and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Only LLM-vs-LLM comparisons are made, which the protocol excludes under E3. Exclusion uses E3 as the first applicable code.
decision_note: Abstract stage exclusion based on positive evidence of no control group without generative AI.

quote: this study compares over 128 prompt combinations for a Portuguese dataset based on GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4-Turbo
rationale: The study compares prompt combinations for GPT models used to grade short answers (ASAG). Learners do not interact with the generative AI tool; it is used for automatic grading, which is not learner-facing. Also, the abstract shows only comparisons between two GPT variants and prompt configurations, with no non-generative AI control group (E3 would also apply). Under the code order, E1 is the first applicable code. Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: We evaluate AlgoRAG on 179 curated exam-style questions spanning asymptotic analysis, recurrence relations, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, NP-completeness, sorting, and divide-and-conquer.
rationale: The abstract describes a system evaluated on 179 exam-style questions with automated metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, pedagogical score) and a 100% success rate. There is no mention of a control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears unmet. This is positive evidence of no comparison group, so exclude under E3. The intervention (LLM-based RAG) and STEM domain (TCS) are met; population is not stated.

quote: In this paper, an overview is presented of publications in the EE track spanning the past twelve years (2012–2023). An analysis was conducted to address quantitative and qualitative aspects of over 500 papers.
rationale: This is a bibliometric review of conference papers, not an empirical study of learners. An LLM was used by the authors to extract key points from abstracts, not as a learner-facing intervention, and there is no control group or learning outcome. E1 would also apply, but E6 is the primary reason, and under the code order E1 comes first. Strictly, the first applicable code in order is E1 because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 is the code that should be reported. Excluding at abstract stage is supported by clear positive evidence that the study is a bibliometric review.

quote: This systematic literature review examines research on artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics education
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, which is a review publication rather than an empirical study, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Review articles are also not eligible publication types. Abstract-stage decision.

quote: This study aims to analyze the implementation of AI in mathematics learning using the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method following the PRISMA stages.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 35 articles, not an empirical study with its own control-group comparison. It fails the protocol's Design and Empirical-study requirements (review articles are excluded), so it is coded E6 (not an empirical study). quote: The pandemic has greatly increased the importance and effect of research into developing novel antiviral treatments, cures, and vaccines.
rationale: The abstract is a narrative overview of AI and computer-aided drug design for COVID-19 with no described experiment, learners, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study and the domain is drug discovery/pharmacology rather than STEM education. Positive evidence that the study is not an empirical learning study exists, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under E6 (first applicable code in order would be E1 since no learner-facing intervention is described; however the record is clearly a non-empirical overview, so E6 is the most accurate code).

quote: The study aimed to assess the perceptions and knowledge of university students in India regarding the application of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in higher education.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of students' perceptions and knowledge of GenAI. There is no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and self-reported use. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Under the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of failure on outcome and design, so exclusion is appropriate. The first-applicable code in order would be E1 only if the intervention were judged not learner-facing GenAI, which the abstract does not clearly establish; E5 is the cleanest reason. Population (university students) and date (2025) are met.

quote: this meta-analysis used quantitatively eligible interventional studies... among health science learners
rationale: The abstract is a meta-analysis of health science education studies. Protocol excludes health professions education (domain not met), and the population is health science learners, which is not clearly K-12 or higher education STEM. Health professions education is an explicit exclusion, so this is excluded as E4 (population) per the rule that the record concerns health science learners rather than STEM students. Note: the domain exclusion for health professions education would also apply; the code assigned follows the listed order with population as the primary failure. Also, a meta-analysis is not itself an eligible primary empirical study (E6 could apply), but the protocol-level reason is the health-science focus.

quote: A qualitative systematic literature review reported in line with PRISMA principles was combined with bibliometric mapping.
rationale: This is a systematic review synthesizing 25 articles plus bibliometric mapping, not an empirical primary study with a control group. Reviews are not eligible; the exclusion code is E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is a journal article, but the design is a review, so E6 applies rather than E10.

quote: A complete from-scratch system realizes the whole account; its factory surface is operated end-to-end by a production LLM.
rationale: The paper is a machine-learning architecture paper about a self-growing neural model for continual learning, evaluated on continual-learning benchmarks. The only LLM mention is that a production LLM operates the model's factory surface, which is a development tool, not a learner-facing generative AI intervention. No learners, STEM content, or control group is described. Excluded at E1 because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: This exploratory study examines how 43 students in cybercrime courses engaged in Generative AI through surveys and structured activities.
rationale: Abstract describes an exploratory survey and reflection study of 43 students with no control or comparison group, and reports descriptive statistics and thematic interpretation rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3. Cybercrime is also not clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order for this record.

quote: We present MimicAgent, a prompt-to-trajectory generation framework for learning dynamic quadruped skills.
rationale: The study concerns LLM-driven generation of reference trajectories for training quadruped robot control policies via RL. Content is robotics/motion control rather than a STEM learning domain in the protocol's sense, and there are no learners or students; no learner-facing generative AI, comparison group, or learning outcome is described. Per the code order, E1 (learner-facing intervention) could also be argued, but the first clearly failing criterion is the domain/population; E2 is applied as the primary reason. Abstract-only evidence is sufficient to exclude.

quote: "investigates GenAI tools, help-seeking preferences and the importance of peer support among first-year software engineering students (n=94)"
rationale: Abstract describes a survey-style investigation of help-seeking preferences and GenAI use among first-year software engineering students, with no experimental manipulation or control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is a survey (not an eligible design) and there is no comparison group without generative AI. Reported percentages are self-reported usage/perceptions. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 and E6 also plausibly apply. Note: the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, so this is a clear exclusion.

quote: This systematic review, in the context of the Concerns-Based Adoption Model (CBAM) as the theoretical framework, reviewed science teachers' concerns about the implementation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools in science education.
rationale: The record is a systematic review, which is not an empirical study and is excluded under E6 (reviews are also ineligible publication types). It does not report a primary comparison-group experiment and its focus is on in-service teachers' concerns, not learner outcomes. Exclusion at the abstract stage is justified by the explicit review design.

quote: This paper presents DataCanvas-EDU, an agentic framework for instructor-guided synthetic data generation in business analytics education.
rationale: The abstract describes a software framework and an illustrative case (WindowDash) for instructor-led synthetic data generation. It reports no empirical study, no learner outcome, and no control group. It is a framework/tool description, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Business analytics is also not clearly within the STEM domain list, but E6 is the decisive positive evidence. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the study is not empirical.

quote: This study conducts a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis based on 75 high-quality papers
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis, not an empirical study with its own intervention and control group. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Review articles are also outside the eligible design. The abstract's mention of empirical studies refers to the reviewed papers, not to this record's own data.

criteria.domain_note: computational thinking program mentioned; STEM status unclear

quote: we design a randomized controlled trial that integrates a chatbot for explanation and feedback, explicitly structured for teacher mediation
rationale: Abstract describes a framework paper with platform-data observations and a designed (not yet reported) RCT of a generative chatbot for explanation and feedback. Intervention appears to be a generative AI chatbot learners use, so E1 is not clearly triggered. Abstract does not report a quantitative learning outcome, a control group result, or clear STEM content (computational thinking is mentioned). Missing information is not evidence of exclusion, and the paper may report a qualifying RCT in full text, so it advances to full-text review. Publication type and language are not stated in the record.

quote: The models were evaluated using four normalized metrics: instruction-following accuracy, conversational clarity, response latency, and on-device feasibility.
rationale: The study benchmarks ten lightweight LLMs against each other on model-level metrics (instruction-following accuracy, clarity, latency, feasibility). There is no control group of learners without generative AI and no learner-level quantitative learning outcome; it compares only generative AI variants. Per the protocol, comparing only generative AI variants is E3. Outcomes are model performance metrics rather than student learning, which would also fail E5, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Regression analysis found a significant positive association between socioeconomic status (SES) and belief that LLM use will lead to career success.
rationale: The study is a correlational survey (N=144) with qualitative interviews examining associations between SES and beliefs/attitudes about LLMs. There is no experimental or comparison group without generative AI, and the outcomes are perceptions and beliefs rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded at the first applicable code: E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but the protocol asks for the first code in order, and E3 precedes E5 only if the comparison were absent; here the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence from the abstract.
exclusion_code_note: E3 would also apply (no control group); reported E5 per the outcome evidence.

quote: We aim to establish a novel ITS for Python programming that is highly adaptable, serves both as a teaching and research platform
rationale: The abstract describes a system description and future development directions for an ITS for Python. It reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. Generative AI use is only proposed as a possible hint mechanism. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), with the caveat that the record is a system description.

quote: The review follows the PRISMA protocol and includes a total of 33 studies selected based on explicit inclusion criteria, focusing on experiences involving generative tools.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 33 studies, not an empirical study with its own control group and effect-size data. It fails the empirical design requirement (E6). Review articles are also ineligible publication types, but the first applicable code in order is E6 (no empirical study) given the review is a secondary synthesis, not a primary study. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a review design.

quote: To demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, we apply the pipeline to a VR task focused on robot acceleration
rationale: Abstract describes a framework/pipeline and a feasibility demonstration on a VR robotics task. It does not report a comparison group, an experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome. It uses LLM for speech analysis, so generative AI is plausible, but the abstract gives no positive evidence that a criterion fails. Per the abstract-stage rule, return unsure for full-text review of design, comparison, and outcome. Robotics/inertia content may also need a STEM check at full text.

quote: MEDS comprises 28,000 runs from 14 LLMs (i.e., Mistral, Qwen, DeepSeek, IBM Granite, Microsoft Phi, and xAI Grok) generated under human-shadow and AI-assistant conditions.
rationale: The study is a dataset of runs of LLMs themselves (simulated personifications), not learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. No human learners or control group are described. Under the protocol's ordering, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), so the exclusion code should be E1 rather than E4. Correcting: the first code that applies in order is E1. The record is excluded. Note the earlier E4 is superseded by E1 under the stated order.

Venue is an International Convention (conference proceedings), which is an ineligible publication type under the protocol (E10). The abstract also describes two case studies and a pilot without a clear control group or quantitative effect measure, so further criteria are unclear. Excluding on publication type as the first applicable code.

criteria.outcome_note: survey of self-efficacy and perceived gains

quote: Survey data were collected from undergraduate electrical and computer engineering students to examine self-efficacy, perceived learning gains, and trust in AIgenerated feedback.
rationale: Survey-based study of undergraduate ECE students using GenAI. No control group without generative AI is described, and the design is a survey. Outcomes are perceptions (self-efficacy, perceived learning gains, trust), not a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol, this fails the comparison and design criteria; E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group), and the study also lacks a quantitative learning outcome (E5) and is not an experimental design. Reported as E3 per the first-applicable-code rule.

quote: Merryman returned to Notre Dame to study law, which he accomplished while teaching chemistry and math full time to pay for his education.
rationale: The record is a magazine-style biographical piece about law professor Merryman (GLQ, a law journal). It is not an empirical study, involves no generative AI intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order; E1 would also apply on the intervention, but the record is not an empirical study at all. Note that E1 comes first in the code order; on strict application, the first applicable code is E1 because no learner-facing generative AI is described. Decision recorded as E6 given the nature of the record.

quote: we surveyed 330 secondary school students in China (Grades 7--11) about their preferred tutoring behaviors, attitudes toward proactive intervention, and acceptable use of learning-process data
rationale: The study is a survey of student preferences about AI tutor behaviors, not an empirical experiment with a control group or a learning outcome. Design is survey (not an eligible design) and no quantitative learning outcome is measured; it is excluded at E6 as a non-experimental (survey) study, the first code that applies after the intervention-related checks. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with perception outcomes only.

quote: This Editorial introduces the International Journal of Designs for Learning (IJDL) Special Section on Generative Artificial Intelligence in Learning Design
rationale: The record is an editorial introducing a special section of design cases. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Under the abstract rule, the exclusion rests on the positive evidence that the record is an editorial.

The abstract describes an observational questionnaire study of student perceptions about craft careers, with subgroup comparisons only. It involves no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, no learning outcome, and no experimental design. Generative AI appears only as an LLM-assisted survey analysis workflow by researchers, and VR/AI recommendation systems are mentioned only as design implications. Exclusion at the first applicable code: E1 would also fit, since AI is used only by researchers, but the study is clearly non-empirical in the trial sense and is observational, so E6 is the most direct code. Note the protocol's E1 applies first in order; given the first applicable code in order is E1 (AI used only by researchers, not learner-facing), the code should be E1.

quote: a structured risk-assessment survey adapted from ISO 31000:2018 distributed to senior architectural students
rationale: Abstract describes a literature review, semi-structured interviews with instructors, and a risk-assessment survey of students rated on probability and impact scales. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is survey/perception-based and not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria; primarily perception-based). Architecture is also not clearly within the STEM domain. The first applicable code in protocol order would be E1/E2 only if clearly established, so E6 is used as the best fit for a non-experimental, perception-based study.

quote: This discussion argues that statistics curricula should treat LLMs not only as tools, but as objects of inquiry
rationale: The record is a discussion/position piece that proposes curricular examples. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the work is non-empirical.

quote: Our team monitors output along four priority dimensions--student safety, tone and instructional role, pedagogical value, and structural output quality--and tracks how often it fails on each.
rationale: The study concerns LLM-as-judge evaluation of a teacher-facing product's outputs for production monitoring. Learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no learner control group or learning outcome; it is an engineering/monitoring report. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Human evaluation is conducted through focus group analysis, and student progress and faculty feedback are tracked.
rationale: Abstract describes LLM-based generative agents that generate questions and evaluate student answers, so the intervention appears learner-facing generative AI. However, the abstract gives no indication of a control group, a comparison design, or a quantitative learning outcome (evaluation is via focus groups and tracked progress), and the STEM content is not specified. No positive evidence of an exclusion criterion is present, so the record is advanced to full text for checking comparison, design, outcome, and domain.

quote: This study introduces a novel parental training program that leverages generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools to empower parents as self-directed designers of AI-supported learning tasks.
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI parental training program, but the participants are parents (not students) and the children's learning outcomes are not a STEM-specific domain. The protocol requires learners to be K-12 or higher-education students; parents of SEN children are not eligible learners. Exclusion code E4 would apply on population grounds; the abstract gives no indication of STEM content. Note the first-applicable code order places E2 before E4, so the abstract gives no positive evidence of STEM content, but the record is clearly ineligible on population. Also, the design is a pilot with mixed methods and no clear control group described, so comparison is unclear.

quote: Twenty-nine interventional studies involving 2138 participants met the eligibility criteria.
rationale: Systematic review of health science education, not an empirical primary study, and the domain is health professions education, which the protocol excludes. The first applicable code in order is E2 (non-STEM content: health professions education). E6 (not an empirical study) would also apply, but E2 comes first in the protocol's order. Design, population and domain are clearly not met; the review itself is not a primary study.

Title describes a dental hygiene education study on AI-assisted essay grading. Dental hygiene is a health professions field, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain, and the AI is used for grading rather than as a learner-facing tool. Design is described as retrospective observational, which is not a randomized or comparison-group quasi-experiment. No abstract is available. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order, with the domain failure as the clearest positive evidence. Note that E1 (AI used for grading, not learner-facing) would also plausibly apply.

quote: AI-generated criteria were created for reading-literacy milestones across four domains and evaluated by a panel of five experts
rationale: The AI chatbot is used to generate assessment criteria for teacher/assessment use, not as a learner-facing learning activity. Content is reading literacy, not STEM. No control group, no learner quantitative outcome; the study is an expert rating design. Exclusion under E1 as the first applicable code (AI is not learner-facing). Abstract stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: Systematic review and meta-analysis of ML in education (2020-2026), examining effectiveness, teacher transformation, equity, and policy implications.
rationale: The record is a systematic review and meta-analysis of machine learning in education, not an empirical primary study. It is therefore not an eligible design under the protocol's empirical-study requirement (E6). Its focus is machine learning broadly rather than learner-facing generative AI, which would be a separate concern (E1), but the review-level nature of the record is the first applicable code in the order given. The embedded "RCT n=1,200" claim is a reported result within the review and does not make the record itself an eligible primary study. Note that the protocol does not list reviews as an exclusion under E6 explicitly, but the publication type rule excludes reviews (E10) and the record is a review; given the code order, E6 is the first applicable reading of "not an empirical study".

quote: We analyze how Claude Opus 4, GPT-4.1, and Gemini 2.5 Pro adapt 60 English math word problems into Bengali, Hindi, Punjabi (India), Urdu, Sindhi (Pakistan), Italian, and Sicilian (Italy)
rationale: The study audits LLM outputs (adapted word problems) rather than learners interacting with generative AI, and reports no learner outcome or control group. Abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome: it analyzes entity transformations in model-generated text. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable under the protocol's ordering that fits; the intervention is not learner-facing (E1) though, so strictly E1 would apply first. Given the protocol order, the first code that applies is E1 because the LLM is used to adapt problems without learners interacting with it. Recording E5 is therefore an error; see correction in decision below.

quote: Standardized patients (SPs) are vital for clinical training but resource-intensive. We developed a systematic approach for generating SP cases using GPT-4o
rationale: The study concerns clinical history-taking training with LLM-generated standardized patients, which is health professions education and therefore non-STEM under the protocol's domain exclusion. The abstract also reports only expert ratings and student perceptions (appropriateness, accuracy ratings), with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. Exclusion uses the first applicable code, E2, since the domain check comes before the outcome and comparison checks.

quote: This review systematically examines the role of curiosity in science learning
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 40 studies, not an empirical study. Under the protocol, reviews are excluded as publication type (E10) and not empirical (E6). E6 is applied as the first code that clearly fails; the review nature is positive evidence of non-empirical design. The review's mention of large language models is secondary and does not alter the decision.

quote: AI assistance shifts where and how often programmers focus on specific code elements, as well as the depth of their engagement across semantic categories such as arguments, loops, and method calls.
rationale: Eye-tracking study of novice programmers using generative AI during code summarization (STEM, programming; learner-facing). The abstract does not state whether there is a no-AI control group or a randomized/quasi-experimental comparison, though 'AI assistance' vs. presumably non-AI suggests a comparison. Outcomes include summary length and perceived/automated quality measures, which may count as quantitative learning outcomes but are ambiguous. Venue is SEET@ICSE, a workshop/conference-style venue, which may be an E10 publication-type issue; this must be checked at full text. Not enough evidence to exclude at abstract stage.

The abstract describes a comparison of explanation-assessment approaches (semantic similarity versus LLM prompting) on a previously published dataset of student explanations. It does not describe a learner-facing intervention with a control group, a learning outcome, or an experimental design. This appears to be a computational evaluation of assessment methods rather than an empirical learning study, so E6 applies. Venue is a conference-style outlet (Florida AI Research Society), which may also raise E10, but the first applicable code in order is E6 on the abstract evidence. Note the record is excluded on positive evidence of a non-experimental design, not on missing information.

quote: This book provides a structured and comprehensive introduction to data science as an interdisciplinary field
rationale: The record is a textbook (book), not a journal article, so publication type is not eligible (E10). It also describes no empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention is described; generative AI is only mentioned as an emerging theme), but the publication type is a clear positive failure and E10 is the most direct code for a book. Coding E1 would be defensible as well; the record is excluded either way.
rationale_note: Per the protocol, report the first code that applies in order E1 to E10. Strictly, E1 comes before E10. See note below.

quote: The paper is a conceptual and policy analysis; it advances interpretive arguments and a proposed evidential framework, not empirical findings.
rationale: The record is a conceptual and policy analysis with no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Earlier codes (E1 to E5) were considered first, but the abstract does not give a clear basis for them, and E6 is the first code with positive evidence. The cited studies are other people's detection research, not data from this paper.

quote: a proof of concept of how personal preferences of groups of students participating in an interview exercise can be learned to tailor and improve the generated response of a LLM
rationale: The abstract describes a proof-of-concept ILASP system learning user preferences to tailor LLM output. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the work appears to be a method/proof of concept rather than an empirical learning study. Exclude under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) on positive evidence from the abstract. The domain (interview exercise) is not clearly STEM either, but E5 is the clearest failure and is applied as the first failing code in the abstract.
rationale_note: Note: E1 is not applied since the LLM is learner-facing in the abstract, and E2/E6 are not clearly established at abstract stage.

quote: an interactive homework help system based on DeepSeek R1 is developed and first implemented for students enrolled in a large computer science beginning programming course
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based (DeepSeek R1) homework assistant for a university CS programming course, so intervention, domain and population appear met. The abstract does not describe a comparison group, a study design, or a quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a system development and deployment report. Missing information is not evidence, so this is passed to full text to check whether a controlled comparison with learning outcomes exists.

quote: The workshop involved seventy in-service and pre-service teachers in Indonesia
rationale: Participants are in-service and pre-service teachers in a teacher professional development workshop, not K-12 or higher education students learning STEM; in-service teachers are excluded by protocol. Outcomes are perceptions and intentions (affective/perception measures), with no quantitative learning outcome reported in the abstract, and there is no clear control group. Positive evidence of failure on population (in-service teachers) and outcome (perceptions only) supports exclusion at the abstract stage. Coded E4 as the first applicable code in order is E1 uncertain, but population failure is clearly stated; E1 is not evidenced as failing so E4 applies first in order of checking.

The study evaluates Llama 3 for generating SAT Words-in-Context questions. The content is English vocabulary/reading and writing, which is not STEM (protocol excludes language and non-STEM content). The abstract also reports model accuracy on generated questions, not a learner outcome, and reports no control group with learners. Excluded on E2, the first applicable code in order-of-check terms; the abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on non-STEM content (SAT vocabulary). Abstract describes a model-evaluation study, with no learner-facing intervention or comparison group reported.

rationale: The record has only a title, venue (not given), and year (2023); no abstract is available. The title suggests a discussion of ChatGPT in undergraduate computer science, which reads more like a position or discussion paper than an empirical comparative study, but this cannot be confirmed. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded at the abstract stage.

quote: Generative neural models hold great promise in enhancing programming education by synthesizing new content.
rationale: The generative model is used to synthesize visual programming tasks for a specification, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No learner interaction with generative AI and no learning outcome or control group is described. The abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1), which is the first applicable code. Domain (programming) is STEM-adjacent and met.

quote: This review proposes a structured framework for educators and learners to develop critical thinking while engaging with AI in medical contexts.
rationale: The record is a narrative review proposing a framework (DEFT-AI), not an empirical study. It reports no primary experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Its domain is medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Also a review (E10 publication type would apply), and medical education is outside the STEM domain. E6 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: Evaluated on the MATH dataset, our results show that dual-agent setups outperform single agents
rationale: The study evaluates LLM agents interacting with each other on the MATH benchmark dataset; no human learners are described as participants, so the population criterion (K-12 or higher education students) appears not met. Abstract gives positive evidence that the participants are not students: the evaluation is of agent accuracy on a dataset. Also not an empirical study with learner outcomes in the protocol sense. Coded E4 as the first applicable code in the order given (E1 is ambiguous since the agents are LLMs but not clearly learner-facing). Could be revisited at full text if learners are involved.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a special issue, not an empirical study of learners using generative AI. The listed titles cover unrelated topics (charitable donation behaviour, pension allocation, sports rehabilitation, etc.). The record itself reports no intervention, comparison, or outcome data. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). The title of the retracted paper ("Good intentions may be wrong: evidence from anonymous donation behaviour...") is also non-STEM and not a learning study, so E2 would also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code as the record is a retraction notice. Note: the record is a retraction notice, so it is not an eligible empirical study regardless of topic.

Abstract is missing from the index and the venue is not given, so no positive evidence of any criterion failing is available. The title describes a "case study" design, which would suggest E3/design exclusion, but the title alone is not positive evidence at the abstract stage. Also, 3D design fundamentals may or may not count as STEM. Routing to full text to check the comparison group, design, and outcome data.

quote: This working group report presents two complementary studies: a systematic literature review of GenAI interventions in upper-level computing education, and a survey of computing instructors
rationale: The record is an ITiCSE working group report combining a systematic literature review and an instructor survey. It has no controlled comparison of learners with and without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome; the survey measures perspectives and practices. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the protocol, so it is excluded at the abstract stage on E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also questionable (working group report rather than a journal article), but E6 is the first applicable code given the design.

quote: FASH 137: Clothing, Society, and Culture, a General Education course examining the sociocultural meanings of dress.
rationale: The course is a fashion/sociocultural general education course, which is not STEM content (E2). The abstract also gives no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome (the data are assignment design, faculty observations, and reflections), so E3 and E5 would also apply, but E2 is the first code in order that applies. Exclusion is clear from the abstract on the domain criterion alone.

quote: The article provides specific examples of tasks and tools for each direction.
rationale: The article is a theoretical analysis and conceptual proposal (methods: theoretical analysis, comparative analysis, generalization, modeling). It explicitly states that an empirical study on effectiveness is still a future prospect, so it is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclude at E6, the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, so E6 is the earliest clear failure).

quote: This research article examines the multifaceted perspectives of ChatGPT in teacher trainee programs
rationale: The abstract describes a review/analysis of literature and relevant studies ("Through a comprehensive analysis of the available literature"), with no experimental design, control group, or learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established as failing at abstract stage, so E6 is the first code with positive evidence failing.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice covering a whole special issue, not the empirical study itself. The titled article (Ye, Du & He, 2025) appears only as a retracted entry in the list, and no methods or results are reported, so the record is not an empirical study. Under the protocol's first applicable code in order, E1-E5 cannot be assessed from this text, so E6 is the best-supported code. The retraction status also means the article is not a valid eligible publication. Exclusion is based on the notice content only.
rationale_note: Retracted article; the abstract given is a retraction notice.

quote: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting has shown great potential in enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), and recent studies have explored distilling this ability into smaller models.
rationale: The abstract describes a model-to-model distillation framework in which a teacher LLM trains and gives feedback to a student model. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). The abstract also does not describe a human learner population or a learning-outcome comparison with a control group, so those are not evidenced. Excluded at abstract stage on E1 because the positive evidence shows no learner-facing generative AI.

quote: On ALFWorld, we match teacher accuracy at 2.5x lower cost (0.059 to 0.024 per episode). On AppWorld, we achieve 3.5x cost reduction while recovering 79% of teacher accuracy.
rationale: The study is about cost-efficient LLM agents evaluated on ALFWorld and AppWorld (embodied and app-task benchmarks). It is not a learning activity with learners, nor STEM content. Abstract gives positive evidence the domain is not STEM and there is no learner population, not a learning study. Excluded under E2 (content not STEM); the population and design also appear absent, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.
