criteria.criteria_note: venue is an international conference (ICT Electronics Microelectronics convention); abstract describes questionnaire and interview feedback only, no control group

quote: We taught 140 pupils in this way and collected their feedback through a questionnaire.
rationale: Venue is an international conference (MIPRO-style convention proceedings), which is ineligible publication type under E10. On the abstract alone the study also shows no control group and only perception/feedback outcomes (E3/E5 would also apply), but per the protocol's exclusion order and the publication-type rule the record is excluded as E10.

quote: This study aimed to conduct a systematic review of studies published between 2023 and 2025 regarding the employment of generative artificial intelligence applications in mathematics learning and teaching
rationale: The record is a systematic review of twenty prior studies, not an empirical study with its own control group, so it is not an empirical study (E6). The review synthesizes attitudes and challenges and does not report a primary experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria are not met.

quote: A comparative evaluation of LLMs' performance against that of average Ukrainian students was conducted.
rationale: The study has LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot) solve chemistry tasks and compares them with average student performance. Students do not interact with the LLMs as part of a learning activity; the LLMs are evaluated as solvers. There is no control group of learners without generative AI, so the comparison criterion is not met. Exclusion code E3 applies at the abstract stage on positive evidence that no separate non-generative-AI control group exists. The comparison with student averages is not a learner control group receiving a learning condition.

quote: We propose an interactive learning environment for practicing program design based on the design recipe. Backed by an LLM, the environment guides the student through the design process via conversations in natural language
rationale: LLM-backed, learner-facing environment for program design (programming, STEM), so intervention and domain appear met. The abstract does not state whether there is a control group, the study design, or any quantitative learning outcome; it mentions only a user study with observed flexibility and challenges. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text. Venue SPLASH-E is a workshop-style venue, so publication type (journal article) should be checked at full text.

quote: Many universities are integrating mainstream AI tools, such as ChatGPT, into formal and pilot disability accommodations.
rationale: The abstract is a policy/trend overview of AI accommodations for students with disabilities. It describes no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Domain is also not STEM-specific. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the record is a non-empirical overview.

This is an editorial/commentary on AI use in scholarly publishing in orthopedic surgery. It reports no empirical study, no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Under the code order, E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) would arguably apply first since no learner interacts with AI in a learning activity; however, the record is clearly a non-empirical editorial, so E6 is the most direct fit. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical format.

quote: We interviewed 19 undergraduate students who had recently completed an open-ended computational assignment that encouraged the use of genAI, asking them how they used it.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with thematic analysis of 19 undergraduates; it has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Per the rules, the first applicable code in order is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) since the abstract gives positive evidence of only qualitative interview data. Exclusion is based on the abstract alone; the qualitative design also fails the comparison and design criteria.

quote: This study utilizes a phenomenological approach to investigate students'perceptions on how training shaped AI interactions, attitudes towards problem posing with Generative AI
rationale: The study is a phenomenological investigation of student perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the comparison, design and outcome criteria. Per the protocol, perception-only studies are excluded. The exclusion code is E6 (not an empirical study is the closest fit), but the primary failure is qualitative design with perceptions only; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply. Given the first-applicable ordering, E5 may be the more accurate code: the study reports perceptions, not learning outcomes. Note that E6 is set here as a judgment call because the design is qualitative rather than an experiment.

quote: We interviewed 8 K-12 teachers and asked their practices and needs while using any block-based programming (BBP) platform in their classes.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of eight teachers about their needs for AI features. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, learners interacting with generative AI, or a quantitative learning outcome. It fails on design and outcome, and it is not an eligible empirical study (E6). Teachers are not learners, but the code assigned follows the protocol's order, so E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: This article presents a pedagogical style-conditioned audit protocol for automated evaluators that detect answer leakage in LLM-generated tutoring feedback before deployment.
rationale: The study audits automated evaluators (rule-based, embedding, NLI, LLM-as-judge) of LLM tutoring feedback against a human-annotated gold standard. It is a measurement/evaluation study of classifiers, not an experiment in which learners interact with generative AI, and there is no control group of learners or learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failed criterion is the absence of any learner-level comparison; design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison with learners. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a learning intervention study) is the best fit, though the study is empirical. Flagged as exclude at abstract stage.

quote: A corpus-assisted discourse analysis combined frequency counts, five-word collocations, actor-predicate associations, obligation-clause coding, and heuristic analysis of passives, nominalisations, and reporting metonymies.
rationale: The record is a corpus-assisted discourse analysis of 366 titles and abstracts about how scholars describe GenAI responsibility. It is not an empirical study of learners interacting with GenAI, has no control group, and reports no learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study) in the sense of an intervention study; E1 might also apply since no learner-facing AI is studied. E6 is the most fitting first-applicable code given the design is a text analysis rather than an empirical educational study. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence the design is not an intervention study with a comparison group.

quote: This study reports a PRISMA-guided systematic review of 38 peer-reviewed empirical studies addressing three questions
rationale: This is a systematic review of 38 studies, not an empirical study with its own intervention and control group. It fails the Design criterion and the review publication type (E6, not an empirical study). Its own data-extraction aims are decision-making rather than learning outcomes, and no included comparison is reported in the abstract. Excluded as a review.

quote: In this paper, we reflect on the use of LLMs in the study of infant syntax learning by providing an epistemological assessment of several studies from this research program.
rationale: The paper is a retrospective epistemological/methodological reflection on other studies, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learner outcome data. Its subjects are LLMs trained on corpora, not K-12 or higher education students. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly supported. Note that E1 could arguably apply first (no learner-facing generative AI), but the paper's nature as a non-empirical review is the most direct reason.

quote: We introduce manimator, an open-source system that leverages Large Language Models to transform research papers and natural language prompts into explanatory animations using the Manim engine.
rationale: The abstract describes a system/tool paper: an LLM pipeline that generates Manim animations for educational use. It reports no learner interaction, no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study of learners, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Intervention is also not clearly learner-facing generative AI (the LLM generates content for creators), which would be E1, but the first applicable code in order is E1 if the tool is teacher/creator-facing. Given the rule to report the first code that applies in order, the stronger point is that the record is a tool description rather than an empirical study. Note: strictly by order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would apply first because the LLM is used to produce materials rather than being used by learners; the decision is exclude.

criteria.stage_note: GenAI systems were evaluated directly on course assessments; no learner-facing control group

quote: This study evaluates five widely used GenAI systems, ChatGPT-5.2, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and M365 Copilot, using programming tests and examination tasks from an introductory university OOP course.
rationale: The study evaluates the GenAI systems' own performance on OOP assessments. It compares them with historical student results, not a concurrent control group of learners who do not use GenAI. There is no learner-facing intervention with a control arm, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain (programming) is met and the date is 2026. The abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails.

The title identifies this as a systematic review, which is a review article and not an empirical study. Under the protocol, reviews are excluded and fall under E6 (not an empirical study). No abstract is available, but the title alone gives positive evidence that the design criterion fails. Publication type may also be ineligible, but the review label maps most directly to E6.

quote: A case study illustrates how iterative, AI-guided refinement of hypotheses and calculations enhances both accuracy and understanding.
rationale: The abstract describes a command-line LLM tutor platform (NMC2025) for materials simulation, so the intervention and STEM domain appear met. However, the only evidence offered is a "case study" illustrating the tool's use, with no mention of a control group or comparison condition. This is positive evidence of no comparison group (case-study design, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison), so it fails the comparison/design criteria and is excluded under E3 at the abstract stage.
rationale_note: Abstract describes a case study, not a controlled comparison.

rationale: Record has only a title (no abstract, venue not given). Title suggests a paper on preparing gifted educators for generative AI, which points to a preservice/in-service teacher population and possibly a non-experimental design. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence that a criterion fails, so under the abstract-stage rule it cannot be excluded. Advance to full text to check design, population (preservice vs in-service teachers), and whether any learner-facing GenAI intervention with a control group and STEM outcome exists.

criteria.outcome_note: grade comparisons reported; surveys also reported

quote: Surveys and grade comparisons between Fall 2024 (no PyTutor) and Spring 2025 (with PyTutor) reveal improvements in student confidence, positive perceptions, and modest grade gains.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-powered tutor (PyTutor) in an introductory Python course, a community college population, and a STEM domain (programming), all consistent with inclusion. However, the comparison appears to be a historical cohort (Fall 2024 without vs Spring 2025 with the tool), which may be a non-randomized pre/post-style comparison; design and whether it has a concurrent control group cannot be determined from the abstract. Grade gains are a possible quantitative outcome, but the data needed for an SMD are not visible. Venue is SIGCITE, which may be a conference publication type (E10 risk). Not excluded at abstract stage because positive evidence of failure is not clear; should be checked at full text for design, publication type, and outcome statistics.

quote: We describe a course structured in two sequential and complementary parts: foundational machine learning concepts and contemporary LLM applications.
rationale: The abstract describes a course design and course architecture with no comparison group, no controlled design, and no quantitative outcome reported; it reads as a descriptive course-design paper. Its design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group, so it fails the design criterion. The claim that the approach "enhances student comprehension" is not backed by any reported comparison or statistic. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code, since it presents a pedagogical description rather than an empirical evaluation. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, so exclusion at the abstract stage is justified under Rule 2.

criteria.quote: They do not establish learning gains: faculty ratings, peak-load capacity, and complete public-gateway acceptance remain separate evaluation needs.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a system engineering study (model bake-offs, speed gates, source-fidelity comparison, audits) and explicitly states it does not establish learning gains. No comparison group with a learning outcome is reported. Positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured, so exclude at abstract stage under E5.

quote: They do not establish learning gains: faculty ratings, peak-load capacity, and complete public-gateway acceptance remain separate evaluation needs.
rationale: The abstract reports system engineering benchmarks (model speed, source fidelity, audits) and explicitly says no learning gains are established. There is no controlled learning outcome, so E5 applies. Domain is business education, which is also not STEM, but E5 is the basis given the stated absence of learning outcomes.

quote: Utilizing a qualitative design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 PE teachers across Beijing secondary schools.
rationale: The study is a qualitative design based on teacher interviews and case studies, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Teacher estimates of participation are not learner outcome measures. Domain is physical education, which is not clearly STEM. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study of the protocol type (qualitative design); the first applicable code in order would be E2 for non-STEM content, but E6 reflects the primary design failure. Note that the intervention is teacher-facing AI use for management, which also raises E1.

Title indicates ChatGPT (generative AI) use in Vietnamese high school mathematics, so population and domain appear met. No abstract is available, so whether there is a control group, a learning outcome, the design, and effect-size data cannot be determined. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review.

quote: Using PixVerse.ai, Grok Imagine, and Pippit, three video scenarios were generated to represent distinct resistive force regimes
rationale: The abstract describes generative AI used to create synthetic video content for instructors/course design, with no learner interaction, no control group, and no learning outcome measured on students. It reads as a methods/workflow demonstration rather than an empirical comparative study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the best fit; E1 could also apply since the AI appears to be used to produce materials rather than learner-facing use. Abstract stage evidence of failure is positive for comparison and outcome absence, so exclusion is justified.

Generative LLM tutor (Gemini Gems) for a microwave circuit design course in higher education, so intervention, population and domain fit. However, the abstract reports only student perceptions of helpfulness and accuracy, with no quantitative learning outcome and no described control group. Exclude under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Note the venue is a conference proceeding, which would also fall under E10 if the publication-type check were applied first; the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, and E5 precedes E10 in the list, so E5 is reported here.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was administered to 864 students at the University of Palermo (May–June 2025).
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of student attitudes toward AI, with no experimental or comparison group and no learning outcome measured. Outcomes are perceptions and attitudes (factor scores), which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also fails (survey), but the protocol's code order puts E5 first among the applicable codes after E1 to E4, and the intervention is not clearly described as learner-facing generative AI either; E5 is the first clear failure given the abstract. Population (university students) is met.

Title identifies the paper as a systematic review, which is not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome. No abstract is available in the index, but the title alone gives positive evidence that the design is a review (E6). Exclusion rests on the title; no quote from an abstract is available.

quote: The platform integrates the OpenAI GPT-4 Realtime application programming interface (API) within the Unity 3D engine to enable low-latency conversational interaction in immersive environments.
rationale: The content is L2 (second language) speaking practice, which is non-STEM language learning, so E2 applies. The study is also a technical feasibility and usability study with SUS and latency metrics only, with no control group and no learning outcome, which would fail E3 and E5 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: We propose \textbf{DG-Mem}, a dual-grained agentic memory framework that augments a frozen MLLM with a non-parametric, externally stored memory built once from training-time rollouts and consulted read-only at test time.
rationale: The generative model (a frozen MLLM) is used as a backbone for an agentic memory system evaluated on benchmarks (MathVista, MMMU, MMMU-Pro). There is no indication of learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity; the "learning" is machine memory built from rollouts. The record therefore fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). No human learners, control group, or learning outcome is described. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing. Publication type and venue are not stated, but E1 applies first.

quote: Through semi-structured interviews with nine K-12 STEM teachers in the UAE, the research identifies three main themes
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of nine in-service K-12 STEM teachers about their views on ChatGPT. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, has no quantitative learning outcome, and the participants are teachers rather than students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense; qualitative design), which is the first code that clearly applies after the intervention check. Note that E4 (participants not students) also applies; E6 is reported as the first applicable code in the order given only if E1-E5 are considered not applicable, so this is a judgement call for audit.

quote: we evaluated various NLP tools such as ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. We used them to solve typical problems in mechanical engineering
rationale: The study evaluates LLM tools' accuracy on engineering problems. There is no learner interaction and no control group with a learning outcome; the design is a tool-performance evaluation, not an empirical learning experiment. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of learners). Note: the abstract describes a tool-benchmark design, which fails the design/comparison/outcome requirements.

quote: We report a formative expert review with 18 instructional staff from one early undergraduate programming course.
rationale: Formative expert review by 18 instructional staff, reporting only perceived utility, correctness ratings and survey responses. There is no learning outcome measured in learners and no control group, so it is not an eligible empirical comparative study. Participants are instructional staff, not students. Excluded under E5 as no quantitative learning outcome is reported; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply), but the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, and E3 precedes E5, so strictly the code should be E3. Reconsidering the order: E3 (no control group without generative AI) is checked before E5, so the correct first-applicable code is E3.

quote: Following the PRISMA guidelines, 23 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2022 and 2026 were identified and coded
rationale: This is a systematic review of other studies, not an empirical study itself, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Its domain is L2 speaking, a language-learning context rather than STEM, which would also fail the domain criterion (E2 would be the first code in order if E1 is not triggered; the protocol says report the first that applies in order, and E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract). Review articles are not eligible, so E6 is the best-supported code. The review status is clear from the abstract.

quote: By comparing unproctored homework and proctored exam performance, we analyze how student learning behaviors shift in AI-accessible environments
rationale: Undergraduate mathematics (STEM) with a quantitative performance outcome (exam performance), so domain, population and outcome plausibly met. However, the abstract does not show a separate control group without generative AI: it compares AI-accessible unproctored homework with proctored exams, which reads as a within-course observational comparison rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental control. Whether a comparison group exists and whether SMD-computable statistics are reported cannot be determined from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text for checking the comparison and design.

quote: We use this system to analyze 830 interactions of CS2 students across two programming tasks.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive analysis of student-AI interaction logs (question-type classification) with no control group or comparison condition, and no learning outcome measured. Exclusion E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that applies in order; the study is a case-style analysis of interactions rather than a comparative experiment. Intervention (students interacting with generative AI in CS2 tasks) and population (students, STEM domain) appear to be met.

quote: This critical narrative review examines the methodological transition from board-centred exposition to dynamic, interactive, blended, adaptive and artificial-intelligence-supported mathematics teaching.
rationale: The record is a critical narrative review, not an empirical study. It does not report its own primary data or a comparison group; it synthesizes prior literature. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). Review articles are also outside the eligible publication types, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for a narrative review of this kind.

quote: The capability of ChatGPT for instructional purposes is evaluated based on the responses to different questions about these engineering streams.
rationale: Abstract describes an evaluation of ChatGPT responses to classroom questions plus a student survey. No randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI control group is described, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (the survey measures perceptions). Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Design and outcome also appear unmet; E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: We propose four general guidelines for using AI in the bioethics classroom: transparency, antidiscrimination, privacy, and accountability.
rationale: The record is a position/commentary piece proposing guidelines for AI use in bioethics teaching. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Bioethics is also not clearly STEM. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is supported by the abstract.

quote: This study examines how generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, can be integrated into intercultural competence (IC) instruction through critical incident analysis.
rationale: The content is intercultural education for English majors (language/intercultural competence), which is not STEM. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion, so it is excluded at the abstract stage with E2. Other criteria (generative AI intervention, control group, undergraduate population) appear to be met; the outcome is described as qualitative coding, which also raises an E5 concern, but E2 applies first in the code order.

quote: The methodology followed a systematic review of studies published between 2021 and early 2025 in ACM, IEEE, arXiv, and other recognized repositories.
rationale: The record describes a narrative/qualitative thematic synthesis of prior literature and product documentation ("A qualitative thematic synthesis"), not an empirical study with its own comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not a primary empirical study, so it fails E6. Although the abstract mentions a "meta-analysis", it reports no effect sizes or pooled quantitative statistics, and the stated method is qualitative. Also, it includes industry reports and tool documentation, so the design is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: This study examines the integration of generative AI in Business English Class to enhance EFL learners’ motivation.
rationale: The content is Business English / EFL language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The abstract also describes a single-group pre-post design (before and after being taught with AI, paired t-test) with no control group (E3), and the outcome is motivation, an affective measure (not eligible). E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: This issue of JETS focuses on articles that look critically at a variety of technologies.
rationale: The record is a journal editorial overview, not an empirical study. It describes other papers in the issue and reports no original data, intervention, control group, or outcome of its own. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. The mention of ChatGPT only appears as an example within a conceptual framework, not as a learner-facing study. Publication type is a journal item, but the content is an editorial, so E6 is the first applicable code.

rationale: Population is in-service elementary school teachers (excluded population, not K-12 students). The record is a community service workshop report with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome for students; it also is not a research study with a comparison design. Abstract gives positive evidence of population failure, so excluded under E4, the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's population criterion. Note that E3 (no control group) and E5 may also apply.

quote: "we examine the validity of LLM classifications of five student failure modes in mathematics tutoring dialogue"
rationale: The study uses LLMs to classify existing student-tutor dialogue for diagnostic labels; learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no control group, and the outcome is model-human agreement rather than a learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence of E1, so excluded at abstract stage.

quote: The paper presents the results of a study indicating students' preference for learning through gaming as a method of acquiring algorithms knowledge.
rationale: The VR escape room uses generative AI to generate puzzles, and the domain is algorithms (STEM). However, the abstract reports only student preference, which is a perception outcome rather than a quantitative learning measure, and there is no indication of a control group or effect statistics. Exclusion under E5 applies on the abstract's positive evidence that the reported outcome is preference only.

quote: This editorial connects policy framework suggestions for AI literacy in elementary and secondary schools and the papers published in this special issue.
rationale: The record is a journal editorial introducing a special issue, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Although it summarizes featured papers, including a survey and a qualitative study, the editorial itself does not meet the design or outcome criteria. Under the code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code. Publication type (editorial) also falls under E10, but E6 is listed first for the non-empirical nature and the protocol explicitly names editorials under both; E6 is applied as the earliest fitting code in the order given.

quote: This study examines the performance of a LLM on two related graph theoretic problems
rationale: The study evaluates a single LLM's performance on two graph theory problems against an expert-style protocol. There is no control group without generative AI, and no comparison group of learners; the design is a model evaluation rather than a learner-facing experiment. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3. No quantitative learning outcome is reported either (E5 would also apply), but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Future work includes systematic studies to measure the impact of this tool on students' learning outcomes and enhancements to handle a broader range of problems.
rationale: The abstract describes prompt engineering to contextualize problems with GPT-4 and explicitly defers measurement of learning outcomes to future work. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported, so the study fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order is arguably E3 (no control group); however, the abstract gives positive evidence of no learning outcome measured, so E5 is cited. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
exclusion_code_check: E3 is listed before E5 in the protocol order; no control group is described in the abstract, which is positive evidence for E3.

quote: We tested whether these explanations achieve USML in a human trial teaching active learning strategies across three related domains.
rationale: Abstract describes a human trial with LLM-generated explanations (ILP + LLM pipeline) versus self-learning, with a quantitative out-of-sample performance outcome, so the intervention and comparison may qualify. However, the abstract does not state the learner population (students vs. general adults), the STEM domain (active learning across abstract domains is not clearly STEM), the publication venue or type, or the design details. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is advanced to full text for checking.

quote: The research proves the statement about the importance of inputs being clearly worded in order to get a specific output.
rationale: Abstract describes a prompt-engineering analysis and a catalog of template prompts for ChatGPT use with no comparison group, no learner outcome measure, and no quantitative learning data. It appears to be a methodological/descriptive paper, not an empirical controlled study. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also appears not to be a comparison design (E3/E6 possible). Domain (philology training) also appears non-STEM, which is a further concern that would be checked first under E2 ordering; however, the order rule applies first to E1, then E2. Note: under the strict ordering, E2 would be the first applicable code if philology is clearly non-STEM. Philology is a humanities field, and the abstract describes philologists' training, so E2 applies first.

No generative AI tool is used as a learning intervention, no control group exists, and the outcome is career interest (a perception/affective measure), not a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence: the design is a survey with no intervention. Under the code order, E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention) applies first. The abstract's only AI mention is for editing the manuscript text.

Publication type also falls outside journal articles, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: This edition is a special issue introduction; the 9 articles within this edition do not try and justify the use of ePortfolio
rationale: The record is a journal editorial introducing a special issue on ePortfolio practice. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Generative AI is only mentioned as background context, and no STEM domain or learner-facing generative AI intervention is described.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles

quote: A GenAI Programming Tutor with a Social Robot Interface: A Mixed-Methods Pilot on Theory of Mind Attributions and Technology Acceptance
rationale: Venue is EduRobotX@EC-TEL, a workshop-style venue (EduRobotX is a workshop series), and the title describes a pilot study. Based on the venue, the record appears to be a workshop paper or work in progress rather than a journal article, which the protocol excludes (E10). The abstract is missing, so the other criteria cannot be assessed from the record. The venue inference is the basis for exclusion; a researcher should verify the publication type. Programming domain and generative AI tutor intervention are indicated by the title. Pilot design and outcomes (theory of mind attributions, technology acceptance) are not clearly a learning outcome, so this would be a further concern.

quote: We provide theoretical, methodological and empirical answers in the negative but show how limits can be circumvented.
rationale: The record is a theoretical and model-evaluation paper on LLM checkpoints' conditionals versus Solomonoff induction. It does not describe a learning intervention with learners, a control group, or a learning outcome. It is not an empirical study of learners, so it fails the eligibility criteria on the design and intervention, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order. Field is not STEM learning either, but E6 is reported as the first applicable code under the protocol's order.

quote: This research explores how artificial intelligence (AI) can support secondary computer science (CS) educators by reducing the burden of planning, grading and content alignment
rationale: The AI tools described are used by teachers for lesson planning, assessment design, and grading support, not by learners in a learning activity. The protocol requires learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. No control group, learner outcome, or quantitative design is described in the abstract. Domain (secondary CS) is met.

quote: This work constitutes a secondary analysis; it synthesizes findings from ten peer-reviewed empirical and theory-informed empirical studies
rationale: The record is a systematic review (secondary analysis synthesizing other studies), so it is not an empirical study under the protocol. It also concerns foreign language teacher education, which is non-STEM content, so it would fail the domain criterion as well. The primary exclusion is E6 because the design is a review rather than an empirical study of learners; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply, but E6 is reported first in the protocol's order only if it precedes E2, which it does not. Under the protocol's first-applicable ordering, E1 through E5 are checked first; the abstract gives no clear evidence for E1, but it does show the content is foreign language teaching (non-STEM), which is E2 and comes before E6. Therefore the code should be E2.

quote: It systematically evaluates the readability performance of these three models in generating intermediate Chinese reading text
rationale: The study evaluates text output of three LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, Kimi, Doubao) via NLP readability analysis of 840 generated texts. There are no learners interacting with the tool, no control group, and no learning outcome measured in learners; it is a model-output evaluation. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code given the protocol's ordering, though E1 (not learner-facing) and E3 (no control group) also plausibly apply. Positive evidence of failure exists, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The implementation of ChatISA provided valuable insights and highlighted key challenges.
rationale: The abstract describes a system description and implementation of a generative AI chatbot (ChatISA) for Information Systems students. It reports no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; findings are described as benefits and insights, suggesting a descriptive/development study. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present (no comparison described), and the abstract indicates a tool-development/implementation report. Excluding under E3 (no control group without generative AI) at the abstract stage, though E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also plausibly apply and could be the code on full text review.

quote: A mixed-methods research framework, assisted by AI, is used which utilises large language models (LLMs), cross-lingual semantic analysis and human-controlled validation.
rationale: The AI (LLMs, embeddings) is used by researchers to analyse a corpus of doctoral dissertations, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. There is no learner interaction with generative AI, no control group, and the topic is family representations in education research rather than STEM content. Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code; the abstract gives positive evidence the intervention criterion fails.

quote: The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered using the PRISMA-P protocol.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 22 studies, not an empirical primary study with a control group, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Abstract gives positive evidence the design is a review, which fails the design criterion.

quote: The research employs a qualitative descriptive design to investigate the interactive processes and pedagogical implications of integrating AI.
rationale: The study is explicitly qualitative and descriptive (logs, reflections, interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study is not quite the fit; the closest protocol code for a non-qualifying design is E6 as the empirical design fails the eligibility criteria). Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome is present in the abstract.

quote: We conducted semi-structured interviews with nine key informants (KIs) from six U.S. jurisdictions between May and August 2024.
rationale: Record is a qualitative interview study of policy key informants about HPV vaccination. It has no generative AI intervention, no STEM content, no student population, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also an abstract-only conference record (AACR Annual Meeting), so it is not a journal article. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, and qualitative design) is used as the first applicable code, though E10 (publication type) would also apply. Excluded on positive evidence at abstract stage.

quote: "an online qualitative studies layout became used regarding college, university students and instructors in KPK"
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative design with in-depth interviews analysed by thematic analysis, and no control group. Qualitative designs are excluded by the Design criterion. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, this is an empirical-looking study whose core design is qualitative, so E6 is used as the closest code. The title ("systematic review") conflicts with the described primary study. Note that the abstract also mentions "preliminary quantitative findings" with no described comparison group. Using the abstract alone, the record fails the design requirement, so it is excluded. Although the protocol's codes do not map this exactly, E6 is the best fit because the study is qualitative rather than a comparative experiment.

This record describes a benchmark dataset for evaluating multimodal LLMs on physics questions. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning-outcome study design. It is not an empirical study of learners, so it fails on design/comparison. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), since no learners interact with a generative AI tool in a learning activity; the abstract only evaluates models on benchmark questions. Given the code-ordering rule, E1 is the first that applies, so the exclusion code should be E1 rather than E6. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is model evaluation, not learner-facing use.

quote: This narrative review examines the modalities and clinical evidence for teledentistry
rationale: The record is a narrative review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It has no control group, no learner-facing quantitative outcome, and its topic is dental/teledentistry, not STEM. E6 is the first applicable code in order (E1 to E5 are not clearly established from the abstract, and E6 is the decisive positive evidence of non-empirical design). Using the abstract-stage rule, the exclusion rests on the explicit "narrative review" statement.

quote: The demonstration presents a solution for new engineering education and its application potential.
rationale: Record is a UbiComp Companion demonstration paper (conference venue), so publication type is not eligible (E10). Also, the abstract describes a system demonstration with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well. Per protocol order, E10 is reported first as the publication-type failure applies.

quote: Results of a pedagogical experiment on using ChatGPT for the development of pre-service mathematics teachers' critical thinking are described.
rationale: Abstract reports a pedagogical experiment with ChatGPT used to generate pupil responses for pre-service mathematics teachers (higher education, mathematics: population and domain fit). However, the abstract does not state whether there is a separate control group without generative AI, the experimental design, or the quantitative data for an SMD. Sign test suggests a quantitative outcome, but the comparison and design are not clear. Also, ChatGPT appears to be used to generate responses for analysis, so whether learners interact with the tool is unclear. Not excluded at abstract stage; full text needed to resolve intervention, comparison, and design.

quote: A questionnaire co-created with ChatGPT was administered to nursing students, nurses and educators aiming at exploring how those technologies would impact on the world of healthcare and education.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of perceptions about AI in nursing and healthcare education. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only perceptions. Domain is nursing/health professions, which is also outside STEM as defined by the protocol. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome), though the design and domain also fail, as a survey is an empirical study but not an eligible design.

Abstract describes a semester-long observational study of an embedded AI tutor with 309 students. It reports correlations between query conversation styles and challenge completion, with no control group that lacks generative AI. The design is observational, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, so E3 applies. Cybersecurity is STEM-adjacent (computing), and the students are higher education, so those criteria are not the failing ones. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group. Design is observational, which also fails the design criterion.

criteria.criteria_note: ML model training paper; no learners interacting with a generative AI tool

quote: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant improvements in contextual understanding.
rationale: This is a machine learning methods paper on distilling attention in LLMs, evaluated on benchmarks. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). It is also not an education study and has no learner population.

criteria.intervention_note: ClinicalBERT used as an NLP classifier to detect VTE in EHR notes; no learner interacts with a generative AI tool

quote: We successfully developed and tested a transformer NLP model to detect cancer associated VTE longitudinally using a combination of clinical notes and radiology reports
rationale: The record describes a transformer (ClinicalBERT) NLP classifier applied to EHR notes to detect venous thromboembolism. Learners do not interact with any generative AI tool, there is no learning activity, and the study is not STEM education or a learning comparison. Exclusion E1 applies: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. This is a clear abstract-stage failure on intervention, so the remaining criteria were not weighed further.

quote: we evaluate the informativeness of different curriculum document sources, benchmark the performance of general-purpose LLMs on mapping curricula to competencies, and analyze error patterns
rationale: The study uses LLMs to analyze curriculum documents and map courses to competencies (curricular analytics). No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is also no learner-facing comparison group or learning outcome; the LLM is scored against human annotations, not studied as an intervention with students. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: we explore the efficacy of LLMs to assess the programs across two dimensions
rationale: The LLM is used to assess student-created programs (automated grading), not as a learner-facing tool used within a learning activity. Under the protocol, AI used only for grading is excluded, and E1 applies as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. No control group is described, so the study does not appear to have a comparison design either. Excluding at abstract stage on the positive evidence that the LLM is an assessment tool rather than a learner-facing intervention.

quote: A community-engaged participatory research methodology was employed within a Doctor of Healthcare Administration program.
rationale: The study concerns doctoral writing pedagogy in a Doctor of Healthcare Administration program, which is non-STEM content. It also uses a qualitative participatory design (thematic analysis of discussion posts, reflections, and focus groups) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) maps 421 studies (2015-2026, 2026 partial) along a technical axis (RQ1) and four value dimensions (RQ2-RQ5).
rationale: The record is a scoping review and evidence map of NLP applied to student evaluation of teaching comments. It is not an empirical study with a learner-facing generative AI intervention and a control group, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Reviews are also ineligible publication types under the protocol. Per the protocol's exclusion ordering, E1 would be the first code to check, but the abstract gives no evidence of learner-facing generative AI use; the review's primary failure is non-empirical design, so E6 is the applicable code.
decision_note: Scoping review; not an eligible empirical study.

quote: This white paper was not written using LLMs.
rationale: The record is a white paper describing a graduate class experiment on LLM use for astronomy research. It reports student impressions and anecdotal observations (e.g., about 20% false citations) rather than a controlled comparison with a non-generative-AI control group, and no quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable statistics is described. It is not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in order, since the design is a descriptive white paper; E3 (no control group) would also apply. Abstract stage evidence is positive, so exclusion is supported.

Title describes a systematic review of generative AI in higher art education. Reviews are not empirical studies, so E6 applies. Art education is also not STEM, which would be an independent failure (E2), but the first applicable code in order is E2 only if E1 is not triggered; the protocol's order places E2 before E6. Note: under the strict code order, E2 (content not STEM) is the first code that applies, so the code should be read as E2 on audit. No abstract was available to confirm other criteria.

quote: This paper presents a research-question-driven literature review of VR/XR environments, CAD/CAM-integrated virtual workflows, digital twins and AI-powered tutors applied to semiconductor manufacturing education.
rationale: The record is a literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It is not an original study with a control group and quantitative outcome data. Semiconductor manufacturing education is a STEM-adjacent engineering domain, but the design criterion fails regardless.

quote: An analysis of 58 peer-reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2025 identified three primary categories of AI agents
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 58 studies, not an empirical study with its own control group. Under the protocol's exclusion list for reviews, it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also questionable for a review, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for a review of this kind.

quote: the employees who received training using the system demonstrated more engagement and better job performance than those using traditional methods
rationale: Population is employees in the energy industry receiving workplace training, which the protocol excludes (workplace training and non-student adults; E4). The abstract also reports a survey of perceptions and engagement, with no clear quantitative learning outcome, and the energy-sector training content is not clearly STEM. Exclusion on E4 is the first code that applies in order of the protocol's listing, since E1 (intervention) appears met on the abstract.

quote: A total of 312 records were found in the databases searched, 54 of which were duplicates, 258 were screened, and 26 studies were included in the final analysis.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6 (Not an empirical study). It also mixes adaptive tutors, predictive analytics and non-generative systems, and is not a primary comparison study. Because the review itself is not an empirical study, E6 applies.

The record has no abstract, only a title and venue (Nature Machine Intelligence, 2023). The title suggests a commentary or perspective on LLMs in higher education, which would likely fail E6 (not an empirical study) or E5 at full text. However, the abstract gives no positive evidence of a failed criterion, so under the abstract-stage rule it cannot be excluded now. Sent forward for full-text check of design and study type.

quote: We also provide experimental results on CSEPrompts to evaluate the performance of several LLMs with respect to generating Python code and answering basic computer science and programming questions.
rationale: Abstract describes a benchmark evaluating LLM performance on CS prompts and MCQs, not learners interacting with a generative AI tool in a learning activity. No control group without generative AI is described; the comparison is among LLMs. Exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Fulltext-level detail not available, but the abstract gives positive evidence that the design lacks a non-generative-AI comparison.

quote: Student ratings suggest that LLM feedback is perceived as helpful, constructive, and relevant
rationale: Abstract describes LLM-generated feedback on programming projects in a university STEM course (population and domain appear met). However, the main reported results are preferences and perceived helpfulness, which the protocol excludes as outcomes. It is unclear whether there is a controlled comparison with learning outcomes measured, so the record is advanced to full text rather than excluded on the abstract alone.

quote: Материалы и методы. В работе использованы системный анализ образовательных технологий, обзор цифровых платформ.
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic analysis and review of digital platforms, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. No comparison group, design, or quantitative outcome is reported. The record is a conceptual/review piece, so E6 applies. It is also a conference venue (E10 possible), but E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Domain is mathematics-related, and the AI component is mentioned only as "adaptive courses using artificial intelligence", so the generative nature is unclear.

quote: This research adopts a posthumanist innovative methodology where data is produced through the intra-action between the researcher (human) and ChatGPT (non-human).
rationale: The abstract describes a posthumanist methodology in which data come from intra-action between the researcher and ChatGPT, with "generated examples" illustrating use. There is no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a conceptual or methodological paper and not an empirical comparative study, so E6 applies. Under the first-applicable-code rule, E6 is reported here, since the absence of a comparison group and of a quantitative outcome both point to a non-empirical study.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: Through an investigation of interviews with Pell grant eligible college students at open access colleges, we address the following research questions
rationale: The study is an interview-based qualitative investigation of students' descriptions of generative AI use and attitudes. It has no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense, i.e., qualitative design excluded), it fails. E6 is applied as the first applicable code given design is qualitative; E5 would also apply since no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Protocol ordering places E5 before E6, but the quote supports the qualitative design, which is the primary failing; the record is excluded.

quote: This PhD investigates how learning-related signals become visible in student–LLM interaction, and how temporal and semantic prompting behaviours relate to short-term learning gains in programming tasks.
rationale: This is a PhD doctoral consortium-style proposal (IUI Companion) describing planned work. The abstract describes LLM use in programming with learning gains, which is consistent with the domain and intervention, but it does not state a control group, comparison design, or statistics. It does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so it is not excluded at abstract stage. Publication type (IUI Companion, likely a short doctoral paper rather than a journal article) may fail E10, which should be checked at full text.

decision_note: Systematic review, not an empirical study.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 60 studies, so it is not an empirical study and fails E6. It is also a review in publication-type terms (E10 could apply), but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order, and no primary experiment is reported. Exclusion is clear at the abstract stage.

The record is a position/discussion paper that "examines institutional policies, pedagogical models, and assessment strategies" and presents a rubric. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Also, the venue SIGCITE suggests a conference paper, which would be E10, but E6 applies first in the code order given the abstract's non-empirical nature. No direct quote supports the exclusion beyond the abstract's description of the paper's aims, so quote is null.

quote: we propose a novel benchmark based on authentic Croatian state exams (high school final exams)
rationale: The record is a benchmark evaluating LLMs directly on exam questions, not learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. There is no learner population and no control group without generative AI. Content is Croatian language, which is non-STEM (Domain). Excluded under E6 as a benchmark/evaluation rather than an empirical learning study; the first applicable code in order would arguably be E1 (no learner-facing intervention), but the abstract's core is a model benchmark, so E6 is the closest fit. Also excluded on Domain and Comparison at abstract stage based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: This paper presents NuPaD (Nuclear &Particle Physics -- Deep Learning Tutor), a novel pedagogical framework designed for the graduate-level subatomic physics curriculum.
rationale: The abstract describes a GenAI-based tutoring framework for graduate subatomic physics, which fits intervention, domain, and population. However, it presents an architectural framework and design philosophy with no mention of an experiment, a control group, or any learning outcome data. Design, comparison, and outcome cannot be confirmed as met from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded. Note that the criteria field above contains a duplicated key; the decision is unaffected.

quote: Through a case study of an innovative undergraduate course, we examine how students interact with and adapt to various AI modalities
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory case study with no comparison group, and it reports qualitative insights rather than a quantitative learning outcome. This is positive evidence of a non-empirical-comparative design (E6 applies as the case-study design fails the eligibility design requirement). Business education is also not clearly STEM. Venue is CHI Extended Abstracts, which is a conference publication type (E10) and would be removed by rule before screening; E6 is reported as first applicable in the code order given the case-study design.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome reported in abstract
criteria.design_note: describes a practical framework and implementation; no comparison or experimental design evident

quote: We describe a practical framework for integrating Gen AI into physics instruction through the use of context prompts
rationale: The paper is a practical framework/teaching description for an introductory physics course with about 70 students. The abstract reports no control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome; discussion focuses on conceptual framing and practical considerations. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified by positive evidence that the study is not an experimental comparison with a learning measure. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group) since the design lacks a comparison, but the clearest failure is the absence of any quantitative learning outcome, so E5 is used. Note that E3 could also be argued; the abstract gives no comparison group, so this is a judgment call for the auditor.

Abstract is absent from the index, so no positive evidence of any criterion failure is available. The venue is a German-language e-Learning conference (Fachtagung, Gesellschaft für Informatik), which suggests a conference paper (E10 would apply), but the record does not state the publication type explicitly. The chatbot topic is about study program orientation, and it is unclear whether the intervention is generative, whether there is a control group, or whether any learning outcome is measured. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review, where the publication type (conference proceedings would be E10) and the methods can be checked.

quote: Thirty middle school students participated in a semester-long programming course.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-supported Python learning environment with programming achievement outcomes and middle school students (K-12, STEM programming). However, the abstract does not indicate a control group without generative AI; the design appears to be correlational/clustering and regression on a single cohort, which suggests E3 or design failure. Since the abstract does not give positive evidence of a missing control group, the record is passed to full text to check whether a comparison group exists and whether the design is eligible.

quote: In this paper, we present findings from a focus group study with 29 STEM faculty members at a large public university in the United States.
rationale: The study is a focus group study of STEM faculty perceptions, which is a qualitative, non-empirical-trial design with no learners interacting with GenAI, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense; qualitative design) is applied as the first applicable code given the protocol's exclusion of qualitative designs. Population is faculty, not students, which would also fail E4, but the design failure is the clearest positive evidence. Note: E1 (learner-facing intervention) is arguably the first code in order; however, the abstract gives positive evidence that the study is qualitative focus-group work, and the intervention is not a learner-facing tool, so E1 would also apply. Applying code order strictly, E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Understanding Algorithmic Problem Solving using LLMs
rationale: The venue (SIGCSE Virtual) is a conference, so the record is likely a conference paper and falls under E10 publication type. The abstract also describes GPT-4o being evaluated directly on problems (no learner-facing intervention or control group reported), with no comparison group or learning outcome, which points further toward exclusion. Coding E10 as the first applicable code by the protocol's order is a judgment call; the abstract alone does not explicitly state publication type, so the audit should verify the venue type.

quote: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a standard route to compress Large Language Models (LLMs) into compact students
rationale: The paper is a model-compression method in which an LLM teacher supervises a student model through knowledge distillation. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is no indication of a learner population or a STEM learning outcome. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: Anais do VI Simpósio Brasileiro de Educação em Computação (EDUCOMP 2026)
rationale: The venue is a conference proceedings (Anais of a symposium), which is an ineligible publication type under the protocol (E10). Also, the abstract describes a case study examining LLM prompt quality for GLA structures, with no clear control group or quantitative learning outcome for learners, which would raise further concerns at full text. Exclusion is based on the publication type, which is positive evidence from the venue line.

quote: We present a novel framework for analyzing and interpreting electron microscopy images in semiconductor manufacturing using vision-language instruction tuning.
rationale: The record is a symposium paper (AAAI Spring Symposia), which is a conference-type publication and not an eligible journal article, so E10 applies. It also describes an industrial semiconductor manufacturing tool for model training and analysis, with no learners interacting with the tool, no student population, and no learning outcome. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, but the publication type alone is a clear exclusion.

quote: This book takes that convergence as its subject. The fifteen chapters that follow move from foundations to frontiers.
rationale: The record is a academic book (edited/authored volume) providing an overview of AI paradigms, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM-specific learning intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); publication type is also not a journal article (E10 would be a secondary code, but only the first applicable code is reported and E6 applies first in the ordering).

quote: By analyzing responses from surveys, open-ended questions, and student-ChatGPT dialog data, we aim to provide a comprehensive view of ChatGPT's utility
rationale: Case study using surveys, open-ended questions, and dialog data focused on student perceptions. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is described, and the design is a case study, which is not eligible. Exclude on E5 because the abstract reports only perceptions and interactions, with no quantitative learning measure. Design also appears ineligible (case study), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given for the stated evidence.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of case-study design and perception-only outcomes.

quote: Experimental evaluation shows high groundedness and accuracy, with a low hallucination rate.
rationale: Abstract describes a RAG conversational AI assistant (generative, learner-facing) used by primary-school students in an earthquake education robotics activity, so intervention and population appear met. However, the abstract reports system evaluation (groundedness, accuracy, hallucination rate) rather than a learner outcome, and mentions no control group or comparison design. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text for checking of comparison, design, and learning outcome. Domain (earthquake safety/robotics) is borderline STEM and needs full-text clarification.

quote: Using the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method, the research followed several steps
rationale: This is a systematic literature review of 11 selected articles, not an empirical study. The abstract explicitly states it does not include direct classroom experimentation. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). Review papers are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the primary code applied here.
exclusion_reason: Systematic literature review, not an empirical study
notes: Abstract-stage exclusion; the abstract gives positive evidence of a review design.

quote: Compared to baseline GPT-4o performance without SRG (average accuracy: 55.6%), and with SRG integration achieves 77.1% average accuracy
rationale: Science sketch assessment (STEM) with generative models (GPT-4o/GPT-4.1). However, the abstract is about automated assessment of student sketches by an AI system, not clearly learner-facing use of generative AI (E1 possible). It compares GPT model variants and a multi-agent pipeline against baselines, so whether a non-generative-AI control group exists is unclear. No clear student learning outcome or student-control design is described. Abstract does not give positive evidence of an exclusion, so advance to full text to check intervention (learner interaction), comparison, population (students vs. dataset), and outcome. Venue is NeurIPS, which may raise publication-type concerns (conference proceedings, E10) to verify at full text.

quote: This article describes an action research project that uses a mixed-methods approach to explore postgraduate second language (L2) English Language Learner (ELL) students’ views of artificial intelligence (AI) tools
rationale: The study is an action research project exploring student views (perceptions) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is EAP/English writing, which is non-STEM. Multiple criteria fail on positive evidence from the abstract. Exclusion code set to E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design); the primary failure is the absence of a comparison group, but E3 applies to comparison failures and the first applicable code in order is considered here. Note that E2 (non-STEM content) precedes E3 and E6 in the ordering and clearly applies because the course is English for Academic Purposes; the code ordering should be checked by the auditor.

quote: Our findings demonstrate that CoTAL improves GPT-4's scoring performance across domains, achieving gains of up to 38.9% over a non-prompt-engineered baseline
rationale: The study is about LLM-based automated scoring of formative assessments, with GPT-4 used largely by the teacher/researcher to score responses, not clearly as a learner-facing tool (possible E1). Scoring performance is measured against a non-prompt-engineered GPT-4 baseline, not a non-generative-AI control group, and the abstract's teacher/student feedback is perceptual. Multiple criteria are unclear, but the abstract does not give definitive evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text to check whether learners interact with the generative tool and whether a non-AI comparison and learning outcome exist.

quote: Our system is designed for comprehensive teacher support, including customized teaching material generation and AI-assisted assessment.
rationale: The framework is an educator-facing tool: the LLM is used by teachers to generate teaching materials and assess work, not as a learner-facing intervention. Per the protocol, AI used only by the teacher is E1. No learner interaction with generative AI is described and no control group or learning outcome is evident in the abstract.

quote: The pilot study shows that LLMs can significantly reduce the workload of teachers in creating programming questions
rationale: The abstract describes LLM use for content generation by teachers (creating programming tasks, reference solutions, test examples). Per protocol, AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is E1. No learner-facing generative AI interaction is described, and no control group, learning outcome, or comparative design is reported. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of the teacher-only use.

quote: This paper examines the English language syllabification task, focusing on two advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) models: ChatGPT and Gemini.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT and Gemini's accuracy on English syllabification (phonology/linguistics), which is not STEM content under the protocol. It is also a model-vs-model accuracy evaluation with no learner participants and no control group, so it fails comparison, design, and population criteria as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order, since the content is non-STEM (linguistics/phonology).

At abstract stage, the intervention is ChatGPT (generative LLM) integrated into a second-semester engineering physics course, compared with a control cohort using traditional teaching. Outcomes include grades and Hake factors (learning gains), which are quantitative. Design is described as an experimental analysis with two cohorts, which is not clearly randomized or a quasi-experiment with comparison group; the design criterion is therefore unclear rather than failed, and the full text should confirm whether a comparison group and SMD-computable statistics exist. Population (university engineering students) and domain (physics) are met. No positive evidence of failure, so include for full-text review.

criteria.stage_note: No empirical design or comparison group described

quote: This opinion article argues that universities must take a leadership role
rationale: The record is an opinion article arguing for university leadership on AI. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is non-empirical.

quote: A systematic review approach, adapted through the PRISMA model, was employed to review several studies from 2018 to 2025 from four databases
rationale: The record is a systematic review (secondary synthesis), not an empirical study with its own control group and learning outcome data, so it fails E6. It also does not report a comparison group or SMD-eligible data. Excluded under E6 at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is a review.

quote: This narrative review examined evidence relevant to the use of generative AI, digital translation tools, and e-learning platforms in Filipino instruction
rationale: The record is a narrative review of literature (Methods: literature 2019-2025 identified through searches), not an empirical study. It has no primary comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, and its domain is Filipino language and literature, which is non-STEM. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is supported by the abstract; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply, but E6 is earlier in the sequence only in the listing order of the code table, so E6 is reported as the code that most directly reflects the review design. Note: under the stated order E1-E10, E2 precedes E6 and would be the first code triggered by the non-STEM domain; the audit should confirm which code the researcher prefers.

quote: This descriptive cross-sectional study surveyed 872 tertiary students from public and private institutions in Luzon, Philippines.
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey of perceptions of Meta AI dependency. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; it measures only perceptions and usage-related attitudes. Under the protocol's design and outcome criteria it fails. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) only if unclear; however, the design is not an empirical experiment, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is the best fit, as the survey design is not an eligible empirical design. Abstract provides positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: we compare feedback generated by a frontier LLM (OpenAI o1) to feedback from nine teaching assistants across 90 student responses
rationale: Programming (STEM) with LLM-generated feedback on student short answers. However, the abstract compares LLM feedback to TA feedback, rating feedback quality with a rubric by human and LLM raters. It is unclear whether learners interact with the LLM (feedback may be delivered without learner interaction), whether there is a learning outcome (rubric-scored feedback quality is not a learning measure), and whether the design is an experimental comparison group. Expert ratings of feedback text are not clearly a quantitative learning outcome. Unsure at abstract stage; resolve at full text if the paper reports student reattempt performance under the conditions.

The record has only a title and venue with no abstract. The title suggests a narrative or review-style commentary on LLMs in medicine and surgery, which is not an empirical study. Domain is medicine/surgery (health professions), not STEM as defined by the protocol. No quote is available because the record contains no abstract text. Exclusion uses E6 as the first applicable code; the domain issue (health) also points to E2 but E6 is ordered earlier and the record does not show an empirical design.

quote: Our research utilizes the cubits.ai platform, developed at Princeton University, to demonstrate how generative AI, powered by advanced LLMs, can transform standard video playlists into interactive, AI-enhanced learning experiences.
rationale: The abstract describes an LLM-based platform (generative AI for video summaries and on-demand questions) used by computer science students, so intervention, population, and domain appear met. However, the abstract reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a framework/position paper. Missing information is not positive evidence of failure, so I cannot exclude at the abstract stage and the record should be advanced to full text to check comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: conducted a statistical analysis of ratings provided by 30 high school IT teachers
rationale: At abstract stage, the study evaluates generated MCQs rated by 30 high school IT teachers, not learners. Its participants are not students, and the outcome is teacher ratings of question quality rather than a learning measure.
