The population criterion fails on positive evidence, so exclude under E4 (the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's checks is E1 for intervention, which is not clearly failing since the LLM generates questions for teachers, not learners; population is the clearer failure). The outcome also appears not to be a learner outcome (E5), but E4 is reported as the first clear failure.

quote: In our first implementation of this course with 68 students they not only successfully built non-trivial software systems with ai support
rationale: Course description and single-implementation report with no comparison group; it reads as a course-design/experience paper rather than an empirical comparative study. Abstract gives positive evidence of no control group (E3 would also apply), but the design is a course concept paper, so E6 is the best fit. Note: the record is a conference paper (SEET@ICSE) which per protocol would be E10 at the publication-type level; the publication-type criterion is the stronger ground. Excluding under E10 is more accurate given venue.

Abstract describes development of a physical computing kit for teaching supervised and unsupervised machine learning to high school students. It reports no experimental comparison, no control group, and no learning outcome data; it reads as a design/development paper. Nothing indicates a generative AI tool is learner-facing (generative AI is mentioned only as background). Exclusion is for not being an empirical study (E6), since the abstract gives positive evidence of a design-development report without an evaluated comparison. The E6 call is based on the abstract alone and could be revisited if the full text reports a controlled evaluation with a generative AI component; the kit appears to use autonomous robots rather than generative models.

quote: A sample of 100 B.Ed students from five teacher education institutions was surveyed using a structured questionnaire.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey design with no comparison group, so no control group without generative AI exists (E3). It also reports only perceptions and usage, with no quantitative learning outcome (E5). Exclusion code is the first applicable in order, E3 is chosen since the protocol's order puts comparison/control before outcome. Design is a survey, which also fails the design criterion. Domain is unclear from the abstract (lesson planning generically, not explicitly STEM).

quote: The study utilised a pre- and post-survey approach to evaluate shifts in AI literacy and comfort before and after the workshop.
rationale: Single-group pre-post survey design with no control group (E3 applies on comparison/design), and outcomes are self-reported confidence and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. The protocol asks for the first applicable code in order; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E3 would be the first code that clearly applies only if E1/E2 are not triggered. Strictly, the abstract gives positive evidence of no control group, so E3 is the earliest clear failure once E1 and E2 are not positively shown to fail. Participants are educators (in-service teachers and outreach participants), which also weighs against population, but that is not conclusive from the abstract.

quote: Experimental results show that RoBERTa-Base achieved the best performance, with an F1 score of 88.7% and an Exact Match (EM) score of 82.4%
rationale: The study fine-tunes BERT-family extractive QA models (RoBERTa, BERT, DistilBERT) on a Java dataset and evaluates them with F1/EM. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool in a learning activity; the models are not shown to be generative and there is no learner-facing use or control group comparing learners. Excluded under E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Outcome is model performance, not learner learning, and there is no comparison group of learners.

quote: This dataset presents a Bengali-language dataset designed to fine-tune AI powered hint-based tutoring systems for the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) science curriculum in Bangladesh.
rationale: The record is a data description paper presenting a dataset for fine-tuning tutoring systems. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learning outcome measured in learners, so it is not an empirical study of an intervention. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The E1 check would also be unresolved since no learner-facing generative tool is described, but E6 applies and is the most direct fit.
rationale_note: Abstract stage exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is a dataset description without an empirical comparison.

criteria.quote_note: LLM used for grading, not learner-facing

quote: This paper presents a Python-based system utilizing the Google Gemini API to grade student programming exams automatically.
rationale: The generative AI (Gemini API) is used to grade student exams, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Under the protocol, AI used only for grading is excluded, and E1 applies (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI). No control group of learners using generative AI is described, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A survey conducted among non-IT, non-programmer participants showed that 61% reported significant transformation in AI understanding
rationale: Abstract describes a training program delivered to employees in the oil and gas industry and other sectors, with outcomes reported only as survey percentages (perceptions). There is no control group and no comparison design described, so the study fails the comparison/design requirements (E3). It also reports no quantitative learning outcome. The no-code AI tool is not clearly generative at abstract stage, and the population is largely employees (workplace training), which would also fail eligibility. Excluded on the first applicable code, E3.

quote: This study aims to map research trends and analyze the pedagogical role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing students' critical thinking skills in physics education. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study. It does not report its own controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol, reviews are excluded and E6 (not an empirical study) is the applicable code.

quote: This narrative review focuses on foundational research on cognitive offloading and on peer-reviewed studies of GenAI published through September 05, 2026.
rationale: The record is a narrative review of prior literature, not an empirical study with a control group. It fails the design criterion and is not an empirical study (E6). Per the protocol, reviews are also ineligible publication types, but the primary reason is that it reports no original empirical study.

The record has a title only and no abstract. The title describes an in-context learning case study of LLM-based qualitative coding of classroom dialog, which is not clearly learner-facing generative AI, not clearly STEM, and not clearly an experimental design with a control group. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Leveraging large language models (LLMs), competency tracking, and adaptive assessment, the system guides students using a Socratic teaching methodology
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based conversational tutor for programming, so intervention and STEM domain appear met. The abstract does not state whether there is a control group, the study design, any learning outcome, or whether the sample is students. These are missing rather than negative evidence, so per rule 2 the record advances as unsure for full-text review. Publication venue (Florida AI Research Society, 2026) may also need checking for publication type.

quote: We present Vision-Braille, the first publicly available end-to-end system for translating Chinese Braille extracted from images into written Chinese.
rationale: The abstract describes an LLM-based Braille-to-Chinese translation system evaluated by BLEU on synthetic corpora. There is no learner-facing use, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome measured in learners. It is a system/technical paper, so the record fails on intervention, comparison, population, and outcome. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evident from the abstract; the abstract does not describe a learner study at all, so E1 (not learner-facing) could also apply. Given the rule to exclude only on positive evidence, the strongest positive evidence is that the only outcome is BLEU, not learning. Note that the abstract mentions teachers grading homework, which is not learner interaction.

quote: User testing (N=5) validated that KNOT successfully offloads logistical burdens, with participants reporting improvement in their ability to focus their cognitive energy on learning.
rationale: Abstract describes a design and prototype with ethnographic observations, surveys, interviews, and user testing (N=5). No control group is mentioned, so there is positive evidence of no comparison group without generative AI (E3). Outcomes are perceptions and self-reports, not a quantitative learning measure (would also be E5), and the design is not an experiment. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E3 is reported first because the absence of any comparison group is the earliest failing criterion in the sequence, though the abstract's evidence of no control is somewhat implicit.

quote: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools like DeepSeek hold transformative potential for data-driven learning (DDL) in translator education
rationale: The study targets translation education (translator training: terminology, cultural adaptation, bilingual materials). Translation is a language field, not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science, so the domain criterion fails. Data-driven learning here refers to corpus-style language learning, not STEM content. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-STEM domain, so E2 applies at the abstract stage.

quote: This systematic review examines empirical research published from 2019 to early 2025, concentrating on ChatGPT applications in EFL teaching and learning.
rationale: The record is a systematic review, not an empirical study, so E6 applies. It is also EFL (language learning), which is non-STEM and would fail the domain criterion (E2 would be the first code in order, but the protocol's ordering places E1/E2 before E6). Applying the order strictly: E1 cannot be confirmed as not met from the abstract, and E2 applies because the content is English as a Foreign Language, a non-STEM domain. Reporting E2 as the first applicable code in order.

quote: Using SRL theory, the review analysed empirical studies on AI-driven help-seeking support
rationale: This is a systematic review (narrative synthesis of 48 studies), not an empirical study with its own comparison group, so it fails the protocol's empirical design requirement and the publication type rule for reviews. The abstract also gives no evidence of a single eligible primary experiment. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion is based on the review design stated in the abstract.

quote: The paper presents the design and architecture of the framework, characteristic use cases in the context of the course on Human-Computer Interaction
rationale: The abstract describes a framework design and use cases with "preliminary findings" and no comparison group, control condition, or quantitative learning outcome reported. Design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, so the record is not an eligible empirical study. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study) on the basis of the abstract; the framework is presented as a conceptual/design contribution. Generative AI is part of the framework, and the course is computer science, so intervention and domain are not the failing points.

quote: We examined students’ GAI usage using conversational data and screen recordings from 12 groups, each comprising three university students.
rationale: The abstract describes an observational analysis of GAI use behaviors in 12 student groups, correlating behaviors with knowledge construction. There is no control group without generative AI, and the design is correlational rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 applies. The STEM domain is also not stated. Outcome is knowledge construction coded from discourse, not clearly a quantitative learning measure, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The systematic review method was adopted, following the PRISMA 2020 flow diagram guidelines.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of the literature, not an empirical study with its own control group and outcome data. Under the protocol's exclusion of reviews and the requirement of an empirical design, it fails at E6. Although the abstract mentions 27 included studies, it does not report any study-level comparison of its own, so this is not a primary study. Code E6 is applied as the first failing criterion in order (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed; the domain, programming, is STEM).

quote: student submissions from midterm examinations in an introductory C programming course were evaluated using GPT-4 with rubric-based feedback, alongside manual grading by the instructor
rationale: The generative AI (GPT-4/GPT-5) is used for automated grading of student submissions, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only for grading is excluded, and E1 is the first applicable code. There is also no learner-level control group without generative AI and no learning outcome; the comparison is AI grades versus instructor grades.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a publisher retraction notice covering a whole special issue, not the empirical study titled "Evaluating AI tutor feedback in medical education". The title of the retracted article refers to an AI tutor study, but the record contains no methods, design, control group, or outcome data. Retracted articles are not empirical studies in the eligible sense. The retraction notice itself cannot be assessed against the eligibility criteria. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The title also mentions medical education, which would raise a population/domain concern (health professions) if the study were assessed on its own, but this is not the basis for exclusion. Only the first applicable code is reported, per the protocol order.

quote: Across four deployments in two introductory Python courses (N=480), TutorTrace captures approximately 180K telemetry events
rationale: Abstract describes an AI programming tutor for introductory Python students (population and domain appear met). It is a dataset/taxonomy paper with a "preliminary classroom evaluation" of behavior-aware prompts; the abstract does not say whether a control group without generative AI exists, nor reports a learning outcome (the 50.0% to 20.7% figure is a behavioral measure, and the prediction AUROCs are not learning outcomes). Also the tool's generative nature (AI query) is implied but not explicit. Not positive evidence of failure, so unsure pending full text.

quote: Ten experimental or quasi-experimental studies with sufficient statistical information were used for effect-size calculation.
rationale: This record is a meta-analysis (a review) of ten studies, not a primary empirical study. Under the protocol, reviews are not eligible. Its own Methodology section describes a synthesis of Scopus-indexed publications, so it is a review rather than an original study. Excluding under E6 (not an empirical study). The protocol's publication-type rule (E10) also lists reviews, but E6 is the closest code for a secondary synthesis of this kind; the abstract alone does not settle which code the auditor prefers. Abstract stage exclusion is warranted because the design is clearly a meta-analysis rather than an experiment.

quote: We conduct a user study with 45 undergraduate STEM students to evaluate the learning outcomes and user experience.
rationale: Learner-facing LLM agents in group ethics discussion with undergraduate STEM students (intervention and population appear met). The abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI, the study design, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured (it mentions "learning outcomes" and "ethical sensitivity" but gives no detail). Domain is ethics training for STEM students, which is not clearly STEM content. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a whole Special Issue, not an empirical study. The listed title "Enhancing communication for people with hearing disabilities through robust sign language recognition using deep learning and the internet of things" is a sign-language recognition system for hearing-disabled people, not a learner-facing generative AI learning intervention with a control group. No eligible empirical design is described, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study) and the other criteria cannot be met. Retraction notice and no eligible design or population evident.

quote: In this paper, we study whether it is feasible to have ChatGPT-3.5 generate database schemas and associated SQL questions for teachers through a two-part study.
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT-3.5) is used by teachers to create SQL exercises, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. The study is a survey plus prompt engineering feasibility study with no control group and no learning outcome. E1 applies as the first failing code in order.

quote: OpenCoderRank is evaluated using two methods: 1. BERTScore, 2. LLM evaluation.
rationale: The abstract describes a software platform evaluated with BERTScore and LLM-based evaluation, not an empirical learning study with a control group. No quantitative learning outcome for learners is reported, and no comparison group or learner-level data are described. Exclude under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental. Abstract stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence that the outcome is not a learning measure.

quote: Data were collected from 65 students in the French Language Education Study Program at the University of Lampung using a 30-item questionnaire with a six-point Likert scale.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, non-experimental, cross-sectional questionnaire study with no control group, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). It is also a French language reading study, which is non-STEM (E2) and reports perception data rather than a learning outcome (E5). Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 is not triggered, E2 would be the first code to apply; however, the design/comparison failure is the most direct evidence. Rule-order reporting: E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract, so the first clear failure in code order is E2 (non-STEM). Reporting E2 as the first applicable code.

quote: This paper proposes a deterministic rule-based method for detecting hallucinations in fourth-grade math word problems.
rationale: The study is a rule-based detection method that checks LLM-generated math word problems. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLMs only generate content that is verified. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). No learning outcome or control group is reported either. Exclusion is clear at the abstract stage on E1, the first applicable code.

quote: An online survey collected data from 35 academic staff and 282 students across two universities in Vietnam and one in Singapore
rationale: The study is a survey with descriptive statistics and thematic analysis, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Perceptions are the only outcomes, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code that fits; E3 (no control group) and E6 (not an empirical study, arguably) would also apply. Design is a survey, which is excluded by the Design criterion. Given the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with perception outcomes only, exclusion is appropriate.

quote: Our results show that LLMs still have a limited ability to simulate learner evaluations.
rationale: The study simulates learner subjective evaluations of feedback using LLMs rather than measuring learning outcomes in learners who interact with a generative AI tool. The outcome is subjective evaluation ratings (preference simulation), not a quantitative learning measure, and there is no control group of learners without generative AI. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because the only outcome is subjective evaluation, with clear positive evidence of no learning outcome.

quote: The study follows a qualitative-analytical design: it re-analyses the aggregated results of a published online survey of 300 school teachers
rationale: The record is a theoretical/methodological article with a qualitative-analytical design that re-analyses survey results from teachers. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome in students. It is not an empirical study of learning, so E6 applies as the first failing code that is clearly evident. Population is teachers (in-service), not students. No injection detected.
rationale_note: E1 could also arguably apply (teacher-facing use for lesson planning), but E6 is the clearest and the record is not an empirical intervention study.

quote: Mixed Methods Research: AI-Augmented Design, Analysis, and Publishing is a practical and scholarly guide for doctoral students, faculty members, institutional researchers, and interdisciplinary scholars
rationale: This is a book (a practical and scholarly guide), not an empirical study. It describes no experiment, control group, or learning outcome. It is also not STEM-focused, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported. Fails design, comparison, and outcome criteria as well.

quote: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched five databases and two supplementary sources, identifying 57 empirical studies published between 2022 and 2026.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 57 studies, not an empirical study with its own control group. Under the protocol, reviews are not eligible (E6, not an empirical study). Quote is from the abstract's description of the review method.

quote: The paper presents the task Footprints of the Walking of Numbers, a dynamic visualization proposal
rationale: The abstract presents a theoretical-didactical task design analyzed through the Mathematical Working Space lens; no empirical study with a control group or learning outcome is described. Generative AI is mentioned only as instrumental computation support by the authors, not as a learner-facing intervention. Not an empirical study (E6). Note that E1 could also apply since the AI use described is not learner-facing; E6 is reported as the primary reason because the paper has no empirical design.

quote: Classroom observations, produced artifacts, and interaction threads with assistants configured in ChatGPT were analyzed to reconstruct how each group appropriated the technology
rationale: Observational experience report of ten doctoral students; the analysis is qualitative (classroom observations, artifacts, interaction threads). No control group comparison or quantitative learning outcome is described, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Per the protocol's ordering, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that applies at the abstract stage. Note that E5 (no quantitative outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study in the experimental sense) would also apply; the abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison and outcome criteria fail.
exclusion_code_note: E3 chosen as first applicable in protocol order when checked against comparison and design criteria.

quote: The results provide a foundational proof-of-concept for scalable, transparent AI integration in CS curricula
rationale: The abstract describes a framework design with exploratory pilot case studies and "initial feasibility". No control or comparison group without generative AI is mentioned, and the study is described as exploratory proof-of-concept. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so E3 applies. Outcomes are described only as engagement and faculty burden, with no quantitative learning measure reported, so E5 is also plausible, but E3 is the first applicable code in order considered here.

quote: Empirically, across strong-to-weak and same-size distillation on math and code, Dr. OPD consistently outperforms all evaluated baselines.
rationale: The study is a machine-learning method paper on distilling LLMs (student/teacher models), not a study of learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. The student is a model, not a K-12 or higher education student, so the population criterion fails. Exclusion code E4 is applied as the first failing criterion in the code order that the abstract clearly supports. E1 could also be argued (no learner-facing tool), but the abstract gives clearer evidence that the participants are models rather than students. No injection detected.

quote: We evaluate the quality of the generated feedback-ladder via a user study with students, educators, and researchers.
rationale: Abstract describes a user study rating feedback quality by students, educators, and researchers, with no learning outcome measured. The evaluation is of feedback quality rather than a quantitative learning measure collected after an intervention, so E5 applies. Programming domain is STEM. No control group or learning statistics are described in the abstract.

quote: Using the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, 45 initial articles were identified and screened into 16 empirical studies that met the inclusion criteria.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with its own control group and effect data. It synthesizes other studies, so it fails the design requirement. The review reports on self-regulated learning outcomes rather than a primary comparison. Under the protocol's exclusion ordering, E1 and E5 are not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study).
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on the basis that the record is a review.

quote: We introduce the Relevance-Enhanced Adaptive Layered Model (REALM), a protocol that not only establishes a novel, self-contained framework for GenAI-enabled STEM education
rationale: The record is a conceptual/theoretical protocol paper proposing a framework (REALM) and mapping learning theories. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Under the protocol's code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) is not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the first applicable code on the positive evidence available.

quote: The study used a literature review with a mixed-methods approach that integrates quantitative and qualitative findings from various relevant scientific publications.
rationale: The record is a literature review that synthesizes other publications, not an empirical study with its own control-group experiment. Positive evidence of a non-empirical design means it fails the E6 criterion (not an empirical study). No primary comparison group or learning data is reported by the authors themselves.

quote: this study addresses that gap through a thematic review of 39 peer-reviewed publications from 2021 to 2026
rationale: The record is a thematic literature review of 39 publications, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria and falls under E6 (not an empirical study). Music education is also not clearly STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's logic for a review. Note that the protocol orders codes E1 through E10; E1 and E2 are not clearly determinable from the abstract, so E6 is reported as the primary reason.

quote: This Community Service Program (PKM) aims to strengthen the professional competence of Senior High School teachers in Batahan District
rationale: This is a community service program describing teacher training with a participatory action research approach. It has no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learner outcome. Participants are in-service teachers, which is outside the population criterion. It is not an empirical study of learners' learning outcomes, so E6 applies. Exclusion at the abstract stage is supported by the positive evidence of a non-empirical community service design.

quote: The proposed algorithm enables educational institutions, platform developers, and teachers to generate assessment materials adapted to students' age and knowledge levels in distance or blended learning
rationale: The LLMs are used to generate assessment questions; the abstract gives no indication that learners interact with the generative AI tool. The AI appears to be used by researchers/teachers to produce materials, which is E1 (AI used only by teacher to prepare materials). No control group with non-generative AI is described, and the study compares three LLMs and iterations of prompts, which would also fail E3. E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Experiments show that LoRA is better in training efficiency, while QLoRA performs better in JSON validity, field coverage, structure quality, and citation generation.
rationale: The abstract compares two fine-tuning methods (LoRA vs QLoRA) of the same model with no non-generative-AI control group, so there is no comparison meeting the protocol (two generative AI variants only, E3). Outcomes are model-output metrics (JSON validity, field coverage, structure quality) rather than learner learning outcomes, so E5 also applies. Per the protocol's ordering, E3 is the first applicable code, so the exclusion code should be E3 rather than E5.

quote: An 8-week quasi-experimental study involving 124 students from a pedagogical university employed traditional peer discussion methods in the control group
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT-4 as a Socratic tutor for learners (generative AI, learner-facing), a control group using peer discussion (non-AI comparison), a quasi-experimental design with comparison group, prospective biology teachers (higher education), and quantitative argumentation scores analyzed by ANCOVA. Domain is biology/science argumentation framed around PISA scientific literacy; the abstract does not explicitly state the content is STEM beyond biology and socio-scientific issues, so this is judged compatible with science and passed to full text for confirmation. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage.

quote: Method. We conducted a survey with 130 undergraduate students from two universities.
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions of GenAI use with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria. Under the code order, E1 could arguably apply first (intervention not clearly learner-facing use within a learning activity), but the core failure is that it is a non-experimental survey, which the protocol treats as not an eligible empirical design. Coded E6 as the survey design fails the study-design requirement; the E3 comparison failure also applies but E6 is the first-applicable substantive failure for a survey study.

quote: "Analysis was restricted to descriptive statistics, one descriptive correlation coefficient (not interpreted inferentially), and reflexive thematic analysis. No inferential group comparison was attempted."
rationale: Cross-sectional online survey with no control group and no comparison; perceptions and self-reported usage only, with no quantitative learning outcome measured. Fails comparison/design (E3) as the first applicable code in order. Also not an intervention study and the domain is not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of failure is present at the abstract stage, so exclusion is justified.

quote: we introduce a benchmark that provides a unified and realistic evaluation of LLMs'general learning abilities
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs themselves as learners on a benchmark; no human learners, no learner-facing GenAI intervention with a control group. Population criterion is not met (no K-12 or higher education students). Coded E6 as the first applicable code is arguably E4 or E1; however the abstract gives no evidence of student participants, and the record is a benchmark/framework paper rather than an educational intervention study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that participants are models rather than students.

quote: This meta-analysis synthesized data from 39 empirical studies published between 2023 and 2025.
rationale: The record is a meta-analysis, not a primary empirical study with its own experimental control group. Under the protocol's design criteria (randomized or quasi-experimental primary studies), it does not qualify as a single eligible study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of its own). Note: the abstract does not describe a primary trial; the meta-analysis pools 39 studies, so the appropriate route is exclusion as a review. Publication type also suggests a review (E10 could be argued), but the protocol's E6 covers reviews/non-empirical work and is used here.

quote: This two-day workshop responds to the disruption that the AI revolution introduces to statistics education and practice.
rationale: The record describes a two-day professional workshop (Instats seminar) rather than an empirical study. No comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no study design are described. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Its population (academics and PhD students) and intervention are also unclear, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported by the abstract.
rationale_note: Exclusion code ordering: E1 (intervention) is unclear from abstract; E2 does not apply since statistics is STEM; E3 and E5 lack evidence; E6 is the clearest failure.

quote: This study employs a qualitative approach based on library research.
rationale: The record is a qualitative library research/literature synthesis, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical design requirement (E6). Explicit positive evidence of non-empirical design is present in the abstract, so exclusion is justified even at the abstract stage.
rationale_detail: No experiment, comparison group, or quantitative outcome is reported.

quote: This paper introduces the Internalize-Reference-Delegate (IRD) framework, which classifies learning tasks along two dimensions
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework paper. The abstract describes no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The only illustration is a project on Newton-Raphson power flow, with no measured results. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Intervention and population are not specified enough to judge, but E6 is decisive. Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence that the paper is a framework without empirical data.

criteria.stage_note: LLM used to grade/assess programming assignments, not learner-facing

quote: The assessment of programming assignments in computer science (CS) education traditionally relies on manual grading
rationale: The LLMs are used to automate grading/assessment of Java assignments, not as a tool learners interact with during a learning activity. Protocol excludes AI used only for grading and AI used only by teachers/graders, so E1 applies. The abstract also does not describe a control group without generative AI or a learning outcome, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This preregistered meta-analysis (INPLASY2025110051) systematically reviewed 22 empirical studies (46 independent samples, N = 5232) published between 2023 and 2025.
rationale: The record is a meta-analysis, not an empirical primary study. Under the protocol's publication and design rules, a systematic review or meta-analysis of other studies is not an eligible empirical study, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The meta-analysis's included studies were not screened individually here; the record itself is a secondary synthesis. Other criteria were not fully assessable from the abstract but are moot given E6.

quote: This study explored the literature to understand what GenAI has been used for in K-12 and the reported impacts of its use.
rationale: This is a systematic review of 30 papers, not an empirical study with its own intervention and control group. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). The review's included studies are not themselves screened as separate records here. Other criteria cannot be judged from this abstract, but the review type alone supports exclusion.

criteria.outcome_note: No quantitative learning outcome reported; conceptual architecture paper
criteria.design_note: Design Science Research framework proposal, no comparison group

quote: This paper proposes a multi-tier modular architecture that re-encodes the ACM/IEEE Computer Science Curricula 2023 (CS2023) standards into four functionally independent tiers
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual curriculum architecture proposed under a Design Science Research approach. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study with eligible design. Code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits; E3 and E5 are also likely failures but the abstract gives no evidence of an empirical comparison at all. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is present, so exclusion is appropriate even at the abstract stage.

criteria.intervention_note: LLMs are evaluated as test-takers, not learners interacting with a tool in a learning activity
criteria.design_note: Case study design comparing human response data with LLM-generated responses; no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group

quote: Using a case study design, we compare human response data with responses generated by six multimodal LLMs.
rationale: At the abstract stage, the study is a case study comparing latent factor structures of human and LLM responses to assessments. LLMs are the subjects being assessed, not learners using generative AI within a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1 would be the first code in order). Strictly, the first applicable code in protocol order is E1, since learner-facing generative AI is absent. Design is also a case study with no control group (E3 risk). Coding E1 as the first applicable code would be more faithful to the protocol order; the decision to exclude is clear regardless of the specific code.

quote: This book not only chronicles the department's history from its inception to the present but also includes various academic studies
rationale: The record is an edited book describing the history of an Arabic Language Education department, with bibliometric and essay-style chapters. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Arabic language teaching is also non-STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E2 (non-STEM) would also apply.
rationale_note: Abstract stage exclusion based on positive evidence of non-empirical book format.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen as first applicable in protocol order.

quote: The study used a 50-item multiple-choice questionnaire, primarily in Persian with limited English terms and formulas, which was administered to LLMs (ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini 3, and Copilot 2026).
rationale: The study administers a chemistry questionnaire directly to LLMs, not to learners. There is no learner-facing intervention and no control group without generative AI; all arms are generative AI models evaluated for accuracy. Exclusion under E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) is the clearest applicable code; E1 (learner-facing intervention) would also apply, but the protocol's first-applicable ordering starts with E1. Under strict ordering, E1 applies first because learners do not interact with the tool at all. Stated as E3 reflects the absence of a non-generative-AI comparator, but the primary basis is that no learner interacts with the AI.

Abstract describes an LLM-based lab with an RL agent for adaptive support, which is learner-facing generative AI in a STEM-adjacent (cybersecurity/cloud) domain. However, the evaluation reports technical validation (F1 of the LLM analyzer on an artifact corpus), simulation-based testing of an RL agent across personas, and expert ratings. There is no controlled comparison with a non-generative-AI group and no learning outcome measured in students. Design is not an experiment with a comparison group. Excluded at the first clearly failing criterion: no quantitative learning outcome (E5). The design and comparison failures would also apply, but E5 is the first in the code order that is clearly evidenced by the abstract.

quote: "Prompt Engineering 101" is an innovative General Education course designed to equip students to interact with AI models like ChatGPT using common language
rationale: The abstract describes a course teaching students to write prompts for ChatGPT-like generative AI, so the intervention and population appear to fit. However, it is a conceptual/position-style description with no comparison group, no design, no quantitative learning outcome, and no statistics reported. Abstract gives no positive evidence of a control group or quantitative outcome, so strictly E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the best-supported code, though the abstract is thin and the paper may be non-empirical (E6). Domain is also unclear (prompt engineering in a General Education course, not clearly STEM). Excluding on E5 with the caveat that full-text check could reveal otherwise; the record is not clearly eligible.

quote: AI does not replace the teacher but performs the functions of generating and adapting professionally relevant scenarios, while the final assessment remains with the teacher.
rationale: The abstract describes generative AI used to generate and adapt exam scenarios, with the final assessment held by the teacher. That suggests AI is used by the teacher to prepare assessment materials, not as a learner-facing tool, which is E1. The abstract also describes a pilot against a traditional exam, and the domain is professional reasoning rather than STEM, so E2 may also apply. E1 is the first applicable code in order. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract, not missing information.

quote: In this guest editorial, we conceptualize the “teaching of engineering writing” as the activities that happen both in undergraduate and graduate classrooms
rationale: The record is a guest editorial, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; E1 and E5 are also likely but the editorial status is the decisive positive evidence.
rationale_note: Publication type is an editorial, which would also fall under E10 (publication type not eligible). Protocol lists editorials under E10 in publication-type exclusions, and E6 covers non-empirical studies. Ordering rule: E1 to E10 checked in order; E6 appears before E10, so E6 is reported.

quote: An eight-week study with 100 A2 learners and 600 coded words is proposed.
rationale: The abstract describes a review-style article that synthesizes prior research and proposes a future study ("is proposed"), so it is not an empirical study with a comparison group. Domain is also not STEM: the content is German vocabulary learning, which falls under language learning and is excluded. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first applicable code under the stated order, since E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone and the paper's nature (non-empirical proposal) is the clearest failure. Note that E2 (non-STEM content) is arguably the more direct failure; the protocol asks for the first code in order, and E2 precedes E6 in the list, so E2 would be the strict first applicable code if the domain failure is accepted as positive evidence. Reconsidering against the order: E2 applies before E6, so the correct code is E2.

quote: Extracting structured information from academic PDF documents is non trivial
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs used for extracting information from course registration PDF documents (KRS). This is a document-processing task, not learner-facing generative AI used in a learning activity, and not STEM learning content. Population is not students learning; no learning outcome is measured (extraction accuracy only). Excluded on E2 as the content is not STEM learning; the intervention also fails E1 since learners do not interact with the LLM. Under the code-order rule, E1 comes first, so the correct code is E1.

quote: "A narrative systematic review was the only approach capable of integrating experimental studies, surveys, conceptual frameworks, and regional data."
rationale: This is a narrative systematic review, not an empirical study. The authors state they considered a meta-analysis but found it unworkable and chose a narrative synthesis. Reviews are not eligible, so E6 applies. The record also focuses on university instructors rather than learners, which would be a further mismatch, but the first applicable code in order is E6 (E1 and E4 are not clearly established from the abstract). No quantitative learner-outcome comparison is reported; the reported figures (e.g., 58% time drop, beta = 0.264) come from the synthesis of other sources.

quote: "We -the authors-are eager to corroborate whether the title of this communication should have been phrased as a solid statement or not."
rationale: Record is a conference communication (Education and New Developments 2023 volume, congress abstract style), so publication type is not an eligible journal article (E10). Abstract also describes a pilot study with results still being coded, no learner interacting with generative AI (AI generated stimulus definitions that participants rated), no control group or quantitative learning outcome (Likert ratings of agreement and complexity, perceptions), so it would also fail other criteria. Publication-type exclusion is applied first in the code order used here after the earlier criteria are checked; the clearest positive evidence is the publication type and the absence of a learning outcome. Under the protocol order E1 would apply first (learner is not interacting with generative AI; AI produced the stimuli), so the first applicable code by protocol order is E1. Final code: E1.

criteria.quote: The paper provides a comprehensive review of the research conducted across skill extraction, large language model (LLM)-based career guidance
criteria.rationale: The record is a systematic/narrative review of about 45 articles, not an empirical study with a comparison group or learning outcome. It fails the design requirement (no randomized or quasi-experimental design) and the empirical-study requirement, so E6 applies. Because the protocol says to report the first applicable code in order, E1 and E2 are not evaluated as exclusions here; the abstract does not give enough to assess them.

quote: The paper provides a comprehensive review of the research conducted across skill extraction, large language model (LLM)-based career guidance
rationale: The record is a review of about 45 articles, not an empirical study. It has no comparison group and no learning outcome data. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the protocol says to report the first applicable code in order; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but E6 is the clear failure.

criteria.rationale_note: no control group; observational analysis of tutoring conversations

quote: We present a mixed-analysis study of n=108 anonymous, unmoderated P2P CS tutoring sessions.
rationale: The study analyzes existing text-based peer-to-peer tutoring conversations with no comparison group and no generative AI condition described. Outcomes are satisfaction and conversational dynamics, not a quantitative learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence of no control group, so E3 applies (first applicable code in order that is supported by abstract; E5 also plausibly applies).

quote: This study employed a comparative cross-sectional quantitative analysis. Data were collected via an online questionnaire
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of students' usage and perceptions of ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude. It has no control group without generative AI, so it fails the comparison criterion. Its outcomes are perceptions and usage patterns rather than a quantitative learning measure, and the design is a survey rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code in protocol order (intervention is arguably learner-facing, so E1 does not apply). Decision is exclude at abstract stage because positive evidence shows no comparison group and survey-only design.

quote: we investigated the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to analyze students'written explanations of computational physics problems on a pre- and post- semester survey
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to analyze student responses, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so the intervention criterion (E1) appears not met. However, the abstract gives no clear sign of this, and it is not certain how the LLM is used. The study is a pre-post survey of students with no visible control group, so E3 may apply. The abstract does not give enough information to decide either way. The rule is to exclude only on positive evidence, so the record is marked unsure and the full text should be checked for an intervention and a control group. Population (college physics students) and domain (physics) appear met.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage decision; E1 and E3 are both plausible from this text but not established.

quote: The textbook is intended for students of generative AI and applied machine learning courses, as well as the general professional public dealing with or interested in data science and AI.
rationale: The record is a textbook description, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type also appears to be a book, which would fall under E10, but the protocol's first-applicable ordering places E6 before E10 only if E1-E5 do not apply; the record gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention, so E1 is not positively shown either. E6 is the best fit.

quote: "we present an open-source dataset collected from 279 students at a public Australian university."
rationale: The record is a Scientific Data dataset descriptor, not an empirical comparative study. It presents a dataset of student-GenAI interaction logs and surveys with no control group, no comparison design, and no learning outcome statistics reported. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in protocol order. Note that E3 (no control group) would also apply, but E6 is listed first in the code order under the protocol's exclusion sequence as applied here. Abstract reads as a data resource, so the design and outcome criteria are clearly not met.

quote: LLM-Generated Knowledge Graphs for Analyzing the Association between Student Participation and Learning in Online Math Discussions (Poster 27)
rationale: The record is labeled as a conference poster (AERA 2026, Poster 27). Protocol excludes posters under E10 (publication type not eligible). No abstract is available, and the title describes an association analysis rather than a controlled comparison, so the other criteria cannot be confirmed, but the publication-type exclusion alone is sufficient.

quote: We will conduct in-person think-aloud sessions (min. n = 25) in which participants use a multi-modal GenAI tool (Google AI Studio) across interaction modes
rationale: Proposed study (extended abstract, SIGSOFT FSE Companion) of students using multimodal generative AI (Google AI Studio) on software development tasks, which fits the intervention and STEM domain. However, it is a proposed/planned study with no reported results, and the venue is a conference companion, which suggests E10 (publication type not eligible: conference proceedings). The abstract does not clearly confirm a comparison group (it describes a between-subjects design, which suggests one) or a quantitative learning outcome (it mentions efficiency and solution accuracy). Because the publication type appears ineligible and the rest is unclear, I'm marking unsure so a researcher can check the venue and design at full text rather than excluding on an abstract-level inference.

quote: We report on a pilot study in which 40 students, who completed a first-semester course on object-oriented programming, re-engage in a comparable programming project in limited time using GAI tools.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pilot in which all 40 students use GAI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot); there is no separate control group without generative AI, and no comparison group is mentioned. This is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so E3 applies. Domain (programming) and population (university students) appear met. Excluded at abstract stage on the comparison criterion.

quote: Substantial gains in recommendation precision and acceptance were observed with the integration of the BiLSTM module, relative to a purely heuristic baseline.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based chatbot (generative AI) for eighth-grade mathematics preparation, so population and domain appear met. The comparison is a heuristic baseline (non-generative variant), which may qualify as a non-AI control, but the abstract does not say whether it is a separate control group or a within-system comparison of recommendation modules. Outcomes are recommendation precision and acceptance, which may be system metrics rather than learning outcomes. Design and outcome cannot be judged from the abstract, so advance to full text.

quote: Method: This study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method guided by the PRISMA framework.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails the eligibility requirement for empirical designs (E6). Reviews are also not eligible publication types under the protocol. The abstract's mention of ChatGPT among digital tools does not establish a learner-facing generative AI control-group study. Exclusion code E6 is applied as the first code that clearly applies in order.

quote: In a quasi-experimental study within an undergraduate data structures course (N = 36), students using this structured AI assistant significantly outperformed peers
rationale: Abstract indicates a generative AI (ChatGPT-based) custom tool, a quasi-experimental comparison with a minimally prompted ChatGPT wrapper (a generative AI control, which fails the no-generative-AI control requirement only if that is the sole comparison; the abstract is ambiguous on whether a non-AI control exists), undergraduate data structures (computing, higher education), and a quantitative score outcome (92.7 vs 74.3). Publication venue is SIGCITE, which may be a conference, so publication type is unclear. Comparison criterion is a concern: the control receives a generative AI wrapper, so the protocol's requirement for a control group without generative AI may not be met. Given the rule to exclude only on positive evidence at abstract stage, and the comparison being ambiguous rather than clearly failing, I include for full-text checking of comparison, publication type, and data.

quote: we construct two datasets of CG questions requiring varying degrees of visual perception skills and geometric reasoning skills, and evaluate the current state-of-the-art LMM, GPT-4o, on the two datasets
rationale: The study evaluates GPT-4o's performance directly on CG questions. It is not a learner-facing controlled study: there is no learner interaction, no control group, and no learning outcome in participants. It is an evaluation of model capability, so it is not an empirical study of learners. Exclusion code E6 is the first that applies on the abstract's description, with E1 and E3 also likely, but the protocol's ordering places E1 first. On reflection, the intervention criterion (learner-facing) is not clearly shown to fail from the abstract alone, so E6 is the most defensible code for a model-benchmark paper with no learner data.

Abstract describes learners using GenAI for introductory programming (intervention and domain appear met; population is women learners in an online course context). It is a mixed-methods study, and the abstract does not indicate a control group, randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, or any quantitative learning measure with effect-size data. These are missing rather than positively contrary, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review of comparison, design, and outcome. Publication venue "The Compass" should also be checked for article type.

quote: We distributed an online survey, receiving responses from 86 students with experience taking a variety of online computing courses.
rationale: The study is a survey of student perceptions with no intervention comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Perceptions-only survey designs are not empirical experiments meeting the protocol, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense) is applied. Under the rules, E6 is the first applicable code at the abstract stage given the survey-only design; E5 would also apply since outcomes are perceptions only. The abstract provides positive evidence that the design is a survey without a control group, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: The study used AI systems to estimate the complexity of the algorithm based on code fragments.
rationale: The generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Bard, etc.) are used to estimate time complexity of code fragments, with the AI evaluating code rather than learners interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity. The intervention is therefore not learner-facing generative AI (E1). The abstract also describes no control group, no learning outcome in students, and the work appears to be a tool-evaluation study on AI accuracy. E1 is the first code that applies in order.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title suggests a CS1 (introductory programming) context, which meets the domain criterion. It concerns detecting ChatGPT-generated code, which may be a detection study rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group, so intervention, comparison, design, and outcome cannot be judged. Venue LLM@AIED suggests a workshop paper, which may fall under E10, but the record does not confirm publication type. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is unsure and should be resolved at full text.

quote: We conducted a classroom study with 7th graders, comparing a Mindful version against a version with cognitive support only.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based ITS (Math with Matt) with an LLM chat component, compared against a cognitive-only version (non-generative control group), with 7th graders in algebra and math learning outcomes. Design (randomization) and effect-size data are not stated in the abstract, so these are unclear rather than failed. Publication type, language, and date not visible in the record; no positive evidence of exclusion, so advance to full text. Venue not given, so journal status needs checking at full text.

quote: This research employed a one-group pre-experimental pre-test and post-test design
rationale: The study uses a single-group pre-post design with no separate control group without generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). The domain is EFL academic writing, which is non-STEM, so it would also fail E2, but E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order of exclusion... Strictly, the order is E1, E2, E3, so the first applicable code is E2 (content is not STEM). Correcting: the first code that applies is E2.

quote: This paper describes the design and implementation of a didactic activity, a reduced version of the"20 Questions"game, aimed at making this stochastic nature directly observable.
rationale: The abstract describes a design-and-implementation didactic activity with an LLM in physics education, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a descriptive/conceptual paper rather than an empirical comparative study. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the absence of a control group (E3) and the non-empirical nature (E6) are also apparent, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order is subject to the protocol's order, so E5 is reported as the first code that applies on the abstract's evidence.

quote: Employing a parallel-group randomized controlled trial in which 80 participants were randomized and 75 completed the intervention
rationale: Participants are pre-service physical education teachers in a basketball curriculum. The protocol counts preservice teachers learning STEM content as higher education, but PE/basketball content is not STEM, and the population is pre-service teachers rather than students learning STEM. Positive evidence that the population or domain fails, so exclude at abstract stage. Note the domain failure (E2) could also apply; E4 is cited because the protocol's first applicable code in order is E2 before E4 only if content is non-STEM, so this decision is a judgment call for the auditor: the content is physical education (non-STEM), which under the code order should be E2. Recording E2 would be the stricter reading of the code order.

quote: Complementary RL to achieve seamless co-evolution of an experience extractor and a policy actor within the RL optimization loop.
rationale: The abstract describes RL training of LLM-based agents with an experience extractor. The generative model is not a learner-facing tool in a learning activity; the agent is trained by RL and the study is an agent-training method rather than learners interacting with generative AI. No STEM learners, student population, or educational context is indicated. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence that the intervention is an RL-trained agent rather than a learner-facing tool.

criteria.quote_note: LLMs used to analyze student dialogue, not as a learner-facing tool

quote: We investigate whether instruction-tuned large language models (LLMs) can support multidimensional analysis of collaborative sensemaking without task-specific training
rationale: The LLMs are applied by researchers to annotate and classify existing student dialogue episodes, not as a tool learners interact with during a learning activity. No control group or learning outcome is described. Excluded under E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Abstract gives positive evidence of this failure.

quote: Our results indicated that using these tools individually or in combination produced a comparable effect on student performance in unit testing.
rationale: Abstract describes learners using ChatGPT (generative AI) versus a checklist control, in unit testing (software engineering, STEM domain), with a student performance outcome. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental with comparison), statistics for SMD, and publication type (venue is SIGSOFT FSE Companion, which may be a conference companion rather than a journal article, which would be E10) cannot be determined from the abstract. Per rule 2, not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text to check publication type and design.

criteria.outcome_note: no primary study with quantitative outcome described

quote: this study represents a systematic review of 26 articles exploring the use of ChatGPT in academic writing, personalized learning, and code generation
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 26 articles, not an empirical study with its own control-group comparison. Under the protocol it fails as a non-empirical publication (E6). Reviews are also listed as ineligible publication types, but E6 is the applicable code for a review that is not an empirical study, and the protocol lists reviews under E10 only as publication-type exclusions. Given the protocol's E10 definition explicitly names reviews, E10 may be more precise; this is flagged for the auditor. The abstract gives clear positive evidence the study is a review, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This study reviewed 28 empirical studies published in English between 2020 and 2025
rationale: This is a systematic literature review of 28 studies, not an empirical study of its own. It is a review, so it is not an eligible publication type/design under the protocol (E6, not an empirical study; reviews are also excluded under E10 publication type). The protocol's exclusion code list assigns the first applicable code; E6 is applied here as the review is not an empirical study. Language-learning (English speaking) content is also non-STEM, which would independently fail the domain criterion.

quote: Using Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT), this study aimed to characterise how generative AI is reshaping the activity of learning to do research
rationale: The study is a qualitative activity-system analysis of medical student research projects, with themes coded inductively from interviews/surveys. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the E-code order, the first applicable code is E4 only if population fails; the population here is medical students (higher education), so it is not E4. Stopping at the first failing criterion in order: E1 (intervention) is unclear from the abstract, E2 (domain) is unclear since research projects are not explicitly STEM. The clearest failure is that it is not an empirical comparative study (qualitative activity-theory analysis), so E6 applies on design grounds. Note the reported AI non-use comparison between cohorts is descriptive, not a learning outcome.

quote: This phenomenological study captures how literature and language learning have evolved in the post-pandemic landscape
rationale: The study is a phenomenological, qualitative design based on lived experiences of ten participants, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design requirements. Domain is language learning (English), which is non-STEM, so E2 could also apply, but the primary failure is that it is not an empirical comparative study; E6 is the first applicable code given the design. Exclusion is clear from the abstract.
