rationale: The study is an AutoML framework in which an LLM evolves scikit-learn pipeline code, evaluated on 68 OpenML classification tasks. It is not a learning activity with learners interacting with generative AI; no students or educational population are involved. The protocol's population criterion (K-12 or higher education students) is not met, and the content is tabular ML pipeline search rather than a STEM learning domain. The first applicable code in order is E2 as the closest code, though E1 (not learner-facing) and E4 (population) also apply; the abstract gives clear evidence that the study is not a learner-facing STEM education study.

quote: This study aims to systematically synthesize scholarly findings on the impact of integrating generative AI into the cognitive structure of learning in ITE through a systematic literature review approach.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study. It has no primary control-group experiment, so it fails the protocol's design requirement and the E6 (not an empirical study) code applies. Publication type also reads as a review, which would fall under E10, but E6 is the first applicable code for a review that is not an empirical study.

The record is a conceptual/framework article ("we argue", "we propose a practical framework") illustrated with an example. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that E6 precedes E3 and E5 in the code order only in the sense that it is the first applicable code here as an empirical-study failure; the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: To the editor, With the rapid evolution of scientific literature and technology, experts rely more on new artificial intelligence models
rationale: The record is a letter to the editor offering commentary on ChatGPT in medical education and research. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the text itself, not missing information.

The abstract describes a perspective or position piece on using generative AI to create physics simulations for education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design criterion and is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of non-empirical nature in the abstract.

Abstract is absent from the index; only title, venue, and year are available. The title indicates LLM-generated feedback in real classes, which suggests a generative AI intervention, but the title emphasizes student and instructor perspectives, which hints at perception-based outcomes that would fail the outcome criterion. Comparison, design, domain, and learning outcomes cannot be judged from the record. No positive evidence of exclusion is present, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: The participants were 34 students divided into two groups: an experimental group that utilized ChatGPT during four English reading sessions and a control group that received traditional teacher-led instruction without AI intervention.
rationale: Content is English reading (EFL), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. The first failing criterion in code order is E2 (content not STEM). Outcomes are self-efficacy and AI use motivation, which are affective/perception measures and would also fail the outcome criterion, but E2 is reported first. Abstract gives clear positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: We find that student opinions toward LLMs vary, with generally favorable perceptions of their capabilities but greater skepticism regarding their value for learning.
rationale: The abstract reports only perceptions, self-reported usage, and attitudes about LLMs among first-year physics students, with no quantitative learning measure. The study is about perceptions, which the protocol excludes as an outcome (E5). Intervention, comparison, and design are not clearly described in the abstract, but the outcome failure is sufficient for exclusion. Quote is taken from the abstract.

quote: Seven students attended the course, five used the tutor, and three groups produced a final report.
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory qualitative case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it fails the design criterion and the comparison criterion; the outcome is also not quantitative. Per the protocol's exclusion code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. Intervention (GenAI tutor), domain (astrophysics lab), and population (Master's students) appear to be met.

quote: This chapter applies text mining to publications indexed in a leading academic database to map scholarly discourse on ChatGPT in programming education.
rationale: The record is a book chapter applying text mining to published literature on ChatGPT in programming education. It is not an empirical learner study: it has no intervention, control group, or learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, E6 (not an empirical study) applies. It is a bibliometric/literature analysis rather than primary research, so it fails the design and outcome criteria as well.

quote: Gray Box testing showed that all flows operated as designed
rationale: The study is a system development paper evaluated with gray box functional testing. The abstract reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only system functionality is described. Exclusion E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). The abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Note that E3 (no control group) would also plausibly apply; E5 is listed first in the protocol order only if E1-E4 do not apply, and E1 does not apply since the chatbot is learner-facing generative AI (Gemini RAG). Under the code order, E3 precedes E5 when a control group is absent; the abstract does not explicitly show absence of a control group, so E5 is reported on the strongest positive evidence.

quote: The study highlights the need for a thoughtful approach to navigating the benefits and risks of generative AI in education.
rationale: The abstract describes a perception/discussion piece about teachers and generative AI in higher education. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a non-empirical discussion paper, so E6 applies (E6 precedes E3 and E5 in the code order). Title refers to teacher perceptions, which would also fail the population and outcome criteria. The abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: pre- and post-intervention measures of statistical learning (AASCDM), AI literacy (MAILS), and critical thinking (WGCTA)
rationale: The abstract describes a Design-Based Research pilot with N = 14 and pre-post measures only, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. This is a single-group pre-post design, so E3 applies. Intervention (ChatGPT as thinking partner), STEM content (statistics), and undergraduate population fit the protocol, and the outcomes are quantitative.

quote: Using exploratory comparative documentary analysis, public central guidance from 12 universities was theoretically sampled
rationale: The study is a documentary analysis of university policy documents, not an empirical learner-facing intervention study. It has no learner interaction with generative AI, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study) in the sense of an empirical trial; the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since no learners interact with a GenAI tool. Coding E1 as the first applicable code under protocol order would be appropriate, but the protocol says to report the first that applies in order. Checking in order: E1 applies because the intervention is policy governance text, not learner-facing GenAI.

quote: we benchmark language models for programming feedback generation across several performance criteria, including quality, cost, time, and data privacy
rationale: The paper benchmarks language models for generating programming feedback across quality, cost, time and privacy. It is a model benchmarking study with no learner-facing comparison group and no learning outcome measured in learners. Abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome (outcomes are model quality, cost, time, privacy). Excluded under E5. Note the venue is NeurIPS, which may also raise publication-type concerns, but the abstract does not establish that alone.

quote: Generative AI as a Conditional Facilitator of Student Self‐Directed Learning: Insights From Health Sciences Education
rationale: The title places the study in health sciences education, which the protocol excludes as health professions education (domain not STEM). No abstract is available. The title gives positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so exclude at abstract stage under E2. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone.

The record has only a title, venue (iTextbooks@AIED, 2025), and year. There is no abstract. The title suggests AI-enhanced texts and learning gains, which could involve a generative AI component, a control group, and a learning outcome, but none of this can be verified. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is not excluded. Venue is a workshop/conference-type series, which may raise a publication-type question (E10) that should be checked at full text. Advance to full text to check intervention, comparison, design, population, domain, outcome, and publication type.

quote: The main aim of the article is to investigate how translation students interact with AI-generated translations
rationale: Content is translation/translation studies (language learning and other non-STEM content), not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science. Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code in order is E1 (generative AI is learner-facing here, so E1 does not apply), then E2. The abstract also gives no sign of STEM content.

Record is a bioRxiv preprint about a computational predictor of antibody-interacting residues from protein sequence. It is not a journal article (publication type ineligible, E10). It is also not an educational study: there is no learner-facing generative AI, no learning population, and no learning outcome. No abstract is available. Excluded on the preprint publication type; the domain (bioinformatics, not STEM education) would also fail.

quote: Journal of Education and Training Studies (JETS) would like to acknowledge the following reviewers for their assistance with peer review of manuscripts for this issue.
rationale: The record is a reviewer acknowledgements listing for a journal issue, not a research study. It describes no intervention, comparison group, or learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). It is also not a journal article reporting research. Excluded at abstract stage on the basis of positive evidence that it is not an empirical study.

quote: students ... were asked to retrospectively and anonymously self-report their GenAI-related behaviors and attitudes
rationale: Survey-based self-report study of students' GenAI behaviors and attitudes on reflective writing assignments. There is no control group and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome is measured; perceptions and self-reported usage only. Exclusion code is E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in order, though E5 and E6 (survey/non-empirical-experimental design) would also apply. Health sciences context also raises domain concerns. Decision is clear at abstract stage on the comparison/design criteria.

quote: This paper presents a case study, a six-week design project carried out in an undergraduate industrial design programme
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of a design project producing conceptual designs. It is not an empirical comparison study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study), as the record is a descriptive case study/design paper. Domain and population are also unclear, but the first applicable code is E6.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of a case study with conceptual outputs and no comparison group.

quote: Using the Qwen3 family, we discover a counter-intuitive phenomenon: reasoning can be effectively incentivized by an extremely small fraction of generated tokens
rationale: The study concerns post-training of LLMs via on-policy distillation and RLVR, where the training signal is applied to model parameters. It does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). No human learners, control groups, or learning outcomes in the sense of the protocol are described. Exclusion is on E1, the first applicable code in order.

quote: Ethical acceptance was measured on Likert scales by three items
rationale: The study is a correlational survey of students' ethical perceptions (Spearman correlations between programming grade and Likert ethics items). It has no control group, no generative AI intervention given to learners, and no quantitative learning outcome; the measured outcome is an affective/attitudinal perception. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies; the design is also a survey rather than an experiment, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order for an attitude-only measure. Publication in 2026 is within the date window and the language is fine.

quote: A systematic review of the existing literature was conducted using the Web of Science database
rationale: This is a systematic review (topic modeling and sentiment analysis of 101 papers), not an empirical experimental study with a control group and learning outcome. It is not an empirical primary study, so E6 applies. Reviews are also ineligible under E10, but the protocol's first applicable code in order is E6 for a non-empirical record; no learning outcome or control group is reported, and the record does not meet the design criteria.

quote: Venue: SIGGRAPH Asia Technical Communications
rationale: Venue is SIGGRAPH Asia Technical Communications, a conference venue, so the publication type is not an eligible journal article (E10). The abstract also reports only a preliminary study with 17 novice teenage learners, with no described control group or quantitative learning outcome, so further exclusions would apply if the record were eligible. Exclusion is based on the publication type, which is positive evidence from the record.

quote: Our claim is narrower: prompt literacy describes a second-order inequality among users who have a baseline choice, while access describes a first-order inequality over whether that choice exists.
rationale: This record is a commentary/letter responding to an editorial (Qama [1]). It reports no empirical study, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. It is also health self-management rather than STEM education, which would further fail the domain criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly met.
rationale_short: Commentary on an editorial; no empirical study.

quote: This paper presents a dataset on digital citizenship among Indonesian prospective teachers enrolled in civic education programs.
rationale: The record is a data paper describing a survey dataset (2008 informants) on GenAI usage and digital citizenship among civic education pre-service teachers. It is not an experimental study: there is no control group, no learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome; the content is civic education, not STEM. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6, a dataset/descriptive survey), which is the most fitting code; the design also fails the comparison and outcome criteria.

quote: This is a methodology paper rather than an effectiveness study.
rationale: The abstract states this is a methodology paper, not an empirical effectiveness study. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical.

quote: We use an LLM as a teacher model to generate children's language based on prompt engineering with a beginner's dictionary and children's stories
rationale: The study is a framework for training a lightweight LLM to simplify text for children. Learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity; the LLM is used to produce simplified text, and no learner-facing comparison with a non-AI control group is described. The content is text simplification for children's comprehension, not STEM content. The abstract gives no clear evidence of a learner-facing intervention or a STEM domain, so the first failing criterion is the intervention (E1) since the model is not learner-facing. Note: the rule for abstract stage is to exclude only on positive evidence; the abstract clearly describes a model-development study with no learner interaction, which is positive evidence against the intervention. Domain is also non-STEM (language/reading comprehension).

decision_rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a batch of articles from a Special Issue, not an empirical study of generative AI in STEM learning. The abstract describes no intervention, comparison group, learner sample, or learning outcome. The record is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Note that the record title (Xiao, X., Choral harmony...) concerns collective singing and does not describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group, and the abstract itself lists unrelated topics (pension allocation, medical staff misconduct, schizophrenia MRI, etc.).
quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a publisher retraction notice listing many unrelated articles from a Special Issue; it reports no empirical study with a generative AI intervention, control group, STEM learning population, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The title-matched article (Xiao, X., 2025, Choral harmony) is a retracted paper about collective singing and does not show a generative AI learning intervention in the abstract. Injection not suspected.

quote: We applied 15 standardized student-use vignettes to the public policy environments of 20 Australian universities and produced 300 university-case classifications.
rationale: The study applies policy vignettes to university policy documents and classifies them; no learners interact with a generative AI tool, there is no control group, and no learning outcome is measured. It is a policy analysis, not an empirical learning study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense); E1 could also apply since no learner-facing GenAI is involved, but the first applicable code in order is E1. Correction: E1 applies first in order, so the code should be E1.

Abstract is not in the index, so there is no positive evidence that any criterion fails. Title indicates ChatGPT use by students learning programming (domain and intervention plausibly met). Comparison group, design, outcome measure, and population cannot be judged from the title and venue alone. Per abstract-stage rules, advance to full text for assessment of control group, design, and outcome data.

quote: The research employs a literature review approach by synthesizing findings from recent peer-reviewed international publications, conference proceedings, and authoritative educational reports
rationale: The abstract states the study is a literature review synthesizing prior publications, so it is not an empirical study with a control group and quantitative outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: The study combined questionnaires with semi-structured interviews involving nine students and three instructors.
rationale: Abstract describes a questionnaire and interview study of LLM use among computer science students. There is no control group and no experimental comparison, so the design is survey/qualitative, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. No quantitative learning outcome is reported; only usage and satisfaction. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code under the no-control-group criterion, with E5 and E6 also apparent from the abstract.

Community service program (pengabdian masyarakat) on ethical AI literacy for secondary students. The abstract reports only qualitative outcomes (students "mampu mengidentifikasi", "berkomitmen") with no quantitative learning measure, no control group, and no comparison design. It is not a controlled experiment. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), and E3 (no control group) would also apply; E5 is listed first in code order only if E3 is not earlier, so the first applicable code by protocol order is E3. Correcting: the first applicable code in order E1-E10 is E3 because no comparison group exists. Decision recorded as E3 below.

quote: Graduate students used AI in all domains, although use varied by domain.
rationale: The study is a survey of graduate students' use and perceptions of generative AI across domains. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only usage and perceptions. Exclusion E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also a survey, which fails the design criterion, and the STEM domain is not clearly established from the abstract.

quote: Five tutorials were delivered to fourth-year medical students (n = 38) during dermatology placements.
rationale: Exclude at E2 (content not STEM). The study is dermatology communication training for medical students, which is health professions education and not a STEM domain under the protocol. Also, the abstract reports only perceptions and usage with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5 would also apply), but E2 is the first applicable code in the order given. Rule 2 normally favors inclusion at abstract stage, but the abstract gives positive evidence the domain is health professions communication, which the protocol excludes.

quote: This OER book is the second volume of the YSK: Second Level series developed by the WashU Korean Program.
rationale: The record is an OER Korean language textbook with AI chatbots and study sets. Korean language learning is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also not an empirical study with a control group, but E2 is the first applicable code in order from E1 that is clearly positive. Note that E1 was not clearly failed at abstract stage (chatbots are mentioned), so E2 is the first clear failure.

quote: "The course design includes both formative and summative assessments created for and in response to generative artificial intelligence tools."
rationale: The record is a course syllabus for a rhetoric/writing course, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also not STEM content (rhetoric and civic writing). E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply, but the protocol asks for the first code in order, and E1 is not clearly established from the abstract. Under the order given, E1 is unclear, E2 is the first clear failure. Note: applying the strict order, E2 (content not STEM) comes before E6, so the code should be E2 on reflection. The decision to exclude stands.

quote: This study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental design in the form of a nonequivalent control group design.
rationale: The study teaches argumentative text writing, a language/writing topic, not STEM content. This is positive evidence the domain criterion fails, so E2 applies. Other criteria appear largely met (ChatGPT feedback vs peer reflection, quasi-experimental control group, junior high students, writing test score outcome), but the domain failure is decisive. Exclusion is at abstract stage based on positive evidence.

The record describes a course design paper (teaching description) rather than an empirical study. The abstract reports no comparison group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Some other criteria also appear unmet, but E6 is the first applicable code in the given order that is supported by the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; the exclusion is based on positive evidence that the paper is a course description without an empirical design.

quote: This study uses a systematic literature review approach to 18 relevant scientific articles from 2016 to 2026

The review does not report its own comparison or outcome data, so these are not evaluated further. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a review design.

quote: Through a systematic literature review, this study examines the positive impacts and challenges of integrating ChatGPT in university settings
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group. It therefore fails the design requirement and the empirical-study requirement (E6). Its focus is also EFL writing, which is non-STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly applies from the abstract.

rationale: The record describes a community service (pengabdian masyarakat) program with counseling and a system blueprint design at a junior high school. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order, as the record is a service/program report rather than an empirical study. Note that E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed as positively failed from the abstract alone for intervention and domain, so E6 is assigned on the basis of the non-empirical service design.

quote: This paper proposes the idea of Affective Generative AI in eLearning, combining large language models (LLMs), prompt engineering, and emotion aware computing
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual proposal ("We argue", "Our conceptual framework") with no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Although E1 ordering might be considered first, the abstract does not clearly establish intervention details, and the first applicable code in order would be E1 only if the tool were clearly not learner-facing generative AI; since the paper is not empirical, E6 is the applicable reason. Domain is not STEM-specified in the abstract.

quote: This paper presents the challenges and opportunities of using this technology in the educational sector and analyses how AI is revolutionizing education, research, and academic management
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion paper with a dichotomous synthesis of arguments for and against AI in education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion under E6 applies at abstract stage because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: Using  the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach which refers to the PRISMA guidelines, as many as 19 scientific articles from the Science Direct database  were analyzed qualitatively.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study. It analyzes 19 articles qualitatively, so it has no primary control-group design or SMD data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type also appears to be a review, which would fall under E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order listed by the protocol, and the abstract's design description best matches "not an empirical study."

The record has only a title and year (2023), with no abstract and no venue. The title suggests introductory physics (STEM) and a ChatGPT-related intervention, which is consistent with eligibility. However, the design, comparison group, learning outcome, and publication type cannot be determined from the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is retained as unsure for full-text review.

quote: We develop a coordination-based evolutionary game-theoretic framework that captures learning value, effort, perceived fairness, and transparency
rationale: The paper is a theoretical mathematical modelling study (analytical results and simulations of an evolutionary game). It reports no empirical learners interacting with a generative AI tool and no control group or learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in order that is positively evidenced by the abstract.

quote: A review is conducted on the state-of-the-art methods using the preferred reporting items for reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no experimental control group or quantitative learning outcome. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, but the review design alone is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: The research employs a standardized description of a software system with microservice architecture and unified textual prompts to ensure the correctness and comparability of results obtained from different models.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparison of several LLMs on test case generation, with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. Comparing only generative AI variants meets the E3 exclusion. Evaluation is by quality criteria rather than a clear learning outcome from learners, and the design is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison with a non-AI group. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; the comparison is between LLMs only.

quote: The utilities of these programs as educational tools were evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS) and 30 emergency medical personnel majoring in paramedicine.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT 3.5 vs 4.0 for pre-hospital history-taking training, with no non-generative-AI control group. Domain is paramedicine/medical history-taking, which falls under health professions education and is not STEM. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of failure on outcome (usability only), exclude. Primary code per order: E2 (content not STEM) would apply first in the protocol's order, so the first applicable code should be considered. Strictly, E2 is checked before E3 and E5 in the order, and the content is health professions education, so the first applicable code is E2.

quote: We, the Editor-in-Chief and Publisher of Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology, have retracted the following articles
rationale: The record is a retraction notice for a special issue, listing the retracted articles, including "Hierarchical attention mechanism in deep learning improving music therapy rehabilitation through context aware emotion mapping" (Liu, Z., 2025). It describes no empirical study design, intervention, population, or outcome, so there is no positive evidence of eligibility. The retracted article itself is not an empirical study eligible for inclusion; the record reports only a retraction and cannot support any study-level criterion. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study. Note: the abstract is a retraction notice rather than the study abstract, so this exclusion rests on the record's content alone.

quote: Students in the GAIIM group demonstrated significantly higher posttest performance in algebraic problem-solving, error detection, and error resolution after controlling for pretest scores.
rationale: Abstract reports a randomized pretest-posttest control group design with 86 undergraduate mathematics education students, an AI-supported verification intervention where learners compare and check AI-generated algebra solutions, and quantitative posttest outcomes (algebraic problem-solving, error detection). Year 2026 meets the date rule. Effect size statistics cannot be verified from the abstract, and the journal article status is taken from the venue name; these are left for full-text checking. No positive evidence of a failed criterion at abstract stage, so include.

quote: Foundation models can serve as clinical agents through tool-use harnesses.
rationale: The record is a machine-learning paper on clinical AI agents evaluated on UK Biobank patient MRI and clinical questions. Learners are not students; there is no learner population in K-12 or higher education. The domain is medical reasoning/health, which falls under the health professions exclusion rather than STEM education. Exclusion code E4 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion in order (E1 intervention is arguably a model-evaluation setup rather than learner-facing, but population failure is clearest). No comparison with a learner control group or learning outcome is described in the abstract. Not a STEM learning study.

quote: This workshop aims to guide participants in the process of 1) gaining awareness of the potential, limitations and pitfalls of AI tools
rationale: The record describes a workshop with no empirical design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Its publication type also appears to be a workshop description, not a journal article, but the abstract alone does not settle that.

quote: This study adopts a systematic literature review (SLR) guided by Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses 2020 standards
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 50 studies, not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome data. Under the protocol, reviews are ineligible publication types and also fail the empirical-study requirement, so it is excluded with E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order. The E6 code is used because the review is not an empirical study; E10 would also be plausible since reviews are listed as ineligible publication types, but E6 is the primary reason for exclusion.

quote: Employing a qualitative phenomenological approach, the study utilized a purposive sampling technique
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological design using ten semi-structured interviews and a focus group. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study that can meet the protocol's design or outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E6 (not an empirical study in the sense required), though the study is empirical qualitative work; E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply. Given the protocol order, E3 is the earliest clear failure among the design-related codes, but the abstract clearly shows qualitative perceptions only, so E5 would be the most direct. Final code selected: E6 as the study does not meet the design requirement of a comparison/experimental study.
decision_note: Exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence of qualitative design.

quote: This study addresses this gap through a comparative analysis of GenAI-related policy documents from 14 universities in Switzerland and Spain.
rationale: The study is a qualitative document analysis of university GenAI policies, not an empirical intervention with learners. There is no learner-facing GenAI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 applies as the first failing code in order: E1 would also apply, but the study is not an empirical study of learners at all, so E6 is the most accurate single code. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by clear positive evidence of a non-empirical, qualitative policy analysis.

quote: Here, we highlight some of the concerns and implications of generative Artificial Intelligence (generative AI) for social work education, research, practice, and scholarly publishing.
