rationale_detail: Systematic review, so not an empirical primary study.

rationale: Record has only a title and year (2023); no abstract, venue, or methods are available. The title indicates ChatGPT (a generative AI tool) in education in Ukraine, but nothing shows whether there is a control group, a quantitative learning outcome, a STEM domain, or an empirical design. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: International Convention on Information and Communication Technology, Electronics and Microelectronics
rationale: The venue is a conference (International Convention on ICT, Electronics and Microelectronics), so publication type is not an eligible journal article (E10). The abstract also describes conversations with ChatGPT to discuss myths rather than a controlled learning study with a comparison group and quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail design and outcome criteria as well. Per the protocol's code order, E10 is reported as the first applicable code; the venue is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: We will investigate how to accurately predict student outcomes early in the semester, analyze the dynamics of learning behaviors, and design an AI-assisted tool to recommend tailored learning materials and feedback.
rationale: The abstract describes predictive analytics of student outcomes from interaction logs and a planned AI tool recommending materials. It gives no positive evidence that learners interact with a generative AI tool in a learning activity; the focus is prediction and a design aim. Per the protocol, predictive analytics and non-generative adaptive systems are excluded (E1). No comparison group or quantitative outcome is described either, but E1 is the first applicable code.

The record has no abstract and only a title, venue, and year. The title indicates a large language model chatbot (retrieval augmented generation) for student support, which may meet the intervention criterion. Whether there is a control group, a STEM domain, a quantitative learning outcome, and an eligible design cannot be determined from the record. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text rather than excluded.

quote: The effectiveness of these methods is assessed through a case study involving a graduate student at the University of Pisa.
rationale: The abstract describes a method for building learner knowledge profiles from lesson records, evaluated by a single-student case study. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the study is not an eligible empirical comparison design. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study) as the primary, first-applicable-in-order code reflecting a method/case-study paper; the abstract gives positive evidence the design is a single case rather than a controlled experiment.

quote: In a controlled experiment, we involved 238 undergraduate students studying Software Engineering. We assigned participants the manual and LLM-assisted RE tasks
rationale: At abstract stage, the record describes a controlled experiment with manual (non-LLM) and LLM-assisted conditions among undergraduate software engineering students, with outcomes assessed by rubrics measuring artifact quality (a quantitative learning measure). Requirements engineering is within software engineering, which fits the STEM domain (computer science/software). Effect-size data sufficiency, publication type (FSE Companion may be a conference track), and full-text language cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so no exclusion is made; the record should be checked at full text for publication type (E10) and data sufficiency.

The record has only a title and venue; no abstract is available. The title indicates adult immigrant English language learners and English language learning, which is non-STEM content and adult learners outside the protocol's K-12/higher education population. Both domain and population appear to fail on the title alone, so the record is excluded. Primary code assigned is E2 is the first applicable in order? Note: codes are checked in order from E1, so E2 (non-STEM content) is the first that applies and is the correct code.

quote: This paper systematically reviews the application of prompt engineering in education, synthesizing theoretical foundations, developmental trajectories, models, frameworks, and application domains.
rationale: The record is a systematic review and conceptual synthesis, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Per protocol, reviews are excluded; the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study). Abstract gives positive evidence of review design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: this systematic review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of research on teachers’ use of GenAI in Pre-12 and K-12 education.
rationale: Record is a systematic review (publication type ineligible, and not an empirical study). It also concerns teachers' use of GenAI rather than learner-facing GenAI, so it fails the intervention and population criteria. Per the protocol, reviews are excluded; the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the primary reason is that it is a review, not an empirical study, so E6 is reported. Abstract gives clear positive evidence of a review.

quote: The preliminary findings suggest that GPT-3-enhanced gamification has great potential in scaffolding introductory programming learning
rationale: Programming domain and higher-education/international student population appear met, and the intervention appears to use GPT-3 in an LLM-powered tutor. However, the abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI, the study design is unclear (formative study, user study, simulation study with a study in progress), and it mentions quantitative data but does not clearly report a learning outcome (findings focus on belonging and anxiety, which are affective and not extracted). Ambiguity on comparison, design, and outcome means it should advance to full text.

quote: ChatGPT and medical education: a new frontier for emerging physicians
rationale: The record is a commentary-style piece on ChatGPT in medical education. It describes no experiment, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. The text is an introduction to LLMs, which suggests a non-empirical article (E6). Medical education also falls outside the STEM domain, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence that the record is not an empirical study.

quote: Data were collected through reflective journals, classroom observations and a post‐intervention survey.
rationale: Action research with 44 first-year students using Think Aloud with generative AI; no control group is described, data are qualitative journals, observations and a survey, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply. Domain (entrepreneurship) is not clearly STEM. Per the code ordering, E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: This exploratory study on 236 university educators based in India revealed mixed perceptions of using ChatGPT as a learning and teaching tool.
rationale: The study is a cross-national survey of university teachers' perceptions, not an empirical experiment with learners. It has no control group, no learner-facing intervention, no learning outcome, and participants are in-service educators rather than students. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense; survey perception design) is the most applicable first failing code. Note that E1 could also be argued since teachers, not learners, are the users; E6 is used here because the design is a perception survey. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclude.

quote: Following a single-group pretest-posttest design, data from this focus group were evaluated across four dimensions
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails and the record is excluded under E3. Intervention (generative AI in a learner activity), chemistry domain, junior high population, and quantitative outcomes appear met, but the missing control group is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: AI-assisted procedures enabled data processing in Python (Python Software Foundation, 2025) using the spaCy library
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT and Copilot to help researchers write code for corpus analysis. The AI is used by linguists and researchers, not by learners in a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). The learner corpora are analysed, not produced through a learning activity with AI. There is also no control group without generative AI, and the outcome is a linguistic analysis rather than a learning measure. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This poster presents an AI-powered intelligent tutoring system to enhance programming education
rationale: The record is a poster (and the venue is a research society), which is an ineligible publication type under the protocol (E10). The abstract also reports no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails on design and outcome as well, but the first applicable code in order is E10 for the publication type. Exclusion here is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the item is a poster.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E1 to E9 are checked first; E10 is reported here because no earlier code clearly applies from the abstract alone, and the poster status is explicit.

quote: We ask whether large language models can instead estimate pointwise mutual information zero-shot, using only prompts and elicited probabilities.
rationale: The study is a methods benchmark evaluating LLM prompting estimators of pointwise mutual information on human-annotated datasets. It has no learners interacting with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no learning outcome. The only education element is a case study scoring student knowledge summaries, which is not a learner-facing intervention with a learning outcome comparison. Excluded at the first applicable code; E1 could also be argued since no learner interacts with the tool, but the core failure is no quantitative learning outcome and no control group, so E5 is given as the reported code.

quote: This entry focuses on how students use generative AI while studying, preparing assignments, seeking explanations, revising work, programming, brainstorming, or responding to assessment tasks.
rationale: The record is an encyclopedia entry (conceptual overview, not an empirical study). It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it fails the protocol. Abstract-stage positive evidence of non-empirical type is sufficient for exclusion; the encyclopedia venue also suggests E10 could apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported by the abstract.
rationale_note: Publication type is an encyclopedia entry, which is not a journal article (E10 also plausible). Coded E6 as the primary code since the content is a conceptual, non-empirical entry.

quote: The participants comprised 121 undergraduates enrolled in the Introduction to Political Science course at the School of Political and Social Sciences, University of Phayao.
rationale: The course is Introduction to Political Science, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in code order. The abstract also reports a questionnaire-based analysis of hours and platform use with no evident randomized or comparison-group design, so the design criterion appears unmet as well. Under E2 the first applicable code is reported. Note that the title and abstract are in Thai/English; the English abstract is used for judgment.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: We report on deployment experiences across both settings and use the collected workloads to benchmark the effectiveness of various cost-optimization strategies, analyzing their trade-offs in cost, latency, and response quality.
rationale: This is a systems paper describing an LLM proxy deployed in a WhatsApp Q&A service and a university classroom. The abstract reports deployment experiences and benchmarks of cost-optimization strategies, not a controlled comparison with a separate control group lacking generative AI. No learning outcome (achievement or skill measure) is reported; outcomes are cost, latency, and response quality. Positive evidence that the comparison and outcome criteria fail supports exclusion under E3, the first applicable code in order is E3 for no control group without generative AI; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply. Coded E3 as the first applicable code given no comparison group is described.

quote: We applied the framework to 159 conversations from 78 higher education students interacting with a Socratic LLM-based chatbot deployed in a Thermodynamics course
rationale: The abstract describes only a single-condition analysis of learner-LLM dialogues with a Socratic chatbot; no control group without generative AI is mentioned, and the study appears to be a process/dialogue analysis rather than a comparative experiment. Positive evidence of a missing control group (E3) is present. Thermodynamics is arguably STEM, and the outcome is not a learning measure (dialogue coding, cluster profiles). Excluding under E3 as the first applicable code given the design described.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on E3 based on positive evidence of a single-condition dialogue analysis with no comparison group.

quote: we reflect on a pedagogical inflection point that has become unavoidable over the last year
rationale: This is an EduCHI provocation/reflection paper, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Its domain is HCI/qualitative methods, which is not clearly STEM either, but E6 applies first in the code order given the nature of the paper.

quote: This study investigates senior high school students’ perceptions of using ChatGPT as an AI-based learning tool in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning.
rationale: The content is English as a foreign language, which is non-STEM (E2). The study is also a descriptive survey of perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This scoping review addresses a critical gap in current literature by systematically examining the potential, limitations, and challenges of integrating AI agents in educational settings.
rationale: The record is a scoping review of the literature, not an empirical study with its own comparison group and outcome data, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Its own design is a review, so no primary experiment is reported. The abstract also gives no STEM-specific focus. Exclusion is based on the review design, which is positive evidence that the record is not an empirical study.

quote: By analyzing 28 studies, selected through the PRISMA protocol
rationale: This is a systematic literature review of 28 studies, which is a review publication rather than an empirical study. Under the protocol's publication-type and empirical-study rules, reviews are ineligible. The code E6 (not an empirical study) is used here because the protocol lists reviews under E6/E10; E6 is the closer match for a secondary review synthesis. No primary experimental design or control group is reported, so the record does not meet the design criterion.

quote: The study involved 60 undergraduate students who were divided into an experimental group receiving AI-assisted problem-based learning and a control group receiving conventional problem-based learning without direct generative AI assistance.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental design with a control group receiving conventional PBL without generative AI, 60 undergraduates, and a computational thinking test (quantitative outcome). Vocational higher education students and computational thinking suggest STEM-adjacent content. Intervention is described as AI-assisted PBL with generative AI tools, which appears to be learner-facing, but the abstract does not specify the tool type, so this is unresolved. The abstract reports "simulated empirical results," which raises a question about whether real data exist and whether SMD can be computed; this needs full-text checking. Publication year 2026 meets the date criterion. Venue is a journal article. Because no positive evidence of failure is shown, the record advances to full text.

quote: We propose an alternative that the educator controls directly: an input-side watermark in which an invisible instruction is embedded inside the visible assignment prompt itself.
rationale: The intervention is an invisible watermark embedded by the educator in assignment prompts to detect LLM copy-paste; it is not a learner-facing generative AI learning activity. No learning outcome or control group with learners is described. Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code. Abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI use.

quote: This paper explores the integration of AI tools, such as ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot, in the Software Architecture for Embedded Systems course.
rationale: Generative AI tools (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot) used by students in an embedded systems/software architecture course (STEM, higher education). The abstract does not describe a control group without generative AI, nor a design; it reports "enhanced problem-solving" and "faster development" without indicating a quantitative comparison. Comparison, design, and outcome are unclear from the abstract, so the record is advanced to full text rather than excluded.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 435 students from 37 degree programs and seven faculties at a public university.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey, which is a non-experimental design with no control group and no learning outcome measure. Its findings are prevalence and usage descriptions, and the abstract states they do not establish learning effects. It is not an empirical comparative study eligible under the protocol. E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; the design is a survey (not an experiment), so E3 (no control group) is also true, but the primary failure is the non-empirical-comparative nature. Given the code ordering, E1 is not clearly met since the AI use is by students, and E2 is not clearly failing (English learning is non-STEM, which would be E2 at the first code check). Note: English language learning is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the order before E3/E6. Final coding follows the order: E2.

quote: This poster introduces CourseAssist, a novel LLM-based tutoring system tailored for computer science education.
rationale: The record is a SIGCSE poster, which is an ineligible publication type (E10). Independently, the evaluation compares CourseAssist against GPT-4 (a generative AI variant, not a non-AI control) and reports user interviews and expert ratings rather than a quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also be likely. E10 is the first applicable code in the stated order for this abstract-stage decision.

quote: we evaluating six advanced AI Math LLM tools: Doubao-1.5-Thinking-Pro-Vision, GPT-5, DeepSeek-R1
rationale: The study benchmarks LLMs on math competition questions by scoring their answers; there is no learner interaction with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, and no control group of learners without generative AI. Under the stage-ordering rule, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first. Abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is model evaluation rather than learner-facing use.

quote: This article presents the 2022-2024 SLR study on digital learning with ChatGPT in elementary school mathematics learning.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review (PRISMA, 40 Scopus articles analyzed in ATLAS.ti), not an empirical study with a control group. It fails the design requirement and is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order (E1 to E5 cannot be positively confirmed or refuted from the abstract alone, and E6 is the decisive reason).
rationale_note: Abstract stage exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is a review.

rationale: Survey-based SEM-ANN study of learning intention. Positive evidence of a non-experimental, survey design with no control group, and the outcome is self-reported intention/perception rather than a quantitative learning measure. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order only if E1–E4 do not apply, and the intervention and domain are not clearly failing at abstract stage).

quote: Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline.
rationale: This is an LLM self-correction method in which the model's own reasoning is redirected by a learned intervention point and injected instructions; no learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. Evaluated on math benchmarks with model accuracy as outcome, not students. The intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. No human participants or learning outcomes are described.

quote: The results highlighted the TAM's robustness and identified minor refinements needed for the LSS/LLMs-6
rationale: Abstract describes a redesigned course with a post-course questionnaire on attitudes and learning strategies (TAM, LSS) and a content validity panel. It reports no quantitative learning outcome, no control group, and explicitly states the absence of empirical data. Positive evidence fails E5 (and the design lacks a comparison group, E3-like), but the first applicable code in order is E5 since it is a questionnaire-only perception study. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Participants completed three introductory C programming tasks with access to ChatGPT-4.5 or conventional web search without generative AI.
rationale: Abstract describes a between-subjects experiment with 59 undergraduate CS students, ChatGPT (generative) versus web search control, in programming, with quantitative outcomes (coding scores, cued recall). Year 2026 meets date rule. Venue and publication type are not given, and the abstract does not report SMD-sufficient statistics; these are checked at full text. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so include.

quote: The method employed is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR), with a comprehensive literature search conducted in the Scopus database.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Reviews are also not eligible publication types under the protocol (E10 could apply), but the protocol's review exclusion is best captured by E6 as the study design is not empirical. No primary comparison group or learning outcome data are reported in the abstract.

quote: Title: Literacy as a Technology: a Conversation with Kyle Jensen about AI, Writing and More
rationale: The title describes a conversation/interview with an author about AI and writing. It is not an empirical study, has no control group, no learning outcome, and writing/literacy is not STEM. The abstract is absent, but the title alone is positive evidence that the record is a non-empirical interview piece, so it is excluded under E6 (first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is learner-facing; the record gives no evidence of that, so E6 is the best-supported code).
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on title evidence.

rationale: This is a CHI Extended Abstracts doctoral consortium-style dissertation summary, not a journal article. Publication type is ineligible under the protocol (conference proceedings and dissertations excluded). It also describes no specific comparison, design, or quantitative outcome in the abstract. Excluded under E10 on publication type, which is the first applicable code in the protocol's order given the record's venue and format; the other criteria cannot be verified from this abstract.

quote: The results showed that students tended to favor personalized responses that were generated using their knowledge level as part of the user profile
rationale: The study is a user study in which students evaluated and chose preferred LLM responses under four personalization conditions. The outcome is preference/perceived quality, not a quantitative learning measure (achievement, knowledge, problem solving, or skill performance). No control group without generative AI is described, and the comparisons are among personalization variants of the same LLM. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perceived quality only. Exclusion codes are applied in order and E5 is the first that applies.

quote: RAGMan was deployed as an optional resource in an introductory programming course with an enrollment of 455 students.
rationale: LLM-powered tutor (generative AI) used by students in an introductory programming course (STEM, higher education). The abstract mentions a "comparative grade analysis" but does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI, the design, or the statistics needed for an SMD. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is unsure and should be resolved at full text (check for a non-AI comparison group and quantitative grade data). Also a SIGCSE Virtual venue, so publication type (journal article vs conference paper) needs checking at full text; this is a likely E10 risk.

quote: A review is conducted on the state-of-the-art methods using the preferred reporting items for reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study. It has no primary comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a review, which would be E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: We conducted a crosssectional survey, involving 251 undergraduate dental hygiene students.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with no intervention or control group, so it lacks a comparison group without generative AI. Outcomes are perceptions and attitudes (trust, risk, plagiarism perception), not quantitative learning measures. Dental hygiene is also a health professions field, which falls outside the STEM domain. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention failed; here the learner use is survey-based ChatGPT experience, so E3 is the first clearly positive failure that is evident at abstract stage.

quote: we conducted semi-structured interviews with six CS students both during and immediately after their internships
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of six students (inductive coding), not an empirical controlled experiment. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no SMD-computable data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense; qualitative designs are excluded under Design). Internships are not generative AI learning interventions either, so the first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) since the internship is not a generative AI tool; but the study's primary failure is design/outcome, and the record clearly fails E1 as well. Applying codes in order, E1 is the first that applies: the intervention (summer internship) is not a generative AI tool.

Doctoral project description (likely a doctoral symposium/proposal paper) in programming education with an LLM-based tutor. The abstract describes a proposed approach and investigation, with no reported control group, comparison, learning outcome, or effect data. Nothing in the abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion, so the record is held for full-text review. Publication type (possible doctoral consortium paper, which would be E10 or E6) and whether a controlled study exists cannot be determined from the abstract.

criteria.outcome_note: exam results mentioned; quantitative statistics not clear

quote: The students were divided into two groups, one led by a teacher, and the other tutored by ChatGPT.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT tutor vs teacher-led group in competitive programming (STEM), with learners as participants and a final exam outcome, so intervention, domain, and population appear met. However, it is described as a case study with N=11 and mixed methods, and it is unclear whether the design is a true comparison with quantitative learning data sufficient for SMD. Publication venue is a conference-style volume ("Education and New Developments 2024"), so publication type is also uncertain. Not excluded at abstract stage; needs full text review of design, outcome statistics, and publication type.

quote: Results indicated that students using the AIGC-VR platform demonstrated statistically significant improvements in designing experiments and analyzing data compared to a control group using traditional methods.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study describes a generative AI (AIGC) VR platform with an AI mentor used by secondary students, a control group using traditional methods, pre/post quantitative tests on conceptual understanding and inquiry skills, and a STEM domain. Design (randomization or quasi-experimental comparison) and effect-size data sufficiency cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so no positive evidence of failure is present; advance to full text.

quote: Qualitative findings show that TutorBotz increased teachers' confidence in using social robots, was easy to use, and fit diverse curricula.
rationale: Exploratory study with qualitative findings only; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported in the abstract. Teachers use GenAI to program robots, which is teacher-facing rather than learner-facing. Positive evidence of no comparison group and qualitative-only design supports exclusion. Code E3 applied as the first failing criterion in the order given by the protocol's wording on comparison; E1 could also arguably apply because the GenAI tool is used by teachers, not learners.
exclusion_code_note: E1 applies first by the codebook order

criteria.criteria_note: Exploratory study of perceptions and critical thinking; no control group described

quote: we conducted an exploratory study with 84 German secondary school students aged 16–19 attending software development workshops
rationale: Abstract describes an exploratory study of 84 secondary students' critical thinking, ethics perceptions, and gender differences in AI-assisted programming. No comparison group without generative AI is mentioned, and the outcomes appear to be perceptions rather than quantitative learning measures. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (no control group) is present, so exclude under E3. Note the abstract stage rule would normally favor advancing; however, the abstract explicitly describes a single exploratory study with no control arm, and the outcomes are perception-based.
decision_note: Could arguably be E5 (perceptions only) rather than E3; E3 chosen because the design is described as exploratory with no comparison.

quote: A cross-sectional study was carried out between August to October 2025 involving 328 undergraduate medical students
rationale: The design is a single cross-sectional survey of perceptions, attitudes, and practices with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is not an experiment and the outcomes are self-reported perception scores, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Health professions/medical education is also a domain concern. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not the best fit for an empirical survey, but the first applicable code in order given the record is that the study is not an eligible empirical design; E3 would be the first code in order that applies (no control group without generative AI). Following the protocol's order, E3 is the first applicable code, so the code is corrected below.

quote: The review draws on a dataset of 60 empirical studies published between 2022 and 2025 and retrieved from major academic databases.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group. Under the protocol's publication type and design rules it is not an eligible primary study. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study). The review's synthesized studies are not evaluated individually here, and the record itself is a review, so no primary comparison or outcome data are reported.

quote: We included 8 empirical studies and policy/guidance documents.
rationale: This is a systematic review using narrative synthesis, not an empirical study with its own comparison group. It is therefore not an empirical primary study (E6). It also reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome, and it covers general GenAI awareness and acceptance rather than STEM-specific learning. Exclusion under E6 is the first applicable code in order, since E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone and E6 is positive evidence of a review design.

quote: We investigate an LLM-as-reviewer integrated directly into GitHub pull requests (human-in-the-loop) across two cohorts (>100 students, 2023–2024).
rationale: The abstract describes a two-cohort repeated cross-sectional comparison with no control group lacking generative AI; both cohorts used the LLM reviewer (adoption differed, not a control condition). Outcomes are engagement/responsiveness behaviours and self-reports, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion E3 is the first applicable code in order (E1 and E2 do not apply: the tool is an LLM reviewer, and the domain is software engineering/code review). Positive evidence of no non-generative-AI comparison group is present, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

quote: We then used these impasses to simulate three tutoring conditions to study variation in AI tutor guidance through impasses: baseline, no-direct-answer, and guided tutor.
rationale: The abstract describes simulated tutoring conditions generated from existing authentic impasses, not a learner-facing controlled comparison with a non-generative-AI control group. Observational trajectory analysis of authentic sessions is also described. No positive evidence of a control group without generative AI appears in the abstract, so E3 is the best-supported exclusion, though the design is not fully clear at this stage. Note that the abstract also reports no learning outcome (only next-turn recovery), which may be E5 at full text. Exclusion is based on the absence of a non-generative-AI comparison group in the simulated and observational design.

quote: A total of 41 empirical studies met the eligibility requirements and were subjected to thematic synthesis.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review synthesizing studies through thematic synthesis, not an empirical study with its own control group. It is not an eligible primary study design, so E6 applies. It also focuses on teacher roles rather than learner-facing generative AI with a comparison group and learning outcomes.

quote: Journal of Education and Training Studies (JETS) would like to acknowledge the following reviewers for their assistance with peer review of manuscripts for this issue.
rationale: The record is a reviewer acknowledgements page, not a research article. It describes no intervention, comparison group, or outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). It also does not involve generative AI or STEM learning. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 would apply first if judged strictly on intervention, but the record is clearly not an empirical study, so E6 is the most accurate code. Publication type is also not a research article, which would be E10; E6 is chosen as the best fit for a non-empirical editorial item.

quote: This research paper provides a detailed secondary-data analysis of the historical evolution, statistical expansion, public perception, policy interventions, private-sector role, structural deficiencies, and pathways for transformation.
rationale: The record is a secondary-data review of the history and policy of India's Industrial Training Institutes. It is not an empirical study of learners using generative AI, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first applicable code, but the paper's core nature is a non-empirical review, so E6 is the most accurate single code. The abstract's mention of generative AI concerns the labor market, not a learner-facing intervention. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the abstract.
rationale_note: Code choice: rule 4 requires exactly one code. The protocol says report the first that applies in order; E1 technically could apply first since no learner-facing generative AI intervention is described. Reviewer may prefer E1 if strict ordering is applied.

quote: Each model was prompted to generate 200 Java and 200 Python quiz questions, totaling 1600 unique questions.
rationale: The record is a SIGCSE Virtual paper, a conference venue, so it is not a journal article and fails the publication-type criterion (E10). Also, the study compares LLMs generating quiz questions with no learner-facing intervention or control group, and it reports no learning outcome; these would be additional failures. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing: AI generates content for educators), but the protocol asks for the first code that applies in order, and E1 would be the first applicable one under strict ordering. Note: under strict ordering E1 applies before E10, so the code should arguably be E1. Based on the abstract, the models generate questions and no learners interact with them, so E1 is the first code that applies.

quote: Exploring ChatGPT’s role in reducing EFL students’ speaking anxiety across varying anxiety levels
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language speaking practice, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so E2 applies first in the ordered check. It is also a descriptive mixed-methods study with no control group and no learning outcome measure (questionnaire on anxiety and perceptions), so E3, E5 and design criteria would also fail, but E2 is the first applicable code.

The abstract describes a framework evaluated via a systematic review and "empirical analysis of educational performance indicators", with pre/post-style engagement change (68.7% to 89.8%) and no described control group. No separate comparison group without generative AI is indicated, so the comparison criterion appears unmet. The venue (International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology) is also unusual for this topic, but I rely only on the record. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no control group, consistent with a single-group design.

The record has only a title ("Model student"), a venue (Nature Physics), and a year (2023), with no abstract. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence that any criterion fails, so under the abstract-stage rule it cannot be excluded. The title does not indicate whether a generative AI tool is involved, whether there is a control group, or what the outcome is. It should advance to full-text screening for a check of the methods.

quote: A total of 50 references were analyzed thematically to identify article characteristics, thematic categories, main findings, and their implications for mathematics learning.
rationale: This is a systematic literature review analyzing 50 references thematically, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Reviews are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but the first applicable code in order is E6 given the study is a review rather than an empirical report.

quote: we propose the first benchmark dataset for evaluating LLMs on simulating personas with reversed performance
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs simulating student personas, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. The work is a benchmark of LLM instruction following, with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measured in students. E1 applies as the first failing criterion.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on clear positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: Using a quantitative quasi-experimental design, the study involved 70 sixth-semester students enrolled in a Business Letter course
rationale: Content is business email writing for EFL learners (language/business communication), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. Other criteria appear plausibly met at abstract stage (ChatGPT-assisted instruction, control group receiving conventional instruction, quasi-experimental, higher education), but the domain failure is decisive. Outcome is self-efficacy questionnaire, which is affective and would likely also fail, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: This systematic literature review synthesizes 61 empirical studies published by September 2024
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 61 studies, not a primary empirical study with its own comparison group. Under the protocol's publication-type and design rules, reviews are ineligible. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order given; E10 (publication type) is arguably also relevant, but the review is a secondary synthesis, so E6 is used. The quote is from the abstract and describes the review's synthesis of prior studies.

quote: In this poster, we explore how LLM-based code generation tools can be redesigned as learning artifacts and propose a pedagogical redesign
rationale: The record is a CHI Extended Abstracts poster proposing a redesign, with no empirical study or comparison group described. It is a poster/work-in-progress type, which is not an eligible publication type (E10). Protocol says the first applicable code in order should be reported; E1 does not apply since the tool is an LLM-based coding assistant learners would interact with, and E3/E5/E6 are also plausible, but the publication type is the clearest positive evidence at abstract stage.
exclusion_code_note: E10 chosen; protocol order would put E6 (not an empirical study) possibly earlier, but E10 is explicit from the venue/format.

quote: This research aimed to describe students’ perceptions of using AI-generated translators based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework
rationale: The study is a descriptive quantitative survey of perceptions using UTAUT constructs, with no control group, no learning outcome measure, and the content is EFL translation (language learning, non-STEM). Exclusion uses the first applicable code in order; E2 (non-STEM content) is the first code that clearly applies, as the domain is English language learning. Design and outcome failures would also apply, but E2 is listed first in the order of checking from E1 only if E1 does not apply; E1 is not clearly met because the tools are learner-used generative translators, so E2 is the earliest clear failure.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of non-STEM content and perception-only survey design.

rationale: Abstract stage. The record has no abstract, only a title pointing to a knowledge, attitude and practice measurement study of university students on AI-giarism. The title suggests a survey-type design and an academic integrity topic rather than STEM learning, with no evidence of a generative AI learning intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome. However, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept as unsure for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: We present Argus, an automated detection system for LLM-assisted student work in undergraduate C programming assignments.
rationale: Argus is a detection system for academic integrity; students do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. It is a monitoring/detection tool, not a learner-facing generative AI intervention (E1). The study also reports correlational analysis of flagged LLM use versus exam performance, with no control group without generative AI (E3 would also apply, but E1 is the first applicable code). Domain (C programming) and population (undergraduates) appear met.

quote: A survey of 120 first- to third-year students (12-item questionnaire) was conducted
rationale: Abstract describes a survey and a correlational analysis between LLM usage frequency and performance, with no randomized or quasi-experimental control group that lacks generative AI. The comparison groups (LLM restricted to instructor consultations) are not clearly non-generative-AI controls, and the pilot compares before and after within one group. Positive evidence of a failed criterion is the correlational/survey design without a control group, which corresponds to E3 (no control group without generative AI). Published 2026, so date is met; the venue is a conference proceeding, which would also be E10, but the protocol's first-applicable code order places E3 before E10 is not the first applicable code here... the code order is E1 through E10, and E3 precedes E10, so E3 is reported.

quote: We introduce a specialized dataset designed to support the creation of domain-specific detection tools to fill this gap.
rationale: The record describes a dataset paper of human-written and ChatGPT-generated code samples for source classification. It is not an empirical study of learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity, and it has no control group or learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Quote is from the abstract.

quote: The sample consisted of 700 satisfaction survey responses collected during the fiscal years 2023–2025, with a response rate of 24.60%.
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods satisfaction survey with perceived pre/post knowledge ratings from a single training group. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Outcomes are self-perceived learning rather than a quantitative learning measure, which would also fail E5, but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Although the abstract is in English, the title is in Thai; the record is a satisfaction-based survey and not a controlled comparison.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence: single-group perceived pre-post design with survey data.

quote: Adopting a conceptual and practice-oriented approach, it proposes a privacy-aware decision framework for GenAI use
rationale: The article is a conceptual and practice-oriented paper proposing a decision framework; it reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). The domain is language education, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), but E6 is the first applicable code in the order that reflects the core design issue; the criteria for comparison, design, outcome and population are all not met on the abstract's evidence.
exclusion_code_note: Codes are applied in order E1 to E10. Strictly, E2 (non-STEM, language education) precedes E6 in the protocol order. Reconsider if audit requires strict ordering.

quote: This study systematically examines Turkish peer-reviewed articles published between 2022 and 2025 on AI in the field of science education
rationale: The record is a systematic review of Turkish literature, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. Reviews are not empirical studies, so E6 applies. The abstract states qualitative methods predominated and the review itself is not an experiment. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's description of the study as a systematic review.

Undergraduate students solving programming problems with an AI assistant (domain and population appear met). The abstract does not state whether the AI is generative (intervention unclear). It describes a controlled task with accurate and deliberately incorrect suggestions, but does not mention a control group without AI, so comparison is unclear. Outcomes are mainly reliance patterns plus correlations with self-efficacy, trust and satisfaction; it is unclear whether a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement was measured. The study is a correlational-style survey plus task, so design is unclear. No positive evidence of a failed criterion appears in the abstract, so it advances to full text.

Abstract stage: the index has no abstract, only a title and venue (AERA 2026 conference). The title ("Unpacking Engineering Students' Perceptions Toward Generative AI in Learning") suggests a perceptions/intention focus, which would fail the outcome criterion, and the venue suggests a conference paper (E10), but neither is confirmed from the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: This panel aims to bring computing education researchers together to discuss the main challenges around teaching decomposition and planning using common patterns
rationale: The record is a SIGCSE Virtual panel description, not a journal article, so it fails publication type (E10). It also reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data; these are additional failures but E10 is the first applicable code in the stated order when checked as publication type. Abstract stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of a panel format rather than an empirical study.

quote: Fifteen international students participated in Korean typing activities using Hancom Typing Practice and completed an online survey.
rationale: The study reports perceptions via survey from 15 international students, with no control group or comparison condition described; the prototype was evaluated by three experts. There is no quantitative learning outcome comparing groups, so the design fails the comparison requirement. Korean typing is also arguably non-STEM language content. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order here (no control group without generative AI). Note the record would also plausibly fail E2 (Korean language content, not STEM) and E5 (perceptions only); the code ordering in the protocol places E2 and E5 before E3 only if they apply on the text, so this is a judgment call the auditor should check.

quote: Participants were asked to solve the "8 Queens" problem in two 30-minute phases: first independently, and then with assistance from the ChatGPT-4 model
rationale: Abstract describes learners (students from informatics and engineering faculties) using ChatGPT-4 on a programming task, with a quantitative accuracy outcome. The within-subject design (first independently, then with LLM) suggests a single-group pre-post structure, which would be E3, but the abstract does not clearly state whether a separate control group exists, so the comparison and design criteria remain unclear. Venue is AHFE International (likely conference proceedings, possibly E10), which cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Not excluded at abstract stage per rule 2; full text needed to check design and publication type.

quote: The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by adopting the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) protocol.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study. It synthesizes published literature rather than reporting its own experiment with a control group and quantitative outcome, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6) and the review publication-type exclusion does not apply as a journal article. The review is a secondary synthesis, so the study design cannot meet the randomized or quasi-experimental design criterion.

quote: Synthetic data is increasingly used to train large language models (LLMs), yet its security implications remain poorly understood.
rationale: The study concerns covert bias injection into LLMs via synthetic fine-tuning data, not learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. Content is not STEM (security/bias in model training; creative writing and code generation are used only as data-generation domains). No learner population or learning outcome is described. Under the code order, E1 would be the first applicable code, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. However, the abstract gives no evidence of learners at all, so E1 is the most defensible primary code: the record is a model-training security study. Coding E2 is inconsistent with that reasoning, so the decision should be reviewed; E1 is the correct first-applicable code.

quote: Data came from a cross-sectional survey of around 250 university students from Punjab, Pakistan
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey examining digital inequality and generative AI access/use; no learner-facing generative AI intervention is administered and no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group is described. Exclusion E1 applies first (AI is not an intervention learners interact with as part of a learning activity; AI use is measured as a survey variable). Design also fails (survey, correlational), which is noted but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Session-based recommendation (SBR) predicts the next item based on anonymous sessions.
rationale: The record is about multimodal LLM-enhanced session-based recommendation for items, not STEM learning content. It is not an educational study in STEM domain, so E2 applies (first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is a recommender model rather than learner-facing generative AI in a learning activity, which is also arguably E1). Per the code order, E1 would come first; however the abstract gives no learner-facing learning activity, and the clearest failure is domain. Excluding on E2 as the STEM content fails on the abstract's positive evidence of a recommender-systems context.

quote: ChatGPT is emerging as a potentially powerful tool for enhancing learning in medical education despite all its flaws, and we encourage further conversation
rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece on ChatGPT in medical education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Health professions education is also outside the STEM domain under the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies in order, so it is used here; E2 (health professions content not STEM) could also be argued, but E6 comes first and is decisive.

quote: An experimental generation of WPD was conducted using the tools GigaChat, DeepSeek, and ChatGPT, along with an expert evaluation of the results.
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI used to generate course curriculum documents, with expert evaluation of outputs. No learner-level quantitative learning outcome or control group is reported; the outcome is expert rating of generated documents. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design does not appear to be a comparison of learners, so this is positive evidence against the outcome criterion.

quote: We evaluated student interactions with three different configurations of the GPT-3.5 back-end
rationale: The abstract describes a generative AI chatbot (GPT-3.5) for secondary physics with students, but the evaluation reports user experience ratings, perceptions, and intention to use, not a quantitative learning outcome. The comparison is among three GPT-3.5 configurations with no described non-AI control group, which would also fail the comparison criterion (E3). Per protocol order, E1 and E2 do not apply, and E3 is listed before E5; however, the abstract does not clearly show a missing control (it is ambiguous), so E5 is the clearest positive failure at abstract stage. Excluding on E5 because the abstract gives positive evidence that outcomes are perceptions/experience only.

quote: This systematic review synthesizes 64 empirical studies to examine how Generative AI (GenAI) shapes learning in Computer Science Education (CSE)
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 64 studies, not a primary empirical study with its own control group and effect size data. It fails the protocol's design requirement (randomized or quasi-experimental with comparison group) and is a review, which is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain is computer science (STEM), which is met. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code given the review nature; the abstract-stage rule permits exclusion on positive evidence, which the review type provides.

The record has only a title and venue (CSEDM@EDM, 2025); no abstract is available. The title suggests a retrieval-augmented generative AI assistant for competitive programming (STEM domain), but whether learners interact with it, whether a non-generative-AI control group exists, the design, and the outcome cannot be determined from the record. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held as unsure for fulltext review. The venue is a workshop-style track; publication type (journal article vs. workshop paper) should be checked at fulltext, since conference proceedings are ineligible (E10).

Abstract stage. The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. The title suggests a programming context (STEM) and an LLM intervention, but the comparison group, design, outcome, and publication type cannot be assessed from the record. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded. The venue (ECTEL) and year (2024) do not indicate an ineligible publication type or date, but the publication type should be verified at full text.

quote: This study systematically reviews 49 research papers published between 2020 and 2024, using the PRISMA framework and thematic analysis
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 49 papers with thematic analysis, not an empirical study with a control group. It fails the design/empirical requirement (E6). Information literacy education is also not clearly STEM. Because the review is not an empirical study, E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: Distilling the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) into smaller students is a central challenge for efficient deployment.
rationale: The study is a model-distillation method in which a smaller LLM student is trained by reinforcement learning against a teacher model's log-likelihood. No learner-facing generative AI intervention is described; the "students" are neural network models, not human learners. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). Abstract also reports no human comparison group or learning outcome, so the exclusion rests on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: This open access article serves as the introduction to a special issue of the journal on how ChatGPT is being used in mathematics education and presents the results of a scoping review.
rationale: The record is an editorial-style introduction to a special issue that presents a scoping review. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also questionable (editorial/review), but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated sequence for a review-type record. The abstract gives positive evidence of a review rather than an experiment.

quote: This final-year (Year 3) undergraduate textbook introduces students to the principles of genome-wide approaches used to study common polygenic traits.
rationale: The record is a university textbook, not an empirical study. It has no generative AI learner intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as context for prompts. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); publication type is also not a journal article, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: proposing an evaluation framework for intelligent educational literacy for pre-service teachers. Then a LSTM-based evaluation model using multimodal data mining and virtual simulation technologies is given to calculate pre-service teachers' intelligent educational literacy.
rationale: The abstract describes a framework and an LSTM-based evaluation model for computing pre-service teachers' literacy. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome measured after an intervention. It appears to be a system/model proposal rather than an empirical controlled study. Exclusion is on positive evidence that the design is not an experiment with a control group (E6, not an empirical study). Note that E3 could also apply, but the abstract does not give positive evidence of a control group absent, so E6 is the best-supported code.

The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. The title suggests a paper on educator competencies and case-based innovation for GenAI in higher education, which does not clearly indicate a controlled learner-facing study. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for fulltext review rather than excluded. The "quarantine" key in criteria is not part of the schema and was included in error; the other criteria are all unclear. No quote is available.

quote: The document outlines a comprehensive strategy for integrating AI into higher education, emphasizing the need for curriculum restructuring, pedagogical transformation, and strategic implementation
rationale: The record is a strategy/position document (a "blueprint") rather than an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in code order. No STEM content is specified either, but E6 is reported first per the ordering rule.

quote: The integration of Generative AI effectively reduced analysis time and enhanced precision in natural language processing
rationale: Generative AI was used by researchers for systematic data coding and synthesis (thematic analysis), not as a learner-facing tool in the Cell Pizza activity. Exclusion code E1 applies as the first failing criterion.

rationale: The abstract describes a web-based platform for recording and analysing student-AI conversations, with "initial experiences" reported. The abstract also gives no evidence of a control group, but E5 is the first code that applies in order of the scheme, so it is reported as the single code.
rationale_note: Code order: E1 no (generative AI learner-facing), E2 no (electronic engineering, STEM), E3 unclear from abstract, E4 no, E5 yes.

quote: A role-free student generates a trajectory, and a frozen instance of the same base model supplies role-conditioned distributions on its exact prefixes
rationale: The paper is a machine-learning method for distilling LLMs (Qwen3 models) on competition-math benchmarks. quote: Through experiments on a real-world programming education dataset, we show that InfoOIRT can both accurately generate student code and lead to interpretable student knowledge representations.
rationale: The paper is a computational model (IRT-based generative model) evaluated on an existing programming dataset. It does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool in a learning activity, and there is no control group or quantitative learning outcome from a learner intervention; the evaluation is code-generation accuracy and interpretability of latent representations. Excluded at abstract stage with E5 as the primary failing criterion (no quantitative learning outcome). Note the intervention/comparison criteria also appear not to be met, so E1 or E3 could be argued; E5 is applied as the most direct positive failure shown in the abstract.

quote: This paper articulates a standardized and practicable CPTC paradigm—Consensus, Platform, Training, and Case.

It is also medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion, but the protocol's domain exclusion is not the first applicable code in order here, and the abstract does not clearly establish a STEM domain either way. quote: The purpose of the article is to determine the features ofthe methodological model for developing the learning-strategic competence of pre-service English teachers based on artificial intelligence tools.
rationale: The study concerns English language teacher training (language learning, non-STEM content), so E2 applies. No embedded instructions were found in the record.

quote: We argue that the way RLHF changes the behavior of LLMs highlights how communicative interaction and socially informed feedback, in addition to input-driven statistical learning, can explain fundamental aspects of language learning.
rationale: The record is a theoretical/position article (argues a perspective; takes LLMs as models of idealized learners). It presents no empirical study with a control group or learning outcome data. It is also about human language learning (linguistics), not STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the stated order is E1 check: the intervention is not a learner-facing AI tool here, but E6 is the most direct applicable failure given the argumentative nature of the paper.
